_meta.purpose: Self-contained disease specs that DRIVE the emergence pipeline. Each disease lists its CAUSAL GENES (with role x mechanism), its CITED therapeutic axes (pathway A: switch levers), optional small-molecule candidates (pathway B: VP chemistry), and >=1 measurable falsifier. The pipeline pulls each gene's real DNA from NCBI, emerges the R19 switch, reads the disease as a perturbation, and assembles corrective directions. NOTHING here is a classifier label; every entry is an input to an emergence.
_meta.selection_rule: A disease is INCLUDED only if its cause is a promoter-switch-readable monogenic locus whose DNA NCBI resolves. If not (e.g. whole-chromosome dosage, structural/repeat loci with no clean promoter read), it is SUSPENDED with a stated reason -- the author's rule: no analyzable DNA -> hold.
_meta.grades: [V] reproducible read | [F] forced direction (cited biology) | [O] open magnitude (runtime/Layer-2) | [CAL] external measured input
_meta.firewall: gamma reads promoter switch-threshold STRUCTURE only; directions are forced+cited; magnitudes/affinities/doses/efficacy are [O], asserted nowhere; nothing here is a recommendation to treat any individual.

achondroplasia.summary: The commonest skeletal dysplasia: a recurrent FGFR3 gain-of-function (G380R) constitutively activates the growth-plate brake, so endochondral elongation is suppressed -> disproportionate short stature.

causal_genes.note: G380R transmembrane substitution -> ligand-independent constitutive kinase
causal_genes.src: Shiang 1994 Cell 78:335; Rousseau 1994 Nature 371:252

context_genes.note: CNP receptor; cGMP arm OPPOSES the FGFR3/MAPK brake
CNP ligand for NPR2
master chondrocyte TF
Indian hedgehog proliferation signal
PTHrP keeps chondrocytes proliferating

therapeutic_axes.push: boost CNP->NPR2->cGMP, which OPPOSES the over-active FGFR3/MAPK brake
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] the downstream brake-suppression magnitude is not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Savarirayan 2020 Lancet 396:684; vosoritide FDA/EMA 2021

therapeutic_axes.push: reduce FGFR3 tyrosine-kinase output directly
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: FGFR3-TKI / soluble FGFR3 decoy (infigratinib, recifercept; investigational)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] potency/selectivity/dose not asserted
therapeutic_axes.src: Legeai-Mallet lineage; infigratinib paediatric program

falsifiers.claim: FGFR3 GOF moves the growth-plate emergent axis DOWN (brake over-active)
falsifiers.falsifier: an FGFR3 GOF allele that INCREASES limb length, or a growth-plate in which constitutive FGFR3 signalling raises chondrocyte proliferation, refutes the brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation index in an Fgfr3-G380R model; limb-length cohort by genotype

falsifiers.claim: boosting NPR2/CNP (vosoritide axis) is the CORRECTIVE direction (opposes the brake)
falsifiers.falsifier: if CNP/NPR2 activation reduced rather than restored endochondral growth, the 'oppose the brake' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: endochondral growth response to a CNP analogue in an Fgfr3-GOF growth-plate

cystic_fibrosis.summary: CFTR loss-of-function (commonest allele F508del) leaves the epithelial chloride channel mis-folded/closed -> the gate is stuck in the OFF basin, drying secretions across lung, pancreas, gut.

causal_genes.note: F508del: folding/trafficking defect; gate fails to reach/hold the ON basin
causal_genes.src: Riordan 1989 Science 245:1066; Kerem 1989

context_genes.note: ENaC alpha; CFTR loss disinhibits Na+ absorption (drives the dehydration)

therapeutic_axes.push: increase open-probability of channels already at the membrane (open the gate)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] gating kinetics/dose not asserted
therapeutic_axes.src: Ramsey 2011 NEJM 365:1663 (ivacaftor, G551D)

therapeutic_axes.push: rescue folding/trafficking so F508del-CFTR reaches the membrane
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] rescue fraction/dose not asserted
therapeutic_axes.src: Middleton 2019 NEJM 381:1809 (triple combination, F508del)

falsifiers.claim: CFTR LOF moves the conductance axis DOWN (gate stuck OFF)
falsifiers.falsifier: a CFTR LOF allele that INCREASES chloride conductance refutes the OFF-basin direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: Ussing-chamber chloride current in CFTR-mutant epithelium

falsifiers.claim: potentiate/correct is the CORRECTIVE direction (restore conductance)
falsifiers.falsifier: if a potentiator/corrector reduced CFTR conductance, the lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: short-circuit current response to ivacaftor in gating-mutant epithelium

phenylketonuria.summary: PAH loss-of-function lowers phenylalanine-hydroxylase throughput -> phenylalanine accumulates and is neurotoxic. A subset of alleles keep residual enzyme that a BH4 cofactor can stabilise -> a SMALL-MOLECULE (pathway-B) correction.

causal_genes.note: many alleles; BH4-responsive subset retains residual activity
causal_genes.src: DiLella 1986; Blau 2010 Lancet 376:1417

context_genes.note: BH4 regeneration; defects mimic PKU via cofactor loss

therapeutic_axes.push: supply the enzyme activity another way (enzyme substitution)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] activity/dose not asserted
therapeutic_axes.src: Thomas 2018 (pegvaliase)

chem_candidates.name: sapropterin (BH4)
chem_candidates.modality: PAH cofactor rescue (supply the missing cofactor; stabilises residual PAH)
chem_candidates.rationale: BH4 binding stabilises the residual enzyme fold -> restores partial throughput; thermodynamic FEASIBILITY of the cofactor-stabilisation step (representative inputs)

chem_candidates.name: large-neutral-amino-acid mix
chem_candidates.modality: substrate competition at the blood-brain barrier
chem_candidates.rationale: competes phenylalanine transport into brain; thermodynamics not supplied -> feasibility [O]

falsifiers.claim: PAH LOF moves the metabolic-throughput axis DOWN (substrate accumulates)
falsifiers.falsifier: a PAH LOF allele that LOWERS blood phenylalanine refutes the throughput-down direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: plasma phenylalanine by PAH genotype / enzyme activity assay

falsifiers.claim: BH4 cofactor rescue is a thermodynamically feasible CORRECTIVE step in BH4-responsive alleles
falsifiers.falsifier: if the cofactor-stabilisation step were non-spontaneous at body T (dG>0) or BH4 failed to raise residual activity in responsive alleles, the feasibility read is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: PAH activity +- BH4 in responsive vs non-responsive alleles; ITC of BH4 binding

sickle_cell_disease.summary: A single recurrent HBB coding substitution (Glu6Val) makes adult haemoglobin polymerise when deoxygenated (HbS), so the supply of FUNCTIONAL non-sickling haemoglobin is effectively reduced. The lesion is qualitative (a coding missense, not a promoter change); the promoter switch-threshold read here is of the beta-globin LOCUS structure, and the disease direction (functional-Hb axis DOWN) is forced by the loss-of-FUNCTION biology of HbS.

causal_genes.note: beta-globin subunit of the haemoglobin tetramer; Glu6Val (HbS) is expressed at normal level but is dysfunctional (polymerises on deoxygenation) -> qualitative/FUNCTIONAL loss of normal adult haemoglobin. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does not encode the coding lesion (firewall).
causal_genes.src: Ingram 1957 Nature 180:326; Pauling 1949 Science 110:543

context_genes.note: erythroid repressor that switches haemoglobin from fetal (HBG) to adult (HBB) after birth; disrupting its erythroid enhancer de-represses HBG -> re-induces non-sickling fetal haemoglobin (HbF)
fetal (gamma) globin; HbF does not sickle and inhibits HbS polymerisation
context_genes.src: Platt 1994 NEJM 330:1639 (HbF inversely tracks crisis rate)

therapeutic_axes.push: disrupt the BCL11A erythroid enhancer -> de-repress HBG -> re-induce fetal haemoglobin (HbF), which OPPOSES HbS polymerisation and restores functional Hb
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] HbF induction magnitude / polymerisation suppression not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Frangoul 2021 NEJM 384:252; exa-cel (Casgevy) FDA/EMA 2023

therapeutic_axes.push: add a functional anti-sickling beta-globin gene -> supply non-sickling adult haemoglobin
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] transduced functional-Hb fraction not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Kanter 2022 NEJM 386:617; lovo-cel (Lyfgenia) FDA 2023

therapeutic_axes.push: pharmacologically raise fetal haemoglobin to oppose HbS polymerisation
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] hydroxyurea HbF-induction mechanism partly debated; magnitude not derived
therapeutic_axes.src: Charache 1995 NEJM 332:1317; hydroxyurea FDA 1998

falsifiers.claim: HBB Glu6Val (functional LOF) lowers the supply of functional non-sickling haemoglobin
falsifiers.falsifier: an HbS context in which polymerisation INCREASES functional oxygen-carrying capacity, or an HBB allele where HbS raises functional adult Hb, refutes the functional-loss direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: HbS polymerisation / functional haemoglobin fraction by genotype

falsifiers.claim: re-inducing fetal haemoglobin (oppose BCL11A) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if reducing BCL11A LOWERED fetal haemoglobin or WORSENED sickling, the 'oppose BCL11A' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: fetal-haemoglobin fraction and sickling response to BCL11A enhancer disruption in erythroid cells

familial_hypercholesterolaemia.summary: A monogenic defect in LDL-receptor-mediated clearance of plasma LDL. The commonest cause is LDLR loss-of-function (the receptor that internalises LDL); a gain-of-function in PCSK9 (which targets LDLR for degradation) is a second monogenic cause. Either way the LDL-clearance axis is driven DOWN, so plasma LDL accumulates.

causal_genes.note: the hepatic LDL-uptake receptor (the gate through which LDL particles are internalised); LOF leaves the uptake gate stuck OFF -> LDL clearance lost. Commonest cause of FH.
causal_genes.src: Brown & Goldstein 1986 Science 232:34 (Nobel); Goldstein & Brown 2009

causal_genes.note: PCSK9 binds LDLR and routes it for lysosomal degradation; a GOF allele over-brakes clearance by lowering LDLR density. Stiffest promoter switch of the pair -> primary.
causal_genes.src: Abifadel 2003 Nat Genet 34:154 (PCSK9 GOF -> FH)

context_genes.note: apolipoprotein B is the LDL ligand recognised by LDLR; ligand-defective APOB is a third (rarer) monogenic FH cause and a production-arm drug target (not scored on the clearance axis here)

therapeutic_axes.push: inhibit PCSK9 -> spare LDLR from degradation -> raise LDLR density -> restore LDL clearance (axis UP)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] LDL-lowering magnitude not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Sabatine 2017 NEJM 376:1713 (evolocumab); Ray 2020 NEJM 382:1507 (inclisiran)

therapeutic_axes.push: up-regulate LDLR transcription via SREBP-2 (intracellular sterol depletion) -> more receptor -> more LDL clearance (axis UP)
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor -> SREBP-2 -> LDLR up-regulation)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] receptor-up-regulation magnitude not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Endo 1976 (statin discovery); Brown & Goldstein 1997 (SREBP/LDLR)

falsifiers.claim: LDLR LOF lowers LDL-receptor-mediated clearance (plasma LDL rises)
falsifiers.falsifier: an LDLR LOF allele associated with LOWER plasma LDL, or hepatocytes in which LDLR loss INCREASES LDL uptake, refutes the clearance-down direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: LDL uptake assay in LDLR-null vs wild-type hepatocytes; plasma LDL by LDLR genotype

falsifiers.claim: opposing PCSK9 (sparing LDLR) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if PCSK9 inhibition LOWERED hepatic LDLR or RAISED plasma LDL, the 'oppose PCSK9' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: hepatic LDLR level and plasma LDL response to PCSK9 inhibition

gaucher_disease.summary: Loss-of-function of lysosomal acid beta-glucosidase (GBA1 / glucocerebrosidase) lowers the catabolism of glucosylceramide, so the substrate accumulates in macrophages. The throughput axis is driven DOWN; correction is to restore enzymatic throughput (replace the enzyme / stabilise residual enzyme) or to lower the substrate load upstream.

causal_genes.note: lysosomal acid beta-glucosidase (glucocerebrosidase); LOF lowers glucosylceramide catabolism -> substrate accumulates (Gaucher cells). NCBI official symbol GBA1 (formerly GBA).
causal_genes.src: Brady 1965 (enzyme defect); Beutler & Grabowski 2001 OMMBID

therapeutic_axes.push: supply recombinant acid beta-glucosidase -> restore catabolic throughput (axis UP)
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: enzyme replacement (imiglucerase, velaglucerase alfa, taliglucerase alfa)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] restored throughput / substrate-clearance magnitude not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Barton 1991 NEJM 324:1464; imiglucerase (Cerezyme) FDA 1994

therapeutic_axes.push: stabilise the residual mutant enzyme fold so more functional enzyme reaches the lysosome (chaperone-style rescue; allele-dependent)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] fold-stabilisation magnitude / allele responsiveness not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Maegawa 2009 JBC 284:23502; Narita 2016 (ambroxol)

chem_candidates.name: substrate-reduction (glucosylceramide-synthase inhibition)
chem_candidates.modality: lower glucosylceramide synthesis upstream -> less substrate for the deficient catabolic step
chem_candidates.rationale: reduces influx into the throttled catabolic step; pathway-B reports the equilibrium-feasibility DIRECTION only. Measured thermodynamics not supplied here -> [O] (no number -> hold it).

chem_candidates.name: pharmacological chaperone (ambroxol)
chem_candidates.modality: stabilise residual mutant GCase fold (cofactor/chaperone-style stabilisation)
chem_candidates.rationale: a stabilising binder would restore partial fold/throughput for chaperone-responsive missense alleles; the feasibility QUESTION is reported, the thermodynamics are not supplied -> [O].

falsifiers.claim: GBA1 LOF lowers lysosomal glucosylceramide catabolism (substrate accumulates)
falsifiers.falsifier: a GBA1 LOF allele that INCREASES glucocerebrosidase throughput, or macrophages in which GBA1 loss REDUCES glucosylceramide, refutes the throughput-down direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: lysosomal glucocerebrosidase activity and glucosylceramide level in GBA1-deficient macrophages

falsifiers.claim: restoring enzyme throughput (replace / correct) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if supplying or stabilising the enzyme REDUCED catabolic throughput or RAISED substrate, the 'replace enzyme' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: substrate-clearance response to recombinant glucocerebrosidase in patient-derived macrophages

spinal_muscular_atrophy.summary: Loss-of-function of SMN1 lowers full-length SMN protein, the housekeeping factor for spliceosomal snRNP assembly, and motor neurons are selectively vulnerable to the deficit. The near-identical paralog SMN2 makes mostly exon-7-skipped (truncated) SMN, so promoting SMN2 exon-7 inclusion or replacing SMN1 raises full-length SMN -- the corrective direction.

causal_genes.note: SMN1 encodes the SMN snRNP-assembly housekeeping protein; homozygous LOF lowers full-length SMN, reducing motor-neuron viability (a required cellular component whose deficiency lowers integrity). Read as a structural/housekeeping LOF.
causal_genes.src: Lefebvre 1995 Cell 80:155 (SMN1 determines SMA)

context_genes.note: near-identical paralog; a c.840C>T silent change biases exon-7 SKIPPING so SMN2 makes mostly truncated SMN. SMN2 copy number modifies severity and is the splicing drug target.

therapeutic_axes.push: promote SMN2 exon-7 INCLUSION -> convert the backup paralog to full-length SMN (axis UP)
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: SMN2 splicing modifier (nusinersen -- ASO; risdiplam -- small molecule)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] full-length-SMN gain / motor-neuron rescue magnitude not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Finkel 2017 NEJM 377:1723 (nusinersen); Baranello 2021 NEJM 384:915 (risdiplam)

therapeutic_axes.push: deliver a functional SMN1 gene -> supply full-length SMN directly (axis UP)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] transduced SMN dose / durability not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Mendell 2017 NEJM 377:1713; onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma) FDA 2019

falsifiers.claim: SMN1 LOF lowers full-length SMN and motor-neuron survival
falsifiers.falsifier: an SMN1 LOF context with PRESERVED motor-neuron survival independent of SMN2 dosage, or a model where SMN1 loss RAISES full-length SMN, refutes the direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: full-length SMN protein and motor-neuron count in an SMN1-null background by SMN2 copy number

falsifiers.claim: raising full-length SMN (potentiate SMN2 / replace SMN1) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if SMN2 exon-7 inclusion or SMN1 addition REDUCED motor-neuron survival, the lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: motor-neuron survival response to an SMN2 splicing modifier in patient-derived motor neurons

duchenne_muscular_dystrophy.summary: A single-gene DMD loss-of-function (X-linked): out-of-frame deletions/duplications or nonsense alleles abolish dystrophin, the protein that anchors the muscle cytoskeleton to the sarcolemmal dystroglycan complex, so the membrane becomes fragile and muscle degenerates progressively -> the supply of FUNCTIONAL dystrophin (sarcolemmal structural integrity) is driven DOWN. The frame-disrupting lesion is a CODING change, not a promoter change (like sickle cell's coding missense): the promoter gamma read here is of the DMD LOCUS switch structure, and the disease direction is forced by the structural loss-of-function biology. In-frame deletions (Becker MD) leave a partial dystrophin -> milder, which is the dosage axis the corrective levers exploit. Magnitude [O].
duchenne_muscular_dystrophy.emergent_axis: sarcolemmal structural integrity (supply of functional dystrophin to muscle)

causal_genes.note: Dystrophin links F-actin to the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex at the sarcolemma; out-of-frame/null alleles abolish functional dystrophin -> membrane fragility and contraction-induced damage. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the frame-disrupting coding lesion (firewall). In-frame (Becker) deletions yield a shorter but partly functional dystrophin -> milder phenotype, consistent with a functional-dystrophin dosage axis.
causal_genes.src: Hoffman 1987 Cell 51:919; Koenig 1987 Cell 50:509

context_genes.note: Utrophin is the autosomal dystrophin paralogue, expressed in fetal/regenerating muscle; its sustained up-regulation can partially substitute for absent dystrophin (mutation-independent compensation axis).

therapeutic_axes.push: deliver a functional micro-dystrophin transgene -> restore a partial dystrophin at the sarcolemma
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] restored functional-dystrophin fraction / membrane-stabilisation magnitude not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Mendell 2023 JAMA Neurol; delandistrogene moxeparvovec (Elevidys) FDA 2023

therapeutic_axes.push: exon-skipping antisense restores the reading frame around the deletion -> a Becker-like internally-truncated but functional dystrophin
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotide (eteplirsen / golodirsen / viltolarsen / casimersen; exon-specific)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] frame-restored dystrophin level / clinical magnitude not derived from sequence; benefit is exon-specific
therapeutic_axes.src: Mendell 2013 Ann Neurol; eteplirsen FDA 2016 (accelerated)

therapeutic_axes.push: promote ribosomal read-through of a premature stop codon -> full-length dystrophin (nonsense-allele subset only)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] read-through efficiency / dystrophin recovery not derived from sequence; nonsense-mutation subset only
therapeutic_axes.src: Bushby 2014 Muscle Nerve; ataluren EMA conditional 2014

therapeutic_axes.push: up-regulate the dystrophin paralogue utrophin to compensate for absent dystrophin (mutation-independent)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] utrophin-compensation magnitude not derived; the lead modulator did not meet its primary endpoint -- direction-only
therapeutic_axes.src: Tinsley 1996 Nature 384:349; PhaseOut DMD (ezutromid) 2018

falsifiers.claim: DMD LOF lowers the sarcolemmal structural-integrity axis (functional dystrophin supply DOWN)
falsifiers.falsifier: a DMD out-of-frame/null allele that PRESERVED or INCREASED sarcolemmal integrity / functional dystrophin would refute the structural-loss direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: sarcolemmal dystrophin immunostaining and membrane-integrity (serum CK / Evans-blue dye uptake) by genotype in a Dmd-null model

falsifiers.claim: restoring partial dystrophin (replace / exon-skip / read-through) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if supplying micro-dystrophin or frame-restored dystrophin WORSENED or failed to improve sarcolemmal integrity, the restore-dystrophin lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: membrane-integrity / muscle-function response to micro-dystrophin transfer or exon-skipping in a Dmd-null model

huntington_disease.summary: A single-gene HTT CAG-repeat EXPANSION in exon 1 produces a polyglutamine huntingtin with a dominant TOXIC gain-of-function that progressively impairs striatal (medium spiny) neuron homeostasis and survival -- a pathological BRAKE on the neuronal program -- so the striatal-neuron axis is driven DOWN. The lesion is a CODING repeat expansion, not a promoter change (exactly like sickle cell's coding missense): the promoter gamma read here is of the HTT LOCUS switch structure, and the disease direction is forced by the toxic gain-of-function biology. Longer repeats -> earlier onset (the repeat-length/dosage axis), but the repeat tract itself is not read from the promoter window. An approved SYMPTOMATIC therapy for chorea exists (VMAT2 inhibitors) but does not address the HTT switch; no disease-modifying therapy is yet approved. Magnitude [O].

causal_genes.note: An expanded CAG tract (commonly >36 repeats) in HTT exon 1 yields polyglutamine-huntingtin that acts as a dominant TOXIC gain-of-function -- a pathological brake on striatal neuronal homeostasis (proteostasis / mitochondrial / transcriptional dysregulation and aggregation) -> neuronal function and survival suppressed. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the CAG-repeat coding lesion (firewall), exactly as for HBB's coding missense. Repeat length sets onset but is not read from the promoter window.
causal_genes.src: MacDonald 1993 Cell 72:971 (HDCRG); DiFiglia 1997 Science 277:1990

therapeutic_axes.push: lower mutant huntingtin transcript -> relieve the toxic gain-of-function brake on striatal neurons
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] HTT-lowering magnitude and neuronal-rescue extent not derived from sequence; no disease-modifying therapy is yet approved
therapeutic_axes.src: Tabrizi 2019 NEJM 380:2307; GENERATION HD program

therapeutic_axes.push: AAV-delivered microRNA durably lowers huntingtin in striatum -> relieve the toxic brake
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] durable-knockdown magnitude / clinical effect not derived from sequence; investigational
therapeutic_axes.src: Spronck 2019 Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev; uniQure AMT-130 program

therapeutic_axes.push: allele-selective lowering directed at the expanded allele (repeat/SNP context) -> spare wild-type huntingtin
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] allele selectivity / wild-type sparing not derived from sequence; direction-only
therapeutic_axes.src: Carroll 2011 Mol Ther; Southwell 2014 Mol Ther

falsifiers.claim: mutant HTT (CAG expansion, toxic GOF) lowers the striatal-neuron homeostasis/survival axis
falsifiers.falsifier: a CAG-expanded HTT allele that PRESERVED or IMPROVED striatal neuron survival/function would refute the toxic-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: striatal medium-spiny-neuron survival / striatal volume by CAG-length genotype in an HTT-expansion model

falsifiers.claim: lowering mutant huntingtin (reduce HTT) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if HTT-lowering WORSENED or failed to improve striatal neuronal survival/function, the reduce-HTT lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: striatal neuron survival / motor-behaviour response to HTT-lowering in an HTT-expansion model

rett_syndrome.summary: A single-gene MECP2 loss-of-function (X-linked, mostly de novo) removes the methyl-CpG-binding transcriptional regulator MeCP2 that is broadly required for post-natal neuronal maturation and synaptic regulation, so the MeCP2-dependent program is under-driven and that axis is forced DOWN. MECP2 is sharply DOSAGE-SENSITIVE in BOTH directions: too little causes Rett, too much causes a DISTINCT opposite-direction disorder (MECP2 duplication syndrome, OMIM 300260), so the corrective window is narrow and the corrective MAGNITUDE is especially [O]. Most lesions are coding/nonsense, OUTSIDE the promoter gamma firewall (like sickle cell's coding missense); gamma reads the MECP2 LOCUS switch structure. This entry nearly approaches SUSPENSION on dosage grounds, but the cause is a single readable locus with a forced LOF direction, so it RESOLVES with the dosage caveat made explicit. An approved therapy (trofinetide) acts DOWNSTREAM (IGF-1 / synaptic maturation) and does NOT restore MeCP2.
rett_syndrome.emergent_axis: MeCP2-dependent neuronal maturation / synaptic regulation program
rett_syndrome.direction_confidence_basis: MECP2 is exquisitely DOSAGE-SENSITIVE in BOTH directions: loss of function causes Rett syndrome, while the mirror gain -- a genomic duplication of the same MECP2 -- causes MECP2 duplication syndrome, an independently catalogued disease (the kit resolves it separately as the opposite, axis-DOWN read). The corrective direction for Rett is therefore raise MeCP2 function (axis UP), but the therapeutic window is narrow because overshoot reproduces the duplication phenotype; the direction is forced yet the dosage target is two-sided-contested (Chao 2012 Curr Opin Genet Dev 22:308, MeCP2 dosage; Collins 2004 Hum Mol Genet 13:2679, MECP2 duplication = the gain phenotype; Sandweiss 2020 Lancet Neurol 19:689, restoring MeCP2 within a bounded window).

causal_genes.note: MeCP2 is a methyl-CpG-binding transcriptional modulator broadly required for post-natal neuronal maturation and synaptic function; LOF (nonsense / missense / frameshift, X-linked) under-drives that program -> Rett. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). CAUTION -- dosage-sensitive in BOTH directions: MECP2 gain/duplication causes a DISTINCT opposite-direction disorder (MECP2 duplication syndrome, OMIM 300260), so the forced direction here is specific to the LOF (Rett) read and any correction must respect a narrow dosage window.
causal_genes.src: Amir 1999 Nat Genet 23:185; Chahrour 2008 Science 320:1224

context_genes.note: IGF-1 / IGF1R signalling promotes synaptic maturation downstream of MeCP2 deficiency and is the axis engaged by an approved symptomatic therapy; it partially compensates but does NOT restore MeCP2.

therapeutic_axes.push: deliver a DOSAGE-CONTROLLED functional MECP2 transgene -> restore MeCP2 toward the normal narrow window
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: dosage-regulated MECP2 gene transfer (investigational; e.g. mini-/feedback-regulated AAV-MECP2, TSHA-102, NGN-401)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] restored-MeCP2 level not derived from sequence; OVER-supply risks duplication-type toxicity -- correction must stay within a narrow dosage window
therapeutic_axes.src: Gadalla 2013 Mol Ther; Sinnett 2017 Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev; TSHA-102 / NGN-401 clinical programs

therapeutic_axes.push: reactivate the silenced wild-type MECP2 allele on the inactive X -> restore endogenous, natively-regulated MeCP2
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: X-reactivation of the wild-type MECP2 allele (investigational)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] reactivation efficiency / cell fraction not derived from sequence; investigational
therapeutic_axes.src: Carrette 2018 PNAS 115:E668; Lyst & Bird 2015 Nat Rev Genet 16:261

therapeutic_axes.push: promote read-through of a premature stop codon -> full-length MeCP2 (nonsense-allele subset only)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] read-through efficiency / MeCP2 recovery not derived from sequence; nonsense-allele subset only
therapeutic_axes.src: Merritt 2020 Sci Transl Med; Pitsch 2022

therapeutic_axes.push: potentiate downstream IGF-1 / synaptic-maturation signalling to partially compensate for MeCP2 deficiency (does NOT restore MeCP2)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] downstream-compensation magnitude not derived from sequence; symptomatic -- does not correct the MeCP2 switch itself
therapeutic_axes.src: Neul 2023 Nat Med (LAVENDER); trofinetide (Daybue) FDA 2023

falsifiers.claim: MECP2 LOF under-drives the MeCP2-dependent neuronal-maturation / synaptic axis (axis DOWN)
falsifiers.falsifier: a MECP2 null/LOF allele that PRESERVED or INCREASED MeCP2-dependent neuronal maturation/synaptic function would refute the LOF-under-drive direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: MeCP2-target synaptic/maturation readouts (dendritic complexity, synaptic markers, RTT-phenotype score) by genotype in a Mecp2-null model

falsifiers.claim: restoring MeCP2 within a narrow dosage window (replace / reactivate) is the CORRECTIVE direction

alpha1_antitrypsin_deficiency.summary: A single-gene SERPINA1 deficiency: the common Z allele (Glu342Lys) mis-folds, so little functional alpha-1-antitrypsin (the principal serpin that inhibits neutrophil elastase) reaches the circulation -> the antiprotease protection of lung tissue is driven DOWN (unopposed elastase -> early emphysema). This is a SUPPLY-DEFICIENCY (loss-of-function) read on the antiprotease axis, and the approved therapy SUPPLIES the missing protein (augmentation). NOTE the disease is genuinely TWO-SIDED: the same Z allele also has a hepatic TOXIC gain-of-function (Z-polymer accumulates in hepatocytes -> liver disease), a DISTINCT axis the single loss-of-function direction here does NOT fold in; an RNAi approach (silencing SERPINA1) targets that hepatic axis and would LOWER circulating A1AT, so it is not a corrective on the antiprotease axis. The gamma read is of the SERPINA1 locus switch structure; the Glu342Lys lesion is a coding change outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
alpha1_antitrypsin_deficiency.emergent_axis: functional circulating alpha-1-antitrypsin (neutrophil-elastase antiprotease protection of lung tissue)
alpha1_antitrypsin_deficiency.direction_confidence_basis: AATD carries TWO opposite corrective directions in two organs from the same SERPINA1 lesion: in the LUNG it is a loss-of-function antiprotease axis (the Z allele yields too little secreted functional alpha-1-antitrypsin -> unopposed neutrophil elastase -> emphysema), correct = raise functional AAT (augmentation / wild-type replacement, axis UP); in the LIVER it is a toxic gain-of-function axis (the misfolded Z protein POLYMERISES and accumulates in hepatocytes -> hepatotoxicity/cirrhosis), correct = reduce the polymerising Z species (hepatic SERPINA1 knockdown, fazirsiran/ARO-AAT, axis DOWN). The engine emerges one axis; the direction is clean within each organ but organ-contested across the disease (Gooptu 2009 Annu Rev Biochem 78:147, serpin polymerisation gain/loss; Strnad 2020 NEJM 382:1443, AATD lung-vs-liver; Strnad 2023 NEJM 389:514, fazirsiran Z-polymer knockdown).

causal_genes.note: SERPINA1 encodes alpha-1-antitrypsin, the major circulating inhibitor of neutrophil elastase; the Z allele (Glu342Lys) mis-folds and polymerises, so secreted functional antiprotease falls -> loss of lung antiprotease protection. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the Glu342Lys coding lesion (firewall). The hepatic Z-polymer toxic gain-of-function is a separate axis (see summary), not the primary antiprotease loss read here (SERPINA1 gene OMIM 107400).
causal_genes.src: Laurell & Eriksson 1963; Lomas 1992 Nature 357:605 (Z-polymerisation)

hereditary_tyrosinaemia_type_1.summary: A single-gene FAH loss-of-function removes fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase, the LAST enzyme of tyrosine catabolism. FAH normally consumes (detoxifies) fumarylacetoacetate; without it, fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone ACCUMULATE and are hepato- and nephro-toxic -> the toxic-catabolite burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on toxic accumulation (FAH brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> burden UP). The approved therapy is COUNTER-INTUITIVE and the kit re-derives it: nitisinone blocks the UPSTREAM enzyme HPD so the toxic intermediate is never formed (an upstream RESTRAINT), rather than restoring FAH. Definitive correction is restoring FAH (liver transplantation; FAH gene therapy investigational), with dietary tyrosine/phenylalanine restriction as adjunct. The gamma read is of the FAH locus switch structure; the disease lesion is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
hereditary_tyrosinaemia_type_1.emergent_axis: toxic upstream tyrosine-catabolite burden (fumarylacetoacetate / succinylacetone accumulation)

The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the TOXIC BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it.

wilson_disease.summary: A single-gene ATP7B loss-of-function disables the copper-transporting ATPase that exports hepatic copper into bile and loads it onto ceruloplasmin. Without it, copper is not excreted and ACCUMULATES in liver and brain, where free copper is toxic -> the copper burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on copper accumulation (ATP7B brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> copper UP). The kit re-derives the approved therapy, which REMOVES or BLOCKS copper rather than restoring the transporter: chelation (penicillamine / trientine) promotes urinary copper excretion, and zinc blocks intestinal copper absorption (maintenance); restoring ATP7B export is investigational gene therapy. The gamma read is of the ATP7B locus switch structure; the disease lesion is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
wilson_disease.emergent_axis: free / loosely-bound copper burden (hepatic and CNS copper accumulation)

causal_genes.note: ATP7B is a copper-transporting P-type ATPase that exports hepatic copper to bile and loads ceruloplasmin. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the COPPER BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it.

mecp2_duplication_syndrome.summary: A single-locus MECP2 GAIN-of-dosage: a duplication spanning MECP2 (Xq28) roughly doubles MeCP2, and because MeCP2 is sharply dosage-sensitive, the MeCP2-dependent neuronal regulation program is OVER-driven -> that axis is driven UP. This is the EXACT OPPOSITE-direction read of Rett on the SAME cached MECP2 locus (Rett = LOF, axis DOWN, corrective = raise MeCP2; duplication = GOF, axis UP, corrective = lower MeCP2) -- one gene, both dosage directions, both under the firewall. There is no approved therapy; lowering MeCP2 toward normal (antisense) reverses phenotypes in duplication models and is the lead investigational direction, with a NARROW window (over-lowering tips toward the Rett-like loss). The gamma read is of the MECP2 locus switch structure. Magnitude [O].

causal_genes.note: A copy-number GAIN at Xq28 spanning MECP2 increases MeCP2 dosage; as a broadly-acting transcriptional regulator, EXCESS MeCP2 OVER-drives its program -> axis UP. This is the mirror of the Rett LOF read on the same locus. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the lesion here is a structural copy-number gain, and dosage/magnitude is [O]. CAUTION: dosage-sensitive in BOTH directions -- correction must respect a narrow window (over-lowering reproduces Rett-like loss).

transthyretin_amyloidosis.summary: A single-gene TTR proteinopathy: destabilising TTR variants (e.g. Val30Met, Val122Ile) let the transthyretin tetramer dissociate, misfold and deposit as amyloid fibrils in peripheral nerve and heart, progressively SUPPRESSING nerve and cardiac function. Like Huntington, the toxic GAIN is read as an over-active pathological BRAKE on organ function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), and the kit re-derives the approved therapies, which REMOVE the toxic species rather than treating symptoms: TTR-lowering silencers (patisiran / vutrisiran siRNA; inotersen / eplontersen antisense) and a tetramer STABILISER (tafamidis) that blocks dissociation/misfolding; in-vivo CRISPR knockdown is clinical. The gamma read is of the TTR locus switch structure; the destabilising point mutations are coding changes outside the promoter firewall. (The non-hereditary wild-type form, ATTRwt, is an age/conformational aggregation of normal TTR, not a germline sequence lesion, and is outside this single-gene read.) Magnitude [O].
transthyretin_amyloidosis.emergent_axis: nerve and cardiac tissue function (progressively suppressed by TTR amyloid deposition)

causal_genes.note: TTR encodes transthyretin, normally a stable tetrameric transport protein (thyroxine / retinol-binding protein). Destabilising variants promote tetramer dissociation and misfolding into amyloid; the deposited fibrils act as a toxic GAIN that SUPPRESSES nerve and cardiac function -- read here as an over-active pathological BRAKE on organ function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), the same proteinopathy framing used for Huntington. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the destabilising coding lesion's magnitude (firewall).
causal_genes.src: Saraiva 1984 (Val30Met); Jacobson 1997 (Val122Ile); Coelho 2013 NEJM (silencing/stabiliser)

context_genes.note: RBP4 (retinol-binding protein 4) is transthyretin's physiological transport partner; it frames TTR's normal carrier role but is not the amyloidogenic lesion.

acute_intermittent_porphyria.summary: A single-gene HMBS loss-of-function partially blocks heme synthesis at the hydroxymethylbilane-synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase) step. HMBS normally consumes porphobilinogen; when it is deficient, the upstream neurotoxic precursors delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG) ACCUMULATE during attacks -> the toxic-precursor burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on precursor accumulation (HMBS brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> burden UP), the tyrosinaemia pattern. The kit re-derives the approved therapy, which RESTRAINS the UPSTREAM rate-limiting enzyme ALAS1 rather than restoring HMBS: givosiran (an ALAS1-knockdown siRNA) and hemin (heme feedback that down-regulates ALAS1) both lower ALA/PBG production; restoring HMBS (liver transplantation; gene therapy investigational) is definitive. The gamma read is of the HMBS locus switch structure; the disease lesion is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
acute_intermittent_porphyria.emergent_axis: toxic heme-precursor burden (delta-aminolevulinic acid / porphobilinogen accumulation)

primary_hyperoxaluria_type_1.summary: A single-gene AGXT loss-of-function. The liver-peroxisomal enzyme alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase normally detoxifies glyoxylate by transaminating it to glycine; when AGXT is deficient, glyoxylate is instead oxidised to oxalate, so endogenous oxalate is OVER-produced -> the toxic oxalate burden is driven UP (calcium-oxalate nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, and ultimately systemic oxalosis). Read as a released BRAKE on oxalate accumulation (AGXT brakes the build-up; LOF releases it -> burden UP) -- the tyrosinaemia / porphyria pattern. The kit re-derives the approved therapy, which RESTRAINS the UPSTREAM oxalate-producing flux rather than restoring AGXT: lumasiran (an HAO1/glycolate-oxidase-knockdown siRNA) lowers glyoxylate supply, and nedosiran (an LDHA-knockdown siRNA) lowers the final glyoxylate->oxalate step; both reduce oxalate production. Restoring AGXT itself (liver transplantation, historically the definitive correction; AGXT gene / hepatocyte therapy investigational) is the function-restoring lever. The gamma read is of the AGXT locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion (e.g. the Gly170Arg peroxisome-to-mitochondrion mistargeting allele) is coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

causal_genes.note: AGXT (alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase) is the liver-peroxisomal enzyme that transaminates glyoxylate to glycine, keeping oxalate production in check. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the TOXIC OXALATE BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it.

hereditary_angioedema.summary: A single-gene SERPING1 loss-of-function. C1-inhibitor (a serpin) is the principal brake on the contact (kallikrein-kinin) system, inhibiting plasma kallikrein and activated factor XII. When SERPING1 is deficient (type I, low C1-INH) or dysfunctional (type II, normal-level but inactive C1-INH), the kallikrein-kinin cascade is disinhibited, so bradykinin is OVER-produced -> the bradykinin burden is driven UP, causing recurrent bradykinin-mediated angioedema attacks. Read as a released serpin BRAKE on the kallikrein-bradykinin cascade (C1-INH brakes it; LOF releases it -> bradykinin UP). Molecularly this is a SERPIN loss like alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency (SERPINA1) -- the same protein family failing -- but where A1AT is read on the protective-antiprotease-LEVEL axis (DOWN), hereditary angioedema's defining axis is the downstream bradykinin OVER-production (UP), so it joins the axis-UP toxic-over-production class. The kit re-derives BOTH approved arms: RESTRAIN the over-active downstream cascade (plasma-kallikrein inhibitors lanadelumab / ecallantide / berotralstat; bradykinin B2-receptor antagonist icatibant for acute attacks) AND RESTORE the serpin brake by replacement (C1-esterase-inhibitor concentrate). The gamma read is of the SERPING1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the coding / regulatory lesions are outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

causal_genes.note: SERPING1 encodes C1-inhibitor, the serpin that restrains plasma kallikrein and activated factor XII (and C1). As a BRAKE on the contact / kallikrein-kinin cascade, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> plasma kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen unchecked -> bradykinin accumulates and raises vascular permeability. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding / regulatory lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the BRADYKININ BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it. (Same serpin family as SERPINA1 / A1AT, but the defining axis here is the downstream over-production rather than a protective-level loss.)
causal_genes.src: Donaldson & Evans 1963 (C1-INH deficiency in HAE); Zuraw 2008 NEJM review (bradykinin mechanism)

ornithine_transcarbamylase_deficiency.summary: The commonest urea-cycle disorder. Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC), the mitochondrial enzyme that condenses carbamoyl phosphate with ornithine to make citrulline, is the second committed step of the urea cycle that disposes of waste nitrogen as urea. OTC loss-of-function STALLS the cycle, so ammonia (and its upstream carrier glutamine) is no longer cleared and the toxic waste-nitrogen burden is driven UP -> hyperammonaemia (neonatal encephalopathy in hemizygous males; episodic decompensation in heterozygous females). Read as a released BRAKE on ammonia accumulation (OTC brakes the build-up by feeding the detoxifying cycle; LOF releases it -> burden UP) -- the tyrosinaemia / porphyria toxic-metabolite pattern. The kit re-derives the approved therapy, which RESTRAINS the waste-nitrogen burden rather than restoring OTC: nitrogen scavengers (glycerol phenylbutyrate; sodium phenylbutyrate; sodium benzoate + sodium phenylacetate) open an alternative excretion route (phenylacetate conjugates glutamine to phenylacetylglutamine; benzoate conjugates glycine to hippurate; both excreted in urine), and urea-cycle substrate repletion (citrulline / arginine) feeds the distal cycle past the block; both lower the ammonia burden. Restoring OTC itself (liver transplantation, the definitive correction; AAV-OTC / OTC-mRNA gene therapy investigational) is the function-restoring lever. The gamma read is of the OTC locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/splice (e.g. the milder late-onset Arg40His missense allele), outside the promoter firewall. X-linked (Xp11.4), so penetrance/severity are zygosity- and X-inactivation-dependent and held [O] (the B10 X-linked caveat). Magnitude [O].

x_linked_hypophosphataemia.summary: The commonest heritable form of rickets/osteomalacia. PHEX (a membrane endopeptidase expressed by osteocytes/osteoblasts) normally restrains the bone hormone FGF23; PHEX loss-of-function RELEASES that restraint, so circulating FGF23 is OVER-produced. Excess FGF23 downregulates the renal sodium-phosphate cotransporters (NaPi-2a/2c) and suppresses 1-alpha-hydroxylase, causing renal phosphate wasting with inappropriately low calcitriol -> hypophosphataemic rickets, bowing, short stature, dental abscesses and enthesopathy. Read as a released BRAKE on FGF23 (PHEX brakes FGF23; LOF releases it -> FGF23 burden UP) -- the same released-brake -> downstream-over-production pattern as the toxic-metabolite axis-UP diseases, here on a HORMONE axis. The kit re-derives the approved targeted therapy, which RESTRAINS the FGF23 axis: burosumab, an anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody, neutralises the excess hormone and restores renal phosphate reabsorption. Restoring PHEX itself (gene therapy preclinical) is the function-restoring lever. Conventional oral phosphate + active vitamin D (calcitriol/alfacalcidol) is the older symptomatic standard that repletes the downstream phosphate/calcitriol deficit but does NOT lower FGF23 (it can raise it), so it sits OUTSIDE this FGF23 switch axis and is noted as downstream-symptomatic, not a switch lever. The gamma read is of the PHEX locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/deletion (loss-of-function variants across PHEX), outside the promoter firewall. X-linked dominant (Xp22.11); the link PHEX-loss -> FGF23-excess is functionally established while the precise enzymatic substrate is still investigated. Magnitude [O].

pompe_disease.summary: Glycogen storage disease type II (acid maltase deficiency) -- the first lysosomal storage disease ever recognised. Loss-of-function of acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses glycogen to glucose, lowers lysosomal glycogen catabolism so glycogen ACCUMULATES in the lysosomes of cardiac and skeletal muscle -> hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and profound hypotonia in the infantile form; progressive limb-girdle and respiratory (diaphragm) weakness in the late-onset form. The catabolic throughput axis is driven DOWN; correction is to restore enzymatic throughput (replace the enzyme / stabilise the delivered enzyme) or to lower the upstream glycogen load. A lysosomal-storage read on the same level axis as Gaucher, A1AT-style level and Fabry -- but AUTOSOMAL recessive (17q25.3), a fourth storage read on a third enzyme that extends the storage class off the X chromosome. The kit re-derives the approved throughput-restore arms -- replace GAA (enzyme replacement: alglucosidase alfa, avalglucosidase alfa) + correct via a chaperone-stabilised co-dose (cipaglucosidase alfa + miglustat, where miglustat stabilises the recombinant enzyme so more active enzyme reaches the lysosome). The gamma read is of the GAA locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/splice (e.g. the common late-onset leaky-splice IVS1 c.-32-13T>G allele), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

hypophosphatasia.summary: Inborn error of bone mineralization. Loss-of-function of ALPL -- the gene for tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNSALP), the ectoenzyme that dephosphorylates extracellular inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP) and phosphoethanolamine -- lowers TNSALP throughput, so its substrate PPi ACCUMULATES extracellularly. Because PPi is a potent INHIBITOR of hydroxyapatite crystal growth, the deficient enzyme leaves mineralization over-inhibited: rickets/osteomalacia, premature deciduous tooth loss, and in the perinatal/infantile forms respiratory insufficiency and PLP-dependent (vitamin-B6-responsive) seizures. The disease is read as the TNSALP substrate-dephosphorylation / mineralization-throughput axis driven DOWN (a deficient ectoenzyme whose substrate accumulates -- the same enzyme-deficiency-with-substrate-accumulation shape as the lysosomal storage reads, here on an extracellular mineralization enzyme rather than a lysosomal catabolic one). Correction is to restore enzymatic throughput (replace the enzyme). The kit re-derives the approved replace arm -- asfotase alfa, a bone-targeted recombinant TNSALP-Fc-deca-aspartate enzyme replacement that homes to mineralizing matrix and restores local PPi hydrolysis. This pairs with X-linked hypophosphataemia as the OPPOSITE bone-mineral defect: HPP is an ALPL enzyme DEFICIENCY read on the throughput axis DOWN (replace the enzyme), whereas XLH is a PHEX released-brake read on the FGF23 hormone axis UP (restrain the excess hormone). The gamma read is of the ALPL locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding (e.g. p.Glu191Lys, p.Ala116Thr), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O]. NOTE: high-dose vitamin D / calcium / phosphate are NOT corrective switch levers here (they do not restore TNSALP and can drive hypercalcaemia/nephrocalcinosis), and pyridoxine (B6) addresses only the downstream PLP-seizure consequence -- both are downstream-symptomatic, not switch levers (the XLH/Rett downstream-agent discipline).

leber_congenital_amaurosis_2.summary: Severe early-onset inherited retinal dystrophy. Loss-of-function of RPE65 -- the retinal-pigment-epithelium isomerohydrolase (retinoid isomerase) that converts all-trans-retinyl ester to 11-cis-retinol in the visual (retinoid) cycle -- lowers regeneration of the 11-cis-retinal chromophore, so rod and (progressively) cone photoreceptors cannot reconstitute light-sensitive visual pigment -> profound congenital/early-childhood vision loss with a characteristically severe ERG deficit out of proportion to early retinal structure. The disease is read as the retinoid-cycle / 11-cis-retinal-regeneration throughput axis driven DOWN (a deficient catabolic-cycle enzyme whose product fails -- the same enzyme-deficiency shape as the lysosomal storage and HPP reads, here on the RPE retinoid-cycle enzyme; the consequence is chromophore STARVATION rather than substrate storage). Correction is to restore the cycle: replace RPE65 at the locus, or supply the missing cis-retinoid chromophore downstream to bypass the block. The kit re-derives the approved replace arm -- voretigene neparvovec, an AAV2-hRPE65v2 subretinal gene-replacement therapy (the first in-vivo gene therapy approved in the US, 2017). This is the clean case where restoring the deficient gene IS the lead corrective lever -- in contrast to the upstream-restraint diseases (OTC, AIP, PH1) where the lead lever is NOT restoring the deficient gene but diverting an upstream over-accumulating flux; here the deficiency directly starves a needed product, so gene restoration is corrective. A first OCULAR / retinal read for the kit. The gamma read is of the RPE65 locus switch STRUCTURE (an AT-rich promoter, one of the lowest gamma in the kit); the disease lesion is coding (e.g. p.Pro25Leu, p.Tyr368His, founder splice alleles), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

hypertrophic_cardiomyopathy.summary: The commonest inherited cardiac disease, a sarcomere contractility disorder. Two leading causal genes converge on the SAME emergent axis -- the cardiac sarcomere's contractile output -- and drive it UP (hypercontractility): MYH7 (beta-myosin heavy chain) missense alleles are GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (more force-generating cross-bridges / raised actin-activated ATPase), and MYBPC3 (cardiac myosin-binding protein C) truncating alleles are LOSS-OF-FUNCTION of a normal BRAKE on cross-bridge cycling (haploinsufficiency disinhibits contraction). Both therefore perturb the contractile axis UP, producing left-ventricular hypertrophy, hyperdynamic systole, impaired relaxation, and (often) dynamic outflow obstruction. This is read as a NEW KIND of emergent axis for the kit -- a MECHANICAL / contractile axis (force, cross-bridge duty ratio), not a chemical concentration, enzyme throughput, ion or hormone level -- driven UP, so the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN it. The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm -- mavacamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor that lowers the number of force-generating myosin cross-bridges and thereby the hypercontractile output (the first sarcomere-targeted HCM drug). MYH7 is the deeper switch (higher gamma) and is picked as the primary; MYBPC3 is the second causal switch, both perturbing UP. Restoring the MYBPC3 brake (gene-level) is recorded as a restrain-coded lever because its NET effect on the emergent contractile axis is to LOWER it (the same net-effect lever convention used for OTC, where restoring the deficient gene is coded by its axis effect, not its molecular direction). Symptomatic agents (beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers, disopyramide) reduce rate/obstruction but do NOT target the sarcomere hypercontractility switch and are recorded as downstream-symptomatic, NOT switch levers (the XLH/Rett downstream-agent discipline). The gamma reads are of the MYH7 and MYBPC3 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding (MYH7 missense e.g. p.Arg403Gln; MYBPC3 truncating/splice e.g. founder c.3628-41_3628-17del, p.Trp792fs), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
hypertrophic_cardiomyopathy.emergent_axis: cardiac sarcomere contractile output (myosin cross-bridge cycling / actin-activated ATPase duty ratio) -- a mechanical/contractile axis

causal_genes.note: MYH7 encodes the beta-cardiac myosin heavy chain, the force-generating motor of the ventricular sarcomere. HCM missense alleles are gain-of-function: they raise actin-activated ATPase and the fraction of myosin heads available for force generation (destabilising the auto-inhibited super-relaxed state), i.e. hypercontractility -> the contractile axis is pushed UP. Located 14q11.2 (CMH1, OMIM 192600). NCBI official symbol MYH7. Autosomal dominant. Coding missense lesions (e.g. p.Arg403Gln, p.Arg453Cys); promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Geisterfer-Lowrance 1990 Cell 62:999 (MYH7 Arg403Gln, the first HCM mutation); Alfares 2015 Genet Med 17:880 (MYH7/MYBPC3 dominate HCM genetics); Anderson 2018 PNAS 115:E7486 (HCM alleles destabilise the super-relaxed state -> hypercontractility)

causal_genes.note: MYBPC3 encodes cardiac myosin-binding protein C, which normally RESTRAINS actomyosin cross-bridge cycling (a brake that slows/limits contraction). Most HCM alleles are truncating -> haploinsufficiency -> loss of the brake -> disinhibited cross-bridge cycling -> hypercontractility -> the contractile axis is pushed UP (same direction as MYH7 GOF). Located 11p11.2 (CMH4, OMIM 115197). NCBI official symbol MYBPC3. Autosomal dominant; a common founder truncating allele exists in South Asian populations. Coding/splice truncating lesions; promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Watkins 1995 Nat Genet 11:434 and Bonne 1995 Nat Genet 11:438 (MYBPC3 mutations in HCM); Harris 2002 Circ Res 90:594 (MyBP-C restrains cross-bridge cycling / brake function); Dhandapany 2009 Nat Genet 41:187 (MYBPC3 25bp founder deletion)

down_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a WHOLE-CHROMOSOME dosage change (an extra copy of chromosome 21), not a single-gene promoter switch. The emergence engine reads a promoter switch-threshold (gamma) per locus; a chromosomal aneuploidy is not a single-gene gamma shift, so there is no analyzable monogenic DNA read here. Held, per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). A dosage-of-many-genes model is future work, not a v0.1.0 emergence.
down_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- chromosomal dosage, not a single-gene switch)

prader_willi_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is loss of function of PATERNALLY-EXPRESSED, maternally-imprinted genes in 15q11-q13 -- typically a paternal multi-megabase DELETION, maternal uniparental disomy, or an IMPRINTING-CENTRE defect -- not a single-gene promoter switch. The lesion is structural / epigenetic: a parent-of-origin methylation and dosage state spanning many genes, so there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). This hold is a DIFFERENT KIND from Down syndrome's: Down is whole-chromosome aneuploidy, Prader-Willi is an imprinting/structural cause. A parent-of-origin (epigenetic) multi-gene model is future work, not a v0.1.0 single-switch emergence.
prader_willi_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- imprinting/structural cause, not a single-gene switch)

familial_chylomicronaemia_syndrome.summary: A rare autosomal-recessive disorder of extreme hypertriglyceridaemia. Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) is the endothelial enzyme that hydrolyses triglyceride in circulating chylomicrons and VLDL -- functionally a BRAKE that keeps plasma triglyceride low by clearing it. Biallelic LPL loss-of-function (the commonest cause; GPIHBP1, APOA5, LMF1, APOC2 give the same syndrome) RELEASES that brake, so chylomicrons are not cleared and plasma triglyceride over-accumulates -- the emergent lipid-metabolite axis is driven UP (fasting chylomicronaemia, recurrent acute pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomata, lipaemia retinalis). This is read with the released-brake -> downstream over-accumulation pattern already used for the toxic-metabolite diseases (tyrosinaemia, porphyria, hyperoxaluria, OTC), now carried onto a NEW lipid metabolite -- triglyceride -- and is the OPPOSITE mode to familial hypercholesterolaemia, where the defect is loss of LDL-cholesterol clearance read on the level-restore (axis-DOWN) side. Because the axis is driven UP, the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN it. The lead lever the switch re-derives is to RESTRAIN apolipoprotein C-III (APOC3): ApoC-III is an endogenous INHIBITOR of LPL, so lowering it DE-REPRESSES LPL and restores triglyceride clearance -- the approved hepatocyte-targeted APOC3 antisense oligonucleotide olezarsen, and the EU-approved APOC3 ASO volanesorsen, both act this way (the APOC3-siRNA plozasiran is late-stage clinical). Restoring LPL itself (gene therapy) is recorded as a restrain-coded lever because its NET effect on the emergent triglyceride axis is DOWN (the OTC net-effect convention); alipogene tiparvovec, an AAV1-LPL gene therapy, was historically the first gene therapy approved in the Western world (EMA 2012) and was later commercially withdrawn, so current LPL gene-therapy programmes are investigational. Conventional very-low-fat diet and fibrates/omega-3 are recorded as supportive / largely ineffective in true LPL-null FCS and are NOT switch levers. The gamma read is of the LPL promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding (e.g. LPL p.Gly188Glu, p.Asp9Asn), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
familial_chylomicronaemia_syndrome.emergent_axis: circulating triglyceride / chylomicron burden (plasma triglyceride clearance) -- a lipid-metabolite axis

causal_genes.note: LPL encodes lipoprotein lipase, the endothelial-surface enzyme (anchored via GPIHBP1) that hydrolyses core triglyceride in chylomicrons and VLDL, clearing plasma triglyceride. It is the physiological BRAKE on circulating triglyceride. Biallelic LOF (null/severe-hypomorph) abolishes clearance -> the brake is released -> the triglyceride axis is pushed UP (fasting chylomicronaemia). Located 8p21.3 (OMIM 609708). NCBI official symbol LPL. Autosomal recessive. Coding lesions (e.g. p.Gly188Glu founder allele; p.Asp9Asn); promoter firewall respected.

context_genes.note: APOC3 (apolipoprotein C-III, in the APOA1/APOC3/APOA4/APOA5 cluster at 11q23.3) is an endogenous INHIBITOR of LPL and of hepatic remnant uptake -- i.e. a brake ON the clearance brake. Lowering ApoC-III DE-REPRESSES LPL and accelerates triglyceride clearance, which is why it is the lead therapeutic target (olezarsen / volanesorsen / plozasiran). Loss-of-function APOC3 variants are associated with low triglyceride and cardioprotection (the human-genetics validation of the target).

friedreich_ataxia.summary: The commonest inherited ataxia, an autosomal-recessive neurodegeneration. Frataxin (FXN) is a small mitochondrial protein that ACCELERATES iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis (it binds and allosterically activates the NFS1 cysteine-desulfurase assembly complex and chaperones iron), so Fe-S-dependent enzymes (aconitase, respiratory-chain complexes) and oxidative-phosphorylation capacity depend on it. The disease is driven by an intronic GAA triplet-repeat expansion in FXN that epigenetically silences transcription -> frataxin is DEFICIENT -> Fe-S cluster biogenesis and mitochondrial bioenergetics are UNDER-driven -> the emergent axis falls (progressive spinocerebellar and sensory ataxia, plus hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and diabetes). This is read as a DEFICIENCY-driven neurodegeneration -- the contrast to the kit's toxic-aggregate neurodegenerations (Huntington HTT gain-of-function, TTR amyloid), where a toxic species is REMOVED; here a lost function must be RESTORED, so the corrective direction is UP. The clean and honest point of this entry is the LEAD approved drug: omaveloxolone is an Nrf2 (NFE2L2) activator that boosts the antioxidant/mitochondrial gene programme and improves cellular resilience to the oxidative stress that frataxin loss causes -- it is DOWNSTREAM and does NOT restore frataxin (the same Rett/trofinetide discipline: an approved, corrective-direction, symptomatic agent that does not touch the causal switch). The SWITCH-LEVEL lever is to REPLACE frataxin -- frataxin-restoring AAV gene therapy and frataxin protein/mRNA approaches are investigational. Dimethyl fumarate (an approved Nrf2-activating drug in other diseases) is recorded as a downstream, repurposing candidate, not a switch lever. The gamma read is of the FXN promoter switch STRUCTURE; the causal lesion is the intron-1 GAA repeat expansion (a structural/epigenetic lesion), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
friedreich_ataxia.emergent_axis: mitochondrial Fe-S cluster biogenesis / oxidative-phosphorylation capacity (cerebellar, sensory-neuron and cardiomyocyte bioenergetics) -- a deficiency axis

causal_genes.note: FXN encodes frataxin, a mitochondrial iron-binding protein that ACCELERATES iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis by binding/activating the NFS1-ISCU-ISD11(LYRM4) cysteine-desulfurase complex and donating iron. It is the rate-enhancer (accelerator) of Fe-S assembly; its loss removes that drive -> Fe-S enzymes and respiratory-chain function are under-driven -> the bioenergetic axis falls (axis DOWN). Located 9q21.11 (OMIM 606829). NCBI official symbol FXN. Autosomal recessive. The disease allele is an intron-1 GAA triplet-repeat expansion that silences transcription (heterochromatinisation); a minority carry a coding/point LOF allele on one chromosome. The repeat/epigenetic lesion is outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Campuzano 1996 Science 271:1423 (FXN GAA expansion identifies Friedreich ataxia); Tsai 2010 Biochemistry 49:9132 (frataxin activates the NFS1 cysteine-desulfurase / accelerates Fe-S assembly)

context_genes.note: NFE2L2 encodes NRF2, the master transcription factor of the antioxidant-response (ARE) and mitochondrial gene programme. NRF2 signalling is paradoxically LOW in Friedreich-ataxia cells, worsening oxidative stress; pharmacologically ACTIVATING NRF2 (blocking its KEAP1-dependent degradation) raises antioxidant/mitochondrial capacity -- the DOWNSTREAM corrective node that omaveloxolone targets. It does not restore frataxin.
context_genes.src: Paupe 2009 PLoS One 4:e4253 (impaired NRF2 in Friedreich ataxia); Abeti 2018 (Nrf2 induction protects FRDA neurons)

congenital_leptin_deficiency.summary: A very rare autosomal-recessive cause of severe early-onset obesity. Leptin (LEP) is the adipocyte-secreted satiety hormone that signals the body's energy/fat state to the hypothalamus, where it ACCELERATES the satiety and energy-expenditure programme (via LEPR -> POMC -> alpha-MSH -> MC4R). Biallelic LEP loss-of-function (homozygous frameshift/missense or bioinactive-leptin alleles) removes that drive -> hypothalamic satiety signalling is UNDER-driven -> the emergent hormone axis falls, producing intense hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity (with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and immune/metabolic disturbance). Because the axis is driven DOWN, the corrective direction is UP, and the switch the kit re-derives is to REPLACE the missing hormone: recombinant human leptin (metreleptin) restores the satiety signal and reverses the hyperphagia, adiposity and neuroendocrine abnormalities -- the seminal demonstration (Farooqi 1999) that exogenous leptin dramatically reduced food intake in a leptin-deficient child is the direct confirmation of the deficiency-axis read. This is the EXACT CONTRAST PARTNER to X-linked hypophosphataemia in the kit: XLH is a HORMONE axis driven UP (FGF23 over-produced) corrected by RESTRAINING the excess hormone (burosumab), whereas congenital leptin deficiency is a HORMONE axis driven DOWN corrected by REPLACING the deficient hormone (metreleptin) -- the same hormone-axis logic read on opposite signs. The downstream MC4R-pathway agonist setmelanotide is the established therapy for the RECEPTOR-deficient sibling genotypes (LEPR deficiency, and POMC / PCSK1 deficiency), where the ligand is present but its signal is not transduced; it is NOT the lever for LEP-LIGAND deficiency itself (where replacing leptin restores the upstream signal) -- named as a distinct boundary, not folded in. The gamma read is of the LEP promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding (e.g. p.Arg105Trp; the original homozygous frameshift), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
congenital_leptin_deficiency.emergent_axis: leptin (adipostat satiety hormone) signalling tone -- the hypothalamic energy-balance set-point; a hormone axis

causal_genes.note: LEP encodes leptin, the adipocyte-derived type-I-cytokine satiety hormone that signals energy/fat sufficiency to the hypothalamus and ACCELERATES the satiety / energy-expenditure programme (LEPR on POMC neurons -> alpha-MSH -> MC4R). Biallelic LOF (null / frameshift, or a bioinactive-leptin allele) removes the drive -> hypothalamic satiety signalling is under-driven -> the hormone axis falls (axis DOWN), giving hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity. Located 7q32.1 (OMIM 164160). NCBI official symbol LEP. Autosomal recessive. Coding lesions (the original homozygous frameshift; p.Arg105Trp; bioinactive p.Asn103Lys); promoter firewall respected.

hereditary_haemochromatosis_type_1.summary: A single-gene HFE loss-of-function. HFE is required for iron-sensing hepatocytes to induce hepcidin (HAMP), the master peptide BRAKE on iron entry to plasma -- hepcidin degrades ferroportin, the iron exporter on enterocytes and macrophages. With HFE LOF (classically homozygous p.Cys282Tyr / C282Y), hepcidin is inappropriately LOW for the body's iron load -> ferroportin is not restrained -> dietary iron absorption and macrophage iron release run unchecked -> iron ACCUMULATES in liver, heart, pancreas, joints, pituitary and skin -> the iron burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on iron accumulation (HFE -> hepcidin brakes iron entry; LOF releases it -> iron UP) -- the released-brake -> over-accumulation convention (tyrosinaemia / porphyria / OTC / FCS) carried onto a NEW metal-ion metabolite, IRON, and the EXACT CONTRAST to Wilson disease (copper accumulation via the ATP7B export brake): a second toxic-metal overload, but on a different metal and a different brake. The kit re-derives the corrective direction, which REMOVES iron rather than restoring HFE: therapeutic phlebotomy (venesection) is the established first-line and bleeds off the iron burden directly; iron chelation (deferoxamine / deferasirox / deferiprone) removes iron pharmacologically where phlebotomy is not tolerated; and the SWITCH-LEVEL lever RESTORES the released brake -- hepcidin replacement / hepcidin-mimetic (mini-hepcidin) agents are investigational. The contrast to Wilson is also in MODALITY: Wilson's lead corrective is a chelating DRUG, this one's lead corrective is a physical REMOVAL (phlebotomy). The gamma read is of the HFE locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding (C282Y; H63D), outside the promoter firewall. Non-HFE hereditary iron-overload genes (HJV / HAMP / TFR2 juvenile and type-2/3 forms, SLC40A1 ferroportin disease) are distinct loci outside this HFE read. Magnitude [O].
hereditary_haemochromatosis_type_1.emergent_axis: systemic iron burden (hepatic / cardiac / endocrine parenchymal iron accumulation) -- a metal-ion metabolite axis; the iron contrast to Wilson's copper

causal_genes.note: HFE (high-Fe) is an MHC-class-I-like protein that, with transferrin receptors, lets hepatocytes sense iron and INDUCE hepcidin (HAMP) -- hepcidin is the master BRAKE on iron entry to plasma (it degrades the exporter ferroportin). HFE LOF blunts hepcidin induction -> the brake is RELEASED -> ferroportin runs unchecked -> dietary iron absorption and macrophage iron release rise -> systemic iron ACCUMULATES (toxic parenchymal overload). The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the IRON BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it. 6p22.2 (OMIM 613609). NCBI official symbol HFE. Autosomal recessive; incomplete penetrance. Coding lesions (C282Y; H63D).

context_genes.note: HAMP encodes hepcidin, the effector BRAKE peptide HFE induces; hepcidin internalises/degrades ferroportin to restrain iron entry. Restoring/mimicking hepcidin (mini-hepcidins) is the switch-level corrective; biallelic HAMP LOF is the severe juvenile haemochromatosis (type 2B).

context_genes.note: SLC40A1 encodes ferroportin, the cellular iron EXPORTER hepcidin restrains. Loss-of-restraint / gain-of-function ferroportin gives a distinct iron-overload (ferroportin disease, type 4) -- frames the axis but is not the HFE lesion.

leptin_receptor_deficiency.summary: An autosomal-recessive cause of severe early-onset obesity -- the RECEPTOR-side partner of congenital leptin deficiency. LEPR encodes the leptin receptor on hypothalamic POMC / AgRP neurons; it TRANSDUCES the leptin satiety signal that ACCELERATES the satiety / energy-expenditure programme (LEPR -> JAK2/STAT3 -> POMC -> alpha-MSH -> MC4R). Biallelic LEPR loss-of-function leaves the receptor unable to transduce leptin -> the satiety drive is lost DESPITE high (often markedly elevated) circulating leptin -> the emergent hormone-signalling axis falls -> intense hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity (with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism). Because the axis is driven DOWN the corrective direction is UP -- but the KEY CONTRAST to congenital leptin deficiency is that REPLACING THE LIGAND DOES NOT WORK: leptin is already present, so metreleptin cannot rescue a broken receptor. Instead the kit re-derives a DOWNSTREAM BYPASS -- the melanocortin-4-receptor (MC4R) agonist setmelanotide drives the node BELOW the missing receptor, restoring the satiety signal the broken receptor failed to transduce; setmelanotide is FDA-approved (2020) and EMA-approved (2021) for obesity due to LEPR deficiency (and POMC / PCSK1 deficiency), re-deriving the receptor-bypass lever as the approved lead. This is the EXACT CONTRAST PARTNER to congenital leptin deficiency on the SAME satiety cascade: LEP-ligand deficiency -> REPLACE the ligand (metreleptin); LEPR-receptor deficiency -> BYPASS the receptor downstream (setmelanotide) -- a clean ligand-replace vs receptor-bypass pair, the boundary the congenital-leptin-deficiency entry already named, now resolved on its own DNA. The switch-level corrective (restore LEPR itself) is investigational. Leptin replacement is deliberately NOT listed as a lever here (ligand present, receptor broken). The gamma read is of the LEPR promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. the original homozygous splice allele; truncating variants), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
leptin_receptor_deficiency.emergent_axis: leptin-receptor satiety-signalling tone (the hypothalamic energy-balance set-point transduced from leptin) -- a hormone-signalling axis; the receptor-side partner of LEP-ligand deficiency

causal_genes.note: LEPR encodes the leptin receptor (a type-I cytokine receptor) on hypothalamic POMC / AgRP neurons that TRANSDUCES the leptin signal accelerating the satiety / energy-expenditure programme (JAK2 / STAT3 -> POMC -> alpha-MSH -> MC4R). It is a signal-transducing ACCELERATOR of satiety; biallelic LOF leaves leptin unable to signal (despite high circulating leptin) -> the satiety drive is under-driven -> the hormone-signalling axis falls (axis DOWN), giving hyperphagia and severe early-onset obesity. 1p31.3 (OMIM 601007). NCBI official symbol LEPR. Autosomal recessive. Coding/splice lesions; promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Clement 1998 Nature 392:398 (LEPR mutation -> morbid obesity); Farooqi 2007 NEJM 356:237 (clinical spectrum of LEPR deficiency)

context_genes.note: LEP encodes leptin, the ligand. In LEPR deficiency the ligand is PRESENT / elevated (the contrast to congenital leptin deficiency, where leptin is absent and replaceable), so leptin replacement cannot rescue the broken receptor -- the boundary that distinguishes ligand-replace from receptor-bypass.
context_genes.src: Montague 1997 Nature 387:903 (LEP-ligand deficiency, the contrast genotype)

context_genes.note: MC4R is the hypothalamic melanocortin-4 receptor at the bottom of the satiety cascade -- the node BELOW the leptin receptor that the bypass agonist (setmelanotide) drives directly, restoring the signal the broken receptor failed to transduce.
context_genes.src: Huvenne 2016 (monogenic obesity of the leptin-melanocortin pathway)

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of hyperphagia / adiposity normalisation not derived from sequence; downstream bypass of the receptor defect

falsifiers.measurable_by: change in hunger score and body weight on setmelanotide in LEPR deficiency (the Clement 2020 design)

aadc_deficiency.summary: An autosomal-recessive neurometabolic disorder of monoamine-neurotransmitter synthesis. DDC encodes aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC), the enzyme that decarboxylates L-DOPA -> dopamine and 5-hydroxytryptophan -> serotonin, shared by the catecholamine and serotonin pathways. DDC loss-of-function collapses synthesis of dopamine, noradrenaline, adrenaline and serotonin -> the monoamine-neurotransmitter axis falls -> a severe infantile-onset disorder (developmental delay, truncal hypotonia with limb hypertonia, oculogyric crises, autonomic dysfunction, movement disorder). Read as enzyme LOF -> pathway throughput DOWN (substrate L-DOPA / 3-O-methyldopa accumulates while the products fail) -> axis DOWN: a DEFICIENCY-driven neurodevelopmental / neurodegeneration. The honest CONTRAST to Friedreich ataxia is the LEAD lever: in FRDA the approved lead is downstream-only (omaveloxolone, which does not restore frataxin), whereas HERE the approved lead is the SWITCH-LEVEL gene restore -- eladocagene exuparvovec, an AAV2 vector carrying the DDC gene delivered into the putamen, restores AADC enzyme and dopamine synthesis; it is FDA-approved (Kebilidi, Nov 2024 -- the first US gene therapy administered directly into the brain) and EMA-approved (Upstaza, 2022). So this is the gene-restore-IS-the-lead read (like RPE65 / LCA2's voretigene) on a neurometabolic axis -- the deficiency-driven neurodegeneration in which restoring the gene IS the approved lead, the precise complement to FRDA's downstream-only lead. Downstream / supportive agents -- pyridoxal-5'-phosphate / vitamin B6 (the AADC cofactor; helps cofactor-responsive residual-activity alleles but does NOT restore a null enzyme), dopamine agonists and MAO-B inhibitors -- are recorded as downstream-symptomatic, partial NON-switch management, not the lead. The gamma read is of the DDC promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. the founder IVS6+4A>T splice allele common in East Asia; p.Gly102Ser), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
aadc_deficiency.emergent_axis: monoamine-neurotransmitter synthesis throughput (dopamine / noradrenaline / adrenaline / serotonin) -- a neurotransmitter-biosynthesis axis; a deficiency-driven neurodegeneration

causal_genes.note: DDC encodes aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC), the pyridoxal-5'-phosphate-dependent decarboxylase producing dopamine (from L-DOPA) and serotonin (from 5-HTP) -- the shared final enzyme of catecholamine and serotonin biosynthesis. LOF lowers throughput of BOTH monoamine pathways (substrate L-DOPA / 3-O-methyldopa accumulates; products fail) -> the neurotransmitter-synthesis axis falls (axis DOWN). 7p12.2 (OMIM 107930). NCBI official symbol DDC. Autosomal recessive. Coding/splice lesions (the East-Asian founder IVS6+4A>T splice allele; p.Gly102Ser); promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Hyland 1992 (AADC deficiency identified); Brun 2010 Neurology 75:64 (clinical and biochemical spectrum of AADC deficiency)

context_genes.note: TH encodes tyrosine hydroxylase, the upstream rate-limiting step making L-DOPA (the AADC substrate); TH deficiency is a related but distinct dopa-responsive monoamine-deficiency, upstream of the AADC step.

GCH1 (GTP cyclohydrolase 1) heads tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) synthesis; BH4 is the cofactor for TH (and PAH), so BH4-synthesis defects give a separate upstream monoamine-deficiency class -- frames the pathway but is not the AADC lesion.

therapeutic_axes.push: deliver a working DDC copy to putaminal neurons -> restore AADC enzyme -> restore dopamine (and monoamine) synthesis -> raise the deficient axis toward normal (axis UP). The switch-level corrective: it restores the deficient gene itself, and here it is the APPROVED lead (the Friedreich-ataxia contrast, where the approved lead is downstream-only)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] restored-enzyme level / dopamine-synthesis recovery not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Tai 2022 Mol Ther 30:509 (eladocagene exuparvovec long-term outcomes); Upstaza (EMA 2022) / Kebilidi (FDA Nov 2024) -- first US gene therapy administered directly into the brain, for AADC deficiency

DOWNSTREAM and symptomatic -- does NOT restore a null enzyme or correct the DDC switch

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] downstream / partial compensation not derived from sequence; symptomatic, not the switch lever
