falsifiers.falsifier: a DDC LOF genotype that RAISED CSF dopamine / serotonin end-metabolites (HVA / 5-HIAA), or AADC restoration that LOWERED them, refutes the deficiency (axis-DOWN) direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: CSF homovanillic acid (HVA), 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) and 3-O-methyldopa, with plasma AADC enzyme activity, stratified by DDC genotype

falsifiers.measurable_by: dopamine-synthesis (F-DOPA) PET, CSF HVA, and gross-motor-milestone change after AAV2-hAADC (the eladocagene-exuparvovec trial design)

cystinosis.summary: A single-gene CTNS loss-of-function removes cystinosin, the proton-driven lysosomal-membrane transporter that EXPORTS cystine out of the lysosome to the cytosol. Cystinosin is the BRAKE on intra-lysosomal cystine accumulation; with CTNS LOF the brake is released, free cystine accumulates inside lysosomes, crystallises, and damages cells (renal proximal-tubule Fanconi first, then a multi-organ course) -> the intra-lysosomal cystine burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on toxic accumulation (cystinosin clears lysosomal cystine; LOF releases the clearance -> cystine UP) -- the released-brake -> over-accumulation convention (tyrosinaemia / porphyria / OTC / FCS / haemochromatosis) carried onto a lysosomal-storage axis, but with a DISTINCT lysosomal-storage MECHANISM and lever class. Unlike the four enzyme-deficiency lysosomal-storage reads (Gaucher / Fabry / Pompe / -- where catabolic throughput is restored by REPLACING the enzyme), here the defect is TRANSPORT, not catabolism, so the kit re-derives a SMALL-MOLECULE SUBSTRATE-DEPLETER as the lead lever: cysteamine enters the lysosome and reacts with the stored cystine to form cysteine plus a cysteine-cysteamine mixed disulfide, both of which exit through transporters left intact by the CTNS lesion -- the stored substrate is depleted in situ WITHOUT restoring cystinosin (an upstream/in-situ RESTRAINT on the burden, NOT enzyme replacement). The FIFTH lysosomal-storage read and the FIRST whose lead lever is a small-molecule substrate-depleter rather than enzyme replacement -- a new lysosomal lever class. The switch-level lever RESTORES cystinosin (autologous haematopoietic-stem-cell CTNS gene therapy, investigational; net axis effect lowers the burden -> restrain-coded, the OTC/haemochromatosis convention). The gamma read is of the CTNS locus switch STRUCTURE (a GC-rich promoter, one of the higher gamma in the kit); the disease lesion is coding/structural (the common 57-kb founder deletion; truncating/missense alleles), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
cystinosis.emergent_axis: intra-lysosomal free-cystine burden (lysosomal cystine accumulation / crystallisation) -- a transport-defect lysosomal-storage axis, distinct from the enzyme-deficiency storage reads

causal_genes.note: CTNS encodes cystinosin, the H+-driven lysosomal cystine EXPORTER that moves free cystine out of the lysosome. As the BRAKE on intra-lysosomal cystine accumulation, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> cystine accumulates inside lysosomes and crystallises (toxic storage). The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding/deletion lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the LYSOSOMAL CYSTINE BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it. 17p13.2 (OMIM 606272). NCBI official symbol CTNS. Autosomal recessive. Coding/structural lesions (the 57-kb founder deletion; truncating/missense alleles).
causal_genes.src: Town 1998 Nat Genet 18:319 (CTNS identified; 57-kb deletion); Kalatzis 2001 EMBO J 20:5940 (cystinosin is the lysosomal cystine transporter)

therapeutic_axes.push: deplete the stored lysosomal cystine in situ -- cysteamine reacts with cystine to form cysteine + a cysteine-cysteamine mixed disulfide that exit via intact transporters -> lower the intra-lysosomal cystine burden (bypasses the cystinosin defect); the established lead
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] cystine-depletion magnitude / organ outcome not derived from sequence
therapeutic_axes.src: Thoene 1976 J Clin Invest 58:180 (cysteamine depletes cystinotic cystine); Markello 1993 NEJM 328:1157 (cysteamine slows renal decline); cysteamine bitartrate (Cystagon) FDA 1994 / delayed-release (Procysbi) FDA 2013

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] degree/durability of restored cystinosin transport not derived from sequence

alkaptonuria.summary: A single-gene HGD loss-of-function removes homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase, the tyrosine-catabolism enzyme that ring-cleaves homogentisic acid (HGA). HGD normally consumes (clears) HGA; without it HGA ACCUMULATES, is excreted (urine darkening on standing) and, over decades, polymerises and deposits as ochronotic pigment in cartilage/connective tissue -> a destructive arthropathy with cardiac-valve and other involvement -> the HGA burden is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on toxic accumulation (HGD clears HGA; LOF releases it -> HGA UP). HGD sits in the SAME tyrosine-catabolism pathway as FAH (tyrosinaemia type 1), one step downstream of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPD) and upstream of FAH. The kit re-derives the SAME counter-intuitive upstream lever already shipped for tyrosinaemia: nitisinone inhibits the UPSTREAM enzyme HPD so HGA is never formed (an upstream RESTRAINT), rather than restoring HGD -- a clean 'ONE upstream-block lever (restrain HPD / nitisinone), TWO diseases (tyrosinaemia type 1 AND alkaptonuria)' demonstration, because HPD lies upstream of BOTH the HGD lesion (alkaptonuria) and the FAH lesion (tyrosinaemia). The switch-level lever RESTORES HGD (gene/enzyme restoration, investigational; net axis effect lowers the burden -> restrain-coded, the tyrosinaemia convention). Dietary tyrosine/phenylalanine restriction is recorded as adjunct. The gamma read is of the HGD locus switch STRUCTURE (an AT-leaning promoter); the disease lesion is coding (e.g. p.Met368Val and other missense), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
alkaptonuria.emergent_axis: toxic homogentisic-acid burden (HGA accumulation -> ochronotic-pigment deposition) -- the tyrosine-catabolism axis shared with tyrosinaemia, one enzymatic step downstream

causal_genes.note: HGD (homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase) ring-cleaves homogentisic acid in tyrosine catabolism; it consumes HGA. As a BRAKE on HGA accumulation, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> HGA accumulates and polymerises into ochronotic pigment (toxic). The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the HGA BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective levers LOWER it. 3q13.33 (OMIM 607474). NCBI official symbol HGD. Autosomal recessive. Coding lesions (e.g. p.Met368Val).
causal_genes.src: Fernandez-Canon 1996 Nat Genet 14:19 (HGO/HGD is the alkaptonuria gene); La Du 1958 J Biol Chem 230:251 (HGD enzyme defect in alkaptonuria)

context_genes.note: HPD (4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase) acts UPSTREAM of HGD, forming homogentisate; blocking it shuts off the pathway before HGA is made -- the target of the approved upstream-restraint therapy (nitisinone). HPD is the SHARED upstream node: it lies above both the HGD lesion (alkaptonuria) and the FAH lesion (tyrosinaemia type 1), so one nitisinone lever serves both.

haemophilia_b.summary: An X-linked single-gene F9 loss-of-function lowers coagulation factor IX, a vitamin-K-dependent serine-protease zymogen that, once activated (FIXa), drives the intrinsic-tenase step of the coagulation cascade (FIXa with cofactor FVIIIa activates factor X). With F9 LOF the procoagulant DRIVE is lost, thrombin/fibrin generation is under-driven, and haemostasis fails -> spontaneous and trauma-related bleeding (haemarthroses, soft-tissue and other bleeds), severity tracking residual factor IX level -> the coagulation-cascade axis is driven DOWN. Read as a lost ACCELERATOR of the coagulation cascade (factor IX drives clot formation; LOF -> under-driven haemostasis), the deficiency-driven DOWN shape -- but on a NEW physiological axis, the coagulation cascade, not previously represented in the kit. Correction RESTORES factor IX. The kit re-derives the gene-restore lead: etranacogene dezaparvovec, a liver-directed AAV5 F9-Padua gene-transfer therapy (the first approved haemophilia B gene therapy), restoring endogenous factor IX -- gene-restore-as-lead on haemostasis, extending the clean gene-restore reads (RPE65/LCA2, DDC/AADC) onto the clotting axis. The long-standing established replace arm is factor IX protein replacement (recombinant / plasma-derived factor IX, including extended-half-life fusions), also direction-consistent (replace the missing factor). The gamma read is of the F9 locus switch STRUCTURE (an AT-rich promoter, among the lowest gamma in the kit, consistent with its X-linked locus); the disease lesion is coding/regulatory (missense/nonsense; the distinct F9-promoter 'haemophilia B Leyden' androgen-responsive regulatory variants that remit at puberty are a SEPARATE class, noted not modelled), outside the structural promoter-window read. X-linked, so penetrance/severity are zygosity-dependent (males hemizygous; carrier females variable by X-inactivation) and held [O]. Magnitude [O].
haemophilia_b.emergent_axis: coagulation-cascade output (factor-IX-driven intrinsic-tenase / thrombin-fibrin generation) -- a new haemostasis axis, the kit's first coagulation read

causal_genes.note: F9 encodes coagulation factor IX, a vitamin-K-dependent serine-protease zymogen; activated FIXa is a positive DRIVER of the coagulation cascade (with FVIIIa it activates factor X). As an ACCELERATOR of clot formation, its LOF LOSES the drive -> thrombin/fibrin generation under-driven -> bleeding. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the COAGULATION OUTPUT (it goes DOWN), so the corrective levers RAISE it. Xq27.1 (OMIM 300746). NCBI official symbol F9. X-linked recessive. Coding/nonsense lesions; the 'haemophilia B Leyden' F9-promoter variants are a separate regulatory class (noted, not modelled).

menkes_disease.summary: An X-linked single-gene ATP7A loss-of-function disables the copper-transporting P-type ATPase that drives dietary copper OUT of enterocytes into the portal blood, transports copper across the blood-brain barrier, and delivers copper to the secretory pathway for cuproenzymes. Without it, absorbed copper is trapped in the gut mucosa and cannot reach the body and brain, so SYSTEMIC and CNS copper is DEFICIENT and copper-dependent enzymes (lysyl oxidase, dopamine-beta-hydroxylase, cytochrome-c oxidase) fail -> connective-tissue, vascular and severe neurodegenerative disease (the axis -- systemic/CNS copper delivery -- is driven DOWN). Read as a lost ACCELERATOR of systemic copper delivery (ATP7A DRIVES copper into the body; LOF -> drive lost -> copper delivery under-driven), the deficiency-driven DOWN shape. This is the EXACT CONTRAST to Wilson disease, the sibling copper ATPase ATP7B: Wilson is copper axis UP (released brake -> toxic copper accumulation -> RESTRAIN/chelate), Menkes is copper axis DOWN (lost accelerator -> copper deficiency -> REPLACE) -- the SAME metal, the OPPOSITE sign AND the OPPOSITE lever (replace vs chelate). The kit re-derives the corrective direction, which SUPPLIES copper downstream of the broken transporter rather than restoring it: parenteral copper-histidine (copper histidinate) delivers copper directly into the blood, bypassing the intestinal ATP7A defect. HONEST status caveat: copper-histidine is a long-standing clinical / orphan therapy (used since Sarkar's work in the 1970s-80s), NOT a conventional small-molecule regulatory approval, and its benefit is partial and genotype-dependent -- it helps mainly when started very early and where residual transporter or accessible CNS delivery remains (the blood-brain-barrier ATP7A defect limits CNS rescue); efficacy is held [O]. Restoring ATP7A itself (gene / transporter therapy) is investigational. The gamma read is of the ATP7A locus switch STRUCTURE (an AT-leaning promoter, beside its Wilson sibling ATP7B); the disease lesion is coding/structural (missense / splice / deletion), outside the promoter firewall. X-linked, so penetrance/severity are zygosity-dependent and held [O]. Magnitude [O].
menkes_disease.emergent_axis: systemic and CNS copper delivery (intestinal copper efflux into the body + blood-brain-barrier transport feeding the cuproenzymes) -- the copper-DEFICIENCY contrast to Wilson's copper-accumulation axis

causal_genes.note: ATP7A is a copper-transporting P-type ATPase that drives dietary copper out of enterocytes into the portal circulation, transports copper across the blood-brain barrier, and delivers copper to the trans-Golgi secretory pathway for cuproenzyme loading. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is COPPER DELIVERY (it goes DOWN), so the corrective levers RAISE it. Xq21.1 (OMIM 300011). NCBI official symbol ATP7A. The sibling efflux ATPase ATP7B (Wilson) brakes copper accumulation -> the exact opposite-sign copper disease.
causal_genes.src: Vulpe 1993 Nat Genet 3:7; Chelly 1993 Nat Genet 3:14; Mercer 1993 Nat Genet 3:20 (ATP7A / Menkes cloned)

sod1_amyotrophic_lateral_sclerosis.summary: A single-gene SOD1 TOXIC gain-of-function form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: dominant SOD1 variants (e.g. Ala5Val / A4V, Gly94Ala / G93A, Asp91Ala / D90A) do NOT act mainly by losing dismutase activity but by conferring a toxic misfolding/aggregation GAIN that progressively kills motor neurons, suppressing motor-neuron survival and function -> progressive paralysis (the motor-neuron-function axis is driven DOWN). Read with the proteinopathy framing already used for Huntington (HTT) and transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR): the toxic GAIN is an over-active pathological BRAKE on motor-neuron function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), and the kit re-derives the approved therapy, which REMOVES the toxic species rather than treating symptoms -- tofersen, a SOD1 antisense oligonucleotide that lowers SOD1 mRNA/protein (FDA 2023 accelerated approval; the first genetically targeted ALS therapy). This extends the toxic-aggregate 'reduce the poison' pattern (HTT, TTR) onto MOTOR NEURONS, and sits as the toxic-GOF contrast to spinal muscular atrophy's structural-LOF on the SAME cell type (SMA: restore the missing SMN; SOD1-ALS: remove the toxic SOD1). The gamma read is of the SOD1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease-causing point mutations are coding changes outside the promoter firewall, and their toxicity is a protein-misfolding GAIN, not a transcriptional change. (Most ALS is sporadic and non-SOD1; the commonest familial cause is the C9orf72 repeat expansion -- a separate, non-promoter structural lesion outside this single-gene read. This entry is the SOD1 subtype only.) Magnitude [O].
sod1_amyotrophic_lateral_sclerosis.emergent_axis: motor-neuron survival and function (progressively suppressed by toxic misfolded-SOD1 aggregation) -- the motor-neuron toxic-GAIN contrast to SMA's motor-neuron loss-of-function

causal_genes.note: SOD1 encodes Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase 1. The ALS-causing variants act predominantly through a TOXIC gain-of-function: the mutant protein misfolds and aggregates, conferring motor-neuron toxicity (mitochondrial, proteostatic, prion-like propagation) rather than by loss of dismutase activity -- read here as an over-active pathological BRAKE that SUPPRESSES motor-neuron survival/function (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN), the same proteinopathy framing as Huntington and TTR. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the toxic coding lesion's magnitude (firewall). 21q22.11 (OMIM 147450). NCBI official symbol SOD1.
causal_genes.src: Rosen 1993 Nature 362:59 (SOD1 mutations in familial ALS); Gurney 1994 Science 264:1772 (toxic-GOF mouse); Bruijn 1998 Science 281:1851 (toxicity independent of dismutase activity)

A non-coding GGGGCC hexanucleotide repeat expansion in C9orf72 is the commonest familial ALS cause -- a structural/repeat lesion with no clean promoter-switch read, outside this single-gene SOD1 entry (a separate class; cf. the suspension rule).

haemophilia_a.summary: An X-linked single-gene F8 loss-of-function lowers coagulation factor VIII, the non-enzymatic COFACTOR that, once activated (FVIIIa), partners activated factor IX (FIXa) in the intrinsic tenase to activate factor X. Without functional factor VIII the intrinsic-tenase step is crippled, thrombin/fibrin generation is under-driven and haemostasis fails -> spontaneous and trauma-related bleeding (haemarthroses, soft-tissue and other bleeds), severity tracking residual factor VIII -> the coagulation-cascade axis is driven DOWN. This COMPLETES the coagulation A/B pair with haemophilia B (F9): the SAME haemostasis axis broken one component over -- F8 is the cofactor, F9 the protease of the same intrinsic-tenase step (so both are read as lost ACCELERATORS of the cascade -> axis DOWN). Read as a lost ACCELERATOR (factor VIII drives clot formation as FIXa's cofactor; LOF -> under-driven haemostasis), the deficiency-driven DOWN shape. The kit re-derives the corrective direction with a NEW LEVER CLASS not previously in the kit -- the cofactor MIMIC: emicizumab, a bispecific antibody that bridges FIXa and factor X, performing factor VIIIa's bridging FUNCTION WITHOUT being factor VIII (so it works even in people who have developed neutralising anti-FVIII inhibitors). This is distinct from 'replace' (supplying the same molecule) and from 'correct' (rescuing the native protein): the corrective molecule is a DIFFERENT entity doing the missing element's job. The established direction-consistent arms are also re-derived: factor VIII protein replacement (recombinant / plasma-derived, including extended-half-life fusions) and valoctocogene roxaparvovec, an AAV F8 gene-transfer therapy that restores endogenous factor VIII (the first approved haemophilia A gene therapy). The gamma read is of the F8 locus switch STRUCTURE (an AT-leaning Xq28 promoter, sitting above its haemophilia-B partner F9 in gamma); the disease lesion is coding/structural -- most commonly the intron-22 inversion that disrupts the F8 ORF, plus missense/nonsense -- outside the structural promoter-window read. X-linked, so penetrance/severity are zygosity-dependent (males hemizygous; carrier females variable by X-inactivation) and held [O]. Magnitude [O].
haemophilia_a.emergent_axis: coagulation-cascade output (factor-VIIIa-cofactored intrinsic-tenase / thrombin-fibrin generation) -- the same haemostasis axis as haemophilia B, broken at the cofactor instead of the protease

causal_genes.note: F8 encodes coagulation factor VIII, a large non-enzymatic cofactor; activated FVIIIa is a positive DRIVER of the coagulation cascade -- it is the obligatory cofactor for FIXa in the intrinsic tenase that activates factor X. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the COAGULATION OUTPUT (it goes DOWN), so the corrective levers RAISE it. Xq28 (OMIM 300841). NCBI official symbol F8. X-linked recessive. The commonest severe lesion is the intron-22 inversion (plus intron-1 inversion, missense, nonsense), all outside the promoter window.

lysosomal_acid_lipase_deficiency.disease: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency (Wolman disease / cholesteryl ester storage disease)
lysosomal_acid_lipase_deficiency.summary: A single-gene LIPA loss-of-function. Lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) is the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses the cholesteryl esters and triglycerides delivered to the lysosome by receptor-mediated LDL endocytosis, releasing free cholesterol and free fatty acids. LIPA LOF lowers that lysosomal lipid-catabolism throughput, so cholesteryl esters and triglycerides ACCUMULATE in the lysosomes of hepatocytes, macrophages, adrenal cortex and intestinal mucosa -> hepatomegaly with micro/macrovesicular steatosis and fibrosis, dyslipidaemia (raised LDL-cholesterol, low HDL) and accelerated atherosclerosis. The disease is a clinical continuum: near-complete LAL loss gives the fulminant infantile Wolman phenotype (hepatosplenomegaly, malabsorption, adrenal calcification, early death), while residual activity gives the later-onset cholesteryl ester storage disease (CESD). The catabolic-throughput axis is driven DOWN; the correction is to restore enzymatic throughput. Read on the SAME deficient-enzyme / substrate-accumulation level axis as Gaucher, Fabry and Pompe -- but on a LIPID (cholesteryl-ester + triglyceride) substrate, the SIXTH lysosomal-storage read and the FIRST whose stored substrate is a neutral lipid handled by enzyme replacement (the contrast to cystinosis on the same organelle, whose lesion is a cystine TRANSPORT defect corrected by a small-molecule depleter rather than by replacing an enzyme). The kit re-derives the approved throughput-restore arm -- replace LAL via recombinant human lysosomal acid lipase (sebelipase alfa). Lipid-lowering agents (statins / ezetimibe) lower the circulating LDL-cholesterol burden but do NOT restore the lysosomal enzyme and are recorded as downstream-symptomatic NON-levers (the XLH/Rett downstream-agent discipline). The gamma read is of the LIPA locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/splice (notably the common exon-8 splice-junction E8SJM c.894G>A allele of CESD, and null alleles in Wolman), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
lysosomal_acid_lipase_deficiency.emergent_axis: lysosomal neutral-lipid catabolism (lysosomal acid lipase / LIPA throughput on cholesteryl esters + triglycerides)

causal_genes.note: LIPA encodes lysosomal acid lipase (LAL / acid cholesteryl ester hydrolase), the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses cholesteryl esters and triglycerides arriving via LDL endocytosis, liberating free cholesterol and fatty acids. LOF lowers lysosomal neutral-lipid catabolism -> cholesteryl esters and triglycerides accumulate in lysosomes of liver, macrophages, adrenal and gut. Autosomal recessive (10q23.31). NCBI official symbol LIPA. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice lesions (e.g. the CESD exon-8 splice-site c.894G>A; Wolman null alleles) are outside the promoter firewall.

cryopyrin_associated_periodic_syndrome.disease: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS / NLRP3-associated autoinflammatory disease)
cryopyrin_associated_periodic_syndrome.summary: A single-gene NLRP3 gain-of-function. NLRP3 (cryopyrin) is the sensor that nucleates the NLRP3 inflammasome; on activation it recruits the adaptor ASC and pro-caspase-1, and active caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1beta (and pro-IL-18) to their mature, secreted forms. GOF missense alleles render the inflammasome CONSTITUTIVELY / hyper-active (lowering its activation threshold), so IL-1beta is OVER-produced even without a normal trigger -> the IL-1beta inflammatory drive is pushed UP, giving the CAPS spectrum: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome (FCAS, cold-induced urticarial rash/fever), Muckle-Wells syndrome (urticaria, sensorineural hearing loss, AA amyloidosis) and the severe neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID / CINCA, chronic meningitis, arthropathy, developmental impairment). This is read as a NEW kind of emergent axis for the kit -- an INFLAMMASOME / autoinflammatory (IL-1beta cytokine-drive) axis -- driven UP by an over-active accelerator, so the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN it. The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: lower the over-produced signal by IL-1 blockade -- canakinumab (an anti-IL-1beta monoclonal antibody that neutralises the mature cytokine), with anakinra (recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist) and rilonacept (an IL-1 'trap' decoy receptor) as the established alternatives. Direct NLRP3-inflammasome inhibitors are an emerging upstream restrain direction (investigational). Recorded as an IL-1beta OVER-production axis -- the contrast to hereditary angioedema's bradykinin OVER-production: both are axis-UP released/over-driven mediator floods, but on a different mediator (IL-1beta vs bradykinin) with a different lever target (IL-1 blockade vs kallikrein-kinin restraint). The gamma read is of the NLRP3 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding (GOF missense in the NACHT domain, e.g. p.Arg260Trp, p.Asp303Asn / p.Asp305Asn region), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
cryopyrin_associated_periodic_syndrome.emergent_axis: NLRP3-inflammasome IL-1beta drive (caspase-1-processed IL-1beta over-production -> systemic autoinflammation) -- an inflammasome/cytokine axis

causal_genes.note: NLRP3 (cryopyrin; formerly CIAS1) encodes the pattern/danger sensor that nucleates the NLRP3 inflammasome; via ASC it activates caspase-1, which matures pro-IL-1beta to secreted IL-1beta -- the master driver of the autoinflammatory response. CAPS alleles are gain-of-function: they lower the inflammasome's activation threshold so it assembles and fires constitutively -> IL-1beta is over-produced -> the inflammatory drive is pushed UP. As an over-driven ACCELERATOR of IL-1beta output, the pathological axis goes UP and the corrective levers LOWER it. Autosomal dominant (often de novo / somatic mosaic), 1q44 (OMIM 606416). NCBI official symbol NLRP3. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the activating NACHT-domain missense lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Hoffman 2001 Nat Genet 29:301 (CIAS1/NLRP3 mutations cause FCAS and Muckle-Wells); Aksentijevich 2002 Arthritis Rheum 46:3340 (NOMID/CINCA); Agostini 2004 Immunity 20:319 (cryopyrin inflammasome activates caspase-1 / IL-1beta)

context_genes.note: IL1B encodes interleukin-1beta, the effector cytokine the over-active NLRP3 inflammasome over-produces and the proximate driver of the CAPS phenotype. It is the target of the approved lead restrain arm: canakinumab neutralises IL-1beta and rilonacept traps it (the IL-1-blockade mechanism).

CASP1 encodes caspase-1, the inflammasome protease that, once NLRP3/ASC assemble, cleaves pro-IL-1beta to its mature form -- the catalytic step between the over-active sensor and the over-produced cytokine. It frames the axis between NLRP3 and IL1B but is not the CAPS lesion.

sitosterolaemia.summary: A single-pathway disease caused by loss-of-function of either half of an obligate sterol-efflux pump. ABCG5 (sterolin-1) and ABCG8 (sterolin-2) form a heterodimeric ABC transporter that pumps absorbed plant sterols (sitosterol, campesterol) and excess cholesterol BACK out of the enterocyte into the gut lumen and out of the hepatocyte into bile -- the BRAKE that limits whole-body sterol retention. The two genes lie head-to-head at 2p21 sharing a bidirectional promoter, and biallelic LOF of EITHER subunit disables the shared pump, so dietary plant sterols and cholesterol are hyper-absorbed and under-excreted and ACCUMULATE -> the whole-body sterol load is driven UP, giving tendon/tuberous xanthomas, premature atherosclerosis and coronary disease, and stomatocytic haemolysis / macrothrombocytopenia from sterol-laden membranes. Read as a released BRAKE on sterol retention (ABCG5/ABCG8 efflux brakes it; LOF releases it -> sterols UP) -- the released-brake -> over-accumulation convention (tyrosinaemia / haemochromatosis / FCS) carried onto a NEW STEROL-ABSORPTION axis, and a TWO-CAUSAL-GENE read where both subunits perturb the same axis UP (the HCM convergence pattern; the deeper switch is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the targeted approved arm -- RESTRAIN the absorption axis with ezetimibe, which inhibits NPC1L1, the brush-border sterol-uptake transporter, cutting intestinal absorption of both plant sterols and cholesterol so the whole-body sterol load falls (ezetimibe is markedly effective in sitosterolaemia and is its mainstay). A low-plant-sterol diet and bile-acid sequestrants (cholestyramine, which interrupts enterohepatic sterol recycling) are adjuncts; statins are comparatively INEFFECTIVE here because the lesion is sterol ABSORPTION, not endogenous synthesis -- recorded as a downstream/poorly-matched NON-lever. This is the explicit CONTRAST to familial hypercholesterolaemia: FH is an LDL-cholesterol LEVEL axis (LDLR LOF / PCSK9 GOF, axis DOWN -> oppose PCSK9), whereas sitosterolaemia is a sterol-ABSORPTION axis (ABCG5/ABCG8 LOF, axis UP -> restrain absorption). The gamma reads are of the ABCG5 and ABCG8 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. ABCG8 p.Gly574Arg; ABCG5 truncations), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
sitosterolaemia.emergent_axis: whole-body sterol load (intestinal plant-sterol + cholesterol absorption / retention) -- a sterol-absorption axis; the absorption contrast to familial hypercholesterolaemia's LDL-cholesterol level axis

causal_genes.note: ABCG5 encodes sterolin-1, one half of the ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimeric sterol-efflux transporter that pumps plant sterols and excess cholesterol out of enterocytes (to the lumen) and hepatocytes (to bile) -- a BRAKE on whole-body sterol retention. Biallelic LOF disables the shared pump -> plant sterols and cholesterol are hyper-absorbed and under-excreted -> systemic sterol ACCUMULATION (axis UP). 2p21, head-to-head with ABCG8 on a shared bidirectional promoter (OMIM 605459). NCBI official symbol ABCG5. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Berge 2000 Science 290:1771 (ABCG5/ABCG8 mutations cause sitosterolaemia); Yu 2002 J Clin Invest 110:671 (ABCG5/G8 are the sterol-efflux brake)

causal_genes.note: ABCG8 encodes sterolin-2, the obligate partner subunit of the same sterol-efflux transporter; the functional pump is the ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimer, so biallelic LOF of ABCG8 disables sterol efflux just as ABCG5 loss does -> the same released-brake -> sterol over-accumulation (axis UP). 2p21, head-to-head with ABCG5 (OMIM 605460). NCBI official symbol ABCG8. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding/splice lesions (e.g. the recurrent p.Gly574Arg allele) are outside the promoter firewall.

context_genes.note: NPC1L1 (Niemann-Pick C1-like 1) is the brush-border transporter that mediates intestinal uptake of sterols (both cholesterol and plant sterols) -- the influx step UPSTREAM of the broken ABCG5/ABCG8 efflux brake. It is the target of the approved lead lever ezetimibe: inhibiting NPC1L1 cuts sterol absorption and so lowers the whole-body sterol load even though the efflux pump remains broken (the upstream-restraint logic).

It frames the explicit contrast (level vs absorption) but is not the sitosterolaemia lesion; statins act largely through LDLR upregulation, which is why they are poorly matched to the absorption defect here.

deficiency_of_il1_receptor_antagonist.disease: Deficiency of the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA)
deficiency_of_il1_receptor_antagonist.summary: A single-gene IL1RN loss-of-function. IL1RN encodes the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra), the secreted endogenous BRAKE on IL-1 signalling: it occupies the type-1 IL-1 receptor (IL1R1) without triggering it, competitively blocking IL-1alpha and IL-1beta. IL1RN LOF (null/truncating alleles) removes this brake, so IL-1alpha/IL-1beta signal UNOPPOSED -> the IL-1 signalling drive is pushed UP, giving neonatal-onset sterile multifocal osteomyelitis, periostitis and a pustular/ichthyosiform skin eruption (the DIRA / 'osteomyelitis, sterile multifocal, with periostitis and pustulosis' phenotype). This is read on the kit's inflammasome/autoinflammatory (IL-1) axis -- the SAME axis as CAPS but driven UP by a DIFFERENT lesion: CAPS is IL-1beta OVER-PRODUCTION (NLRP3-GOF over-active inflammasome), DIRA is LOSS OF THE IL-1 BRAKE (IL1RN-LOF). As a released brake the axis goes UP and the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN IL-1 signalling. The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: anakinra (recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist) -- which here literally SUPPLIES the missing IL-1Ra, restoring the lost brake at IL1R1; canakinumab (anti-IL-1beta mAb) and rilonacept (IL-1 trap) are established alternatives. Recorded as the ELEGANT 'one drug (anakinra), two opposite IL-1 lesions' pairing with CAPS: anakinra RESTRAINS over-produced IL-1 in CAPS but REPLACES the absent antagonist in DIRA -- the same IL-1 pathway, opposite lesion, both coded restrain by NET axis effect (lower the IL-1 drive). The Wilson/Menkes and CLD/LEPR pair logic (same axis, opposite lesion) carried onto the inflammasome axis. The gamma read is of the IL1RN locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/structural (null/truncating alleles, e.g. the founder genomic deletion at 2q14.1), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
deficiency_of_il1_receptor_antagonist.emergent_axis: IL-1 signalling drive (loss of the endogenous IL-1 receptor antagonist -> unopposed IL-1alpha/IL-1beta signalling at IL1R1 -> systemic autoinflammation) -- the inflammasome/IL-1 axis read as a released brake

causal_genes.note: IL1RN encodes the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra), the secreted competitive antagonist that binds the type-1 IL-1 receptor (IL1R1) without activating it -- the endogenous BRAKE that tunes down IL-1alpha/IL-1beta signalling. DIRA alleles are loss-of-function (null/truncating), removing the brake so IL-1 signals unopposed -> the IL-1 inflammatory drive is pushed UP. As a RELEASED BRAKE the pathological axis goes UP and the corrective levers LOWER it. Autosomal recessive, 2q14.1 (OMIM 147679). NCBI official symbol IL1RN. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the null/truncating coding/structural lesions (including the recurrent IL1RN genomic deletion) are outside the promoter firewall.

context_genes.note: IL1B encodes interleukin-1beta, one of the two IL-1 agonists whose signalling the missing IL-1Ra can no longer restrain (IL-1alpha is the other). It is the over-active effector in CAPS and, in DIRA, the unopposed driver; it frames the shared IL-1 axis linking the two diseases.

hereditary_antithrombin_deficiency.disease: Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (antithrombin III deficiency / thrombophilia type 7)
hereditary_antithrombin_deficiency.summary: A single-gene SERPINC1 loss-of-function. SERPINC1 encodes antithrombin (antithrombin III), the principal plasma serpin BRAKE on the coagulation cascade: it forms irreversible 1:1 complexes with thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa (and IXa/XIa), an inhibition massively accelerated by heparin/heparan-sulfate. SERPINC1 LOF lowers functional antithrombin (type I quantitative deficiency) or yields a dysfunctional molecule (type II qualitative: reactive-site, heparin-binding, or pleiotropic variants), so thrombin and factor Xa are under-restrained -> the coagulation drive is pushed UP, giving heritable thrombophilia: recurrent venous thromboembolism, often early-onset, and pregnancy-associated thrombosis (homozygous complete deficiency is essentially embryonic-lethal, consistent with antithrombin being an essential brake). This is read on the kit's coagulation axis -- the SAME axis as haemophilia but driven the OPPOSITE way: haemophilia is the coagulation axis DOWN (a missing pro-coagulant cofactor/protease -> BLEEDING), antithrombin deficiency is the coagulation axis UP (a missing ANTI-coagulant brake -> CLOTTING). As a released brake the axis goes UP and the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN coagulation. The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: antithrombin concentrate (plasma-derived, or recombinant antithrombin) -- which SUPPLIES the deficient serpin, restoring the brake on thrombin/factor Xa -- used for high-risk windows (surgery, delivery) on a background of therapeutic anticoagulation. Note the heparin caveat: heparin works by POTENTIATING antithrombin, so it is relatively less effective when antithrombin itself is deficient -- a reason the lead is to restore antithrombin and to use anticoagulants that act independently of it. Recorded as the THIRD serpin read in the kit -- after alpha-1-antitrypsin (SERPINA1, a protective-LEVEL axis DOWN: too little protease inhibitor) and hereditary angioedema (SERPING1/C1-INH, a bradykinin OVER-production axis UP) -- now completing the COAGULATION axis in BOTH directions (haemophilia DOWN vs antithrombin deficiency UP). The gamma read is of the SERPINC1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/structural (missense at the reactive site or heparin-binding domain, plus null alleles), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
hereditary_antithrombin_deficiency.emergent_axis: coagulation-cascade restraint (antithrombin / SERPINC1 inhibition of thrombin + factor Xa; LOF -> under-restrained coagulation -> hypercoagulability / thrombophilia) -- the coagulation axis read as a released brake

causal_genes.note: SERPINC1 encodes antithrombin (antithrombin III), the major plasma serpin that irreversibly inhibits thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa (also IXa/XIa) -- the principal endogenous BRAKE on coagulation, with its inhibitory rate hugely accelerated by heparin binding. Deficiency alleles are loss-of-function: type I (quantitative, reduced antithrombin) or type II (qualitative -- reactive-site, heparin-binding-site, or pleiotropic defects). Either way the brake on thrombin/Xa is weakened -> the coagulation drive is pushed UP -> thrombophilia. As a RELEASED BRAKE the pathological axis goes UP and the corrective levers LOWER it. Autosomal dominant for the heterozygous thrombophilia (homozygous quantitative deficiency is embryonic-lethal), 1q25.1 (OMIM 107300). NCBI official symbol SERPINC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the reactive-site/heparin-binding missense and null lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Egeberg 1965 Thromb Diath Haemorrh 13:516 (inherited antithrombin deficiency and thrombophilia); Olds 1994 Blood 84:1031 (SERPINC1 mutation spectrum); Bock 1982 (antithrombin III cDNA)

context_genes.note: F2 encodes prothrombin/thrombin (factor IIa), the central coagulation protease and the chief target antithrombin inactivates. It frames the restrained step: restoring antithrombin re-imposes the brake on thrombin. (F2 is also a thrombophilia locus in its own right via the G20210A prothrombin variant -- a DIFFERENT, gain-of-function thrombophilia mechanism -- but it is not the SERPINC1 lesion.)

F10 encodes factor X; activated factor Xa is the other major protease antithrombin inhibits (at the prothrombinase step). It frames the second restrained node and is the target of factor-Xa-directed anticoagulants used adjunctively, which act independently of antithrombin.

cerebrotendinous_xanthomatosis.summary: A single-gene CYP27A1 loss-of-function. CYP27A1 encodes sterol 27-hydroxylase, the mitochondrial enzyme that 27-hydroxylates sterol intermediates in the PRIMARY (classic and alternative) bile-acid synthesis pathway, a step required to make the primary bile acids chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) and cholic acid from cholesterol. CYP27A1 LOF lowers primary bile-acid synthesis THROUGHPUT, so (i) CDCA falls and (ii) -- because CDCA is the strongest feedback inhibitor of cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) -- that feedback is lost, DE-REPRESSING CYP7A1 and diverting flux down a 25-hydroxylation shunt that over-produces cholestanol and bile alcohols, which ACCUMULATE in brain, tendons (xanthomas), lens (juvenile cataracts) and arteries -> the CTX phenotype: infantile cholestasis/diarrhoea, juvenile cataracts, tendon xanthomas, and progressive adult neurodegeneration (ataxia, spasticity, cognitive decline). The emergent axis is PRIMARY BILE-ACID SYNTHESIS, driven DOWN by the deficient enzyme; the correction is to restore the missing end-product. The kit re-derives the approved replace arm: chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA; chenodiol) -- which SUPPLIES the deficient primary bile acid AND, by restoring feedback inhibition of CYP7A1, suppresses the abnormal cholestanol-producing flux (lowering plasma cholestanol and urinary bile alcohols). This is a NEW bile-acid-synthesis metabolic axis -- distinct from the kit's other lipid reads (familial hypercholesterolaemia's LDL-cholesterol LEVEL axis; sitosterolaemia's sterol-ABSORPTION axis; LAL deficiency's lysosomal neutral-lipid CATABOLISM axis) -- with an END-PRODUCT-REPLACEMENT lever (replace the missing bile acid, which also restores its own feedback). Statins / LDL apheresis lower the cholesterol substrate but do NOT restore bile-acid synthesis and are recorded as downstream-symptomatic NON-levers (the XLH/Rett downstream-agent discipline). The gamma read is of the CYP27A1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (missense/nonsense/splice across the gene), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
cerebrotendinous_xanthomatosis.emergent_axis: primary bile-acid synthesis (sterol 27-hydroxylase / CYP27A1 throughput to chenodeoxycholic acid + cholic acid; LOF -> bile-acid synthesis down, loss of CDCA feedback on CYP7A1 -> cholestanol/bile-alcohol over-production and tissue accumulation) -- a bile-acid-synthesis metabolic axis

causal_genes.note: CYP27A1 encodes sterol 27-hydroxylase, the mitochondrial cytochrome-P450 that 27-hydroxylates sterol intermediates in primary bile-acid synthesis -- the step needed to form chenodeoxycholic acid and cholic acid from cholesterol. LOF lowers primary bile-acid synthesis throughput -> CDCA falls, its feedback inhibition of CYP7A1 is lost, and flux is diverted to over-produce cholestanol and bile alcohols that accumulate in tissues. As a deficient ENZYME the pathway throughput goes DOWN (with downstream accumulation of the aberrant shunt products), so the corrective lever RESTORES the end-product. Autosomal recessive, 2q35 (OMIM 606530). NCBI official symbol CYP27A1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Cali 1991 J Biol Chem 266:7779 (CYP27A1 mutations cause CTX); Bjorkhem 2013 J Intern Med 273:520 (CTX sterol-27-hydroxylase pathophysiology)

context_genes.note: CYP7A1 encodes cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme of the classic bile-acid pathway and the target of CDCA's negative feedback. In CTX the loss of CDCA DE-REPRESSES CYP7A1, driving the cholestanol/bile-alcohol over-production; restoring CDCA re-imposes this feedback. CYP7A1 frames the feedback node the lead lever acts through, but it is not the CTX lesion.
context_genes.src: Ellis 2003 Hepatology 38:930 (CDCA is the strongest feedback inhibitor of bile-acid synthesis / CYP7A1)

context_genes.note: HMGCR encodes HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis and the statin target. Statins lower the cholesterol substrate pool but do NOT restore the CYP27A1 step or bile-acid synthesis, so statins are a downstream-symptomatic adjunct, not the switch-restoring lever; HMGCR frames why substrate-lowering is not corrective here.

beta_thalassaemia.summary: A single-gene HBB loss-of-function -- but a QUANTITATIVE one, the deliberate contrast to sickle cell disease on the SAME HBB locus. HBB encodes the beta-globin chain of adult haemoglobin (HbA = alpha2beta2). Beta-thalassaemia alleles REDUCE (beta+) or ABOLISH (beta0) beta-globin output (promoter/splice/nonsense lesions lowering the amount of an otherwise-normal chain), so beta-globin synthesis falls -> the alpha-globin chains made in excess have no beta partner, precipitate, and damage erythroid precursors -> INEFFECTIVE ERYTHROPOIESIS and haemolysis (transfusion-dependent beta-thalassaemia major; milder beta-thalassaemia intermedia). The beta-globin-output axis is driven DOWN. This is read on the SAME structural-globin axis as sickle cell, but where sickle cell is a QUALITATIVE defect (a single missense, Glu6Val, that makes a normal AMOUNT of an ABNORMAL chain -- HbS -- that polymerises), beta-thalassaemia is a QUANTITATIVE defect (too LITTLE of a normal chain): one gene (HBB), two different KINDS of lesion -- the lesion-TYPE analogue of the Rett <-> MECP2-duplication same-locus pairing (which was a dosage-DIRECTION pair). The kit re-derives the approved corrective arms on the existing engine: (i) POTENTIATE late-stage erythroid maturation -- luspatercept, an activin-receptor-IIB ligand trap that sequesters TGF-beta-superfamily ligands (e.g. GDF11) to relieve SMAD2/3 inhibition of terminal erythroid maturation, raising effective red-cell output despite the beta-globin deficit (the distinctive beta-thalassaemia lead, NOT used in sickle cell); (ii) re-induce FETAL haemoglobin (HbF, alpha2gamma2) to substitute for the missing beta-globin -- oppose BCL11A / exagamglogene autotemcel (the SAME HbF-induction route shared with sickle cell); and (iii) ADD a functional beta-globin gene -- betibeglogene autotemcel (gene addition). The gamma read is of the HBB locus switch STRUCTURE (identical to the sickle-cell read, since it is the same locus); the disease lesions are quantitative (promoter, splice, and nonsense alleles reducing beta-globin amount), outside the promoter-switch firewall as a magnitude question. Magnitude [O].

niemann_pick_disease_type_c.summary: A single-gene NPC1 loss-of-function. NPC1 encodes a large polytopic late-endosomal/lysosomal membrane protein that, with the soluble luminal partner NPC2, EXPORTS unesterified cholesterol (delivered by LDL endocytosis) out of the late endosome/lysosome and coordinates lysosomal sphingolipid trafficking. NPC1 LOF disables this export -> unesterified cholesterol, glycosphingolipids and sphingosine ACCUMULATE in late endosomes/lysosomes of neurons and viscera -> a neurovisceral disease: hepatosplenomegaly, progressive cerebellar ataxia, dystonia, dysphagia, cognitive decline and the characteristic VERTICAL SUPRANUCLEAR GAZE PALSY (the NPC spectrum, from neonatal cholestasis to adult neurodegeneration). The stored-lysosomal-load axis is driven UP by loss of the export 'brake'. This is read on the kit's lysosomal-storage axis -- the SEVENTH lysosomal read -- but as a TRAFFICKING / TRANSPORT defect, NOT a catabolic-enzyme defect: it is the explicit contrast both to the enzyme-replacement lysosomal reads (Gaucher, Fabry, Pompe, LIPA -- a missing catalyst) AND to cystinosis on a DIFFERENT cargo (cystinosis loses a lysosomal cystine EXPORTER; NPC loses a lysosomal cholesterol/sphingolipid EXPORTER -- both transport defects, corrected by lowering the stored substrate rather than by replacing an enzyme). The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: SUBSTRATE REDUCTION -- miglustat, a glucosylceramide-synthase inhibitor that lowers glycosphingolipid synthesis so less accumulates (EMA-approved for NPC neurological manifestations) -- with arimoclomol, a heat-shock-response co-inducer that enhances lysosomal protein handling/function (FDA 2024 for NPC, used with miglustat), as the established adjunct correcting lysosomal function. (Levacetylleucine, approved 2024 for NPC neurological symptoms, is a further symptomatic adjunct.) The gamma read is of the NPC1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/missense (notably the common p.Ile1061Thr allele), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
niemann_pick_disease_type_c.emergent_axis: lysosomal cholesterol/sphingolipid trafficking (NPC1 export of unesterified cholesterol + sphingolipids from the late endosome/lysosome; LOF -> stored lysosomal lipid load UP) -- a lysosomal trafficking/transport axis

As a lost export 'brake' the stored-load axis goes UP (the same released-brake convention used for the cystinosis lysosomal transporter and for tyrosinaemia/haemochromatosis accumulation). Autosomal recessive, 18q11.2 (OMIM 607623). NCBI official symbol NPC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/missense lesions (e.g. p.Ile1061Thr) are outside the promoter firewall.

classical_homocystinuria.summary: A single-gene CBS loss-of-function. CBS encodes cystathionine-beta-synthase, the pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (vitamin-B6)-dependent enzyme that commits homocysteine to the TRANSSULFURATION pathway by condensing it with serine to form cystathionine (en route to cysteine). CBS LOF lowers transsulfuration throughput, so HOMOCYSTEINE ACCUMULATES (and methionine rises) -> classical homocystinuria: ectopia lentis (downward lens dislocation), a marfanoid skeletal habitus, osteoporosis, thromboembolism (the major cause of morbidity/mortality) and variable intellectual disability. The transsulfuration axis is driven DOWN, with the toxic substrate homocysteine accumulating upstream of the block. This OPENS A NEW SULFUR-AMINO-ACID (methionine-homocysteine transsulfuration) metabolic axis for the kit -- the contrast to phenylketonuria's AROMATIC-amino-acid axis (PAH): both are amino-acid enzyme/LOF reads with an accumulating toxic substrate, on different amino-acid pathways. The kit re-derives the approved corrective arms on the existing engine: (i) LOWER the accumulated homocysteine by an ALTERNATIVE remethylation route -- betaine (anhydrous betaine), a methyl donor that drives the betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase (BHMT) reaction to remethylate homocysteine back to methionine, reducing the toxic homocysteine pool (the approved lead); (ii) supply the CBS COFACTOR -- pyridoxine (vitamin B6) -- which restores residual CBS activity in the substantial B6-RESPONSIVE subset (the cofactor-restore arm, analogous to BH4/sapropterin in PKU); plus a methionine-restricted diet (lower the upstream substrate) and folate/B12 to support remethylation. The gamma read is of the CBS locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/missense (notably the B6-responsive p.Ile278Thr and the B6-non-responsive p.Gly307Ser), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

As a deficient ENZYME the pathway throughput goes DOWN with upstream substrate (homocysteine) accumulation, so the corrective levers LOWER the accumulated metabolite and/or RESTORE residual enzyme via cofactor. Autosomal recessive, 21q22.3 (OMIM 613381). NCBI official symbol CBS. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/missense lesions (e.g. the B6-responsive p.Ile278Thr, the B6-non-responsive p.Gly307Ser) are outside the promoter firewall.

niemann_pick_disease_type_a_b.disease: Niemann-Pick disease type A/B (acid sphingomyelinase deficiency, SMPD1)
niemann_pick_disease_type_a_b.summary: A single-gene SMPD1 loss-of-function. SMPD1 encodes acid sphingomyelinase (ASM), the lysosomal hydrolase that cleaves sphingomyelin into ceramide and phosphocholine. LOF lowers lysosomal sphingomyelin-catabolism throughput, so sphingomyelin (and secondarily cholesterol) ACCUMULATE in the lysosomes of macrophages, hepatocytes, spleen and (in the severe infantile form) neurons -> hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial lung disease, dyslipidaemia, and, in type A, rapidly progressive neurodegeneration; type B (chronic visceral) retains residual ASM and largely spares the CNS. The catabolic-throughput axis is driven DOWN; the correction is to restore enzymatic throughput. Read on the SAME deficient-enzyme / substrate-accumulation level axis as Gaucher, Fabry, Pompe and LAL deficiency -- the EIGHTH lysosomal-storage read, here on a SPHINGOLIPID (sphingomyelin) substrate handled by enzyme replacement. The kit re-derives the approved throughput-restore arm -- replace ASM via recombinant human acid sphingomyelinase (olipudase alfa). This is the elegant 'Niemann-Pick, two names, two utterly different mechanisms' CONTRAST to Niemann-Pick type C (NPC1, already in the kit): A/B is an ENZYME deficiency corrected by enzyme replacement (replace), whereas type C is a cholesterol/sphingolipid TRANSPORT (export) defect corrected by substrate reduction (restrain) -- the same eponym, an opposite defect class and an opposite lever. Olipudase alfa addresses the systemic/visceral disease and does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so the neurological component of type A is not corrected by it (a delivery limitation, CNS reach [O]); the SWITCH DIRECTION (restore sphingomyelin catabolism) is nonetheless correct and re-derives the approved enzyme. The gamma read is of the SMPD1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding (the type-A founder alleles p.Leu302Pro / p.fsPro330 / p.Arg498Leu; the type-B p.delR608 allele), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

causal_genes.note: SMPD1 encodes acid sphingomyelinase (ASM / sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 1), the lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyses sphingomyelin to ceramide and phosphocholine. LOF lowers lysosomal sphingomyelin catabolism -> sphingomyelin and cholesterol accumulate in lysosomes of macrophages, liver, spleen and (type A) neurons. Autosomal recessive, 11p15.4 (OMIM 607608). NCBI official symbol SMPD1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding lesions (the type-A founder alleles; the type-B p.delR608) are outside the promoter firewall.

It frames the contrast but is not the SMPD1 lesion.

x_linked_adrenoleukodystrophy.summary: A single-gene ABCD1 loss-of-function. ABCD1 encodes the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP), the peroxisomal-membrane ABC half-transporter that IMPORTS very-long-chain fatty acyl-CoAs (VLCFA-CoA) into the peroxisome for beta-oxidation. ALDP is the BRAKE on VLCFA accumulation; with ABCD1 LOF the import fails, VLCFA cannot reach the peroxisomal degradation machinery, and saturated VLCFA (C24:0, C26:0) ACCUMULATE in plasma and tissues -> adrenal cortical insufficiency (Addison disease), and, in the dreaded childhood cerebral form, an inflammatory demyelination of cerebral white matter; adult males develop the slowly progressive myelopathy adrenomyeloneuropathy. The VLCFA-load axis is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on toxic accumulation (ALDP imports VLCFA for degradation; LOF releases the clearance -> VLCFA UP) -- the released-brake -> over-accumulation convention (tyrosinaemia / haemochromatosis / cystinosis / NPC1) carried onto a NEW ORGANELLE: the PEROXISOME. Every prior storage read in the kit is LYSOSOMAL; X-ALD is the FIRST peroxisomal read, and the contrast is sharp -- the lysosomal transport-defect reads (cystinosis CTNS, Niemann-Pick C NPC1) are EXPORT defects (cargo trapped INSIDE the lysosome), whereas ABCD1 is an IMPORT defect (cargo cannot ENTER the peroxisome to be degraded), opposite transport directions on different organelles, both releasing a brake on accumulation. Because no approved small molecule lowers the CNS VLCFA burden in a disease-modifying way, the lead is the definitive switch-level restoration: add a functional ABCD1 gene (autologous CD34+ haematopoietic-stem-cell ex-vivo lentiviral ABCD1 gene addition, elivaldogene autotemcel / Skysona, approved for early cerebral ALD), whose donor-derived microglia restore peroxisomal VLCFA beta-oxidation in the CNS and arrest demyelination -- the net axis effect LOWERS the VLCFA burden, so it is restrain-coded (the OTC / cystinosis-gene-restore convention). Allogeneic haematopoietic-stem-cell transplantation is the established equivalent (donor-derived microglia supply functional ALDP), also restrain-coded by net axis effect. Lorenzo's oil (glyceryl trioleate + trierucate) NORMALISES PLASMA VLCFA but does NOT prevent or modify cerebral disease and is recorded as a downstream / biomarker-only NON-lever (the LAL-D statin discipline -- it moves a marker without touching the switch outcome). The gamma read is of the ABCD1 locus switch STRUCTURE -- a CpG-island promoter (GC ~0.68), one of the deepest switches in the kit (third behind FGFR3 and HTT); the disease lesion is coding (the recurrent p.Arg104Cys / p.Arg152Cys / p.Pro560Leu missense alleles), outside the promoter firewall. Phenotype is famously UNPREDICTABLE from genotype (the same ABCD1 allele can give cerebral ALD, adrenomyeloneuropathy or Addison-only, even within a family), so penetrance / clinical-course magnitude is held [O]. Magnitude [O].

cystinuria.summary: A single-pathway disease caused by loss-of-function of either subunit of an obligate heterodimeric amino-acid transporter. SLC3A1 (rBAT, the heavy/chaperone subunit) and SLC7A9 (b0,+AT, the catalytic light subunit) assemble into the rBAT/b0,+AT transporter of the renal proximal-tubule (and intestinal) brush border, which REABSORBS cystine and the dibasic amino acids (ornithine, lysine, arginine) from the lumen -- the BRAKE that keeps filtered cystine from being lost in the urine. Biallelic LOF of EITHER subunit disables the shared transporter (type A = SLC3A1, type B = SLC7A9), so cystine is not reabsorbed and its poorly-soluble free form accumulates in the urine and crystallises into recurrent cystine STONES -> obstructive uropathy and progressive renal damage. The free-urinary-cystine axis is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on luminal cystine retention (rBAT/b0,+AT reabsorbs cystine; LOF releases it into the urine -> free urinary cystine UP), and a TWO-CAUSAL-GENE read where both subunits perturb the same axis UP (the HCM / sitosterolaemia convergence pattern -- the THIRD such convergence; the deeper switch, SLC7A9 the catalytic light subunit, is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the established arm -- RESTRAIN the free cystine with a thiol that undergoes thiol-disulfide exchange: tiopronin (and the older D-penicillamine) react with cystine to form a far more soluble cysteine-thiol mixed disulfide, lowering the free-cystine concentration so it no longer crystallises. Urinary alkalinisation (potassium citrate, which raises cystine solubility) and high fluid intake are adjuncts that lower the crystallisation / stone burden. This is the explicit 'CYSTINE, two diseases, two transporters' CONTRAST to cystinosis (CTNS, already in the kit): cystinosis is a LYSOSOMAL cystine-EXPORTER defect -> cystine trapped INSIDE the lysosome (intracellular storage, depleted in situ by the aminothiol cysteamine), whereas cystinuria is a RENAL-TUBULE cystine-REABSORBER defect -> cystine lost into the URINE (luminal stones, solubilised by the thiol tiopronin) -- the SAME molecule, a DIFFERENT transporter, a DIFFERENT compartment, but a strikingly PARALLEL lever (in BOTH a thiol converts cystine into a soluble mixed disulfide; cysteamine intracellularly, tiopronin in the urine). The gamma reads are of the SLC3A1 and SLC7A9 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. SLC3A1 p.Met467Thr; SLC7A9 p.Gly105Arg), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
cystinuria.emergent_axis: free urinary cystine burden (renal-tubular cystine reabsorption / cystine-stone crystallisation) -- the renal-tubular reabsorption contrast to cystinosis's lysosomal cystine-export axis on the same molecule

causal_genes.note: SLC7A9 encodes b0,+AT, the CATALYTIC light subunit of the rBAT/b0,+AT brush-border transporter that reabsorbs cystine and dibasic amino acids from the renal proximal tubule -- the functional permease of the heterodimer. Biallelic LOF (cystinuria type B / non-type-I) disables reabsorption -> free cystine is lost into the urine and crystallises (axis UP). 19q13.11 (OMIM 604144). NCBI official symbol SLC7A9. As the catalytic subunit it is the deeper promoter switch of the pair and is picked as primary; the corrective direction is identical for either subunit. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding lesions (e.g. p.Gly105Arg) are outside the promoter firewall.

NCBI official symbol SLC3A1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding lesions (e.g. the common p.Met467Thr allele) are outside the promoter firewall.

tetrahydrobiopterin_deficiency.summary: PTS encodes 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin synthase, the second (committed) enzyme of de novo tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) biosynthesis from GTP. Loss-of-function collapses the BH4 cofactor supply. BH4 is the obligate cofactor of THREE aromatic-amino-acid hydroxylases -- phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) -- so BH4 deficiency produces (a) hyperphenylalaninaemia, the SAME accumulating metabolite as classic PKU but arising from a COFACTOR lesion rather than the PAH apoenzyme, AND (b) central monoamine-neurotransmitter (dopamine, serotonin) depletion that PKU does NOT cause, giving a severe encephalopathy with dystonia/seizures historically called 'malignant hyperphenylalaninaemia'. This is read as an enzyme/LOF lowering BH4-supply throughput -> the cofactor-supply axis is pushed DOWN, so the corrective direction RESTORES it. The kit re-derives the approved lever: supply the missing cofactor exogenously -- sapropterin (synthetic BH4, Kuvan, FDA 2007) -- which HERE acts to REPLACE the deficient cofactor itself. This is the elegant 'one drug, two lever roles' contrast to PKU, where the SAME sapropterin acts instead as a CORRECT / chaperone arm stabilising residual PAH apoenzyme (BH4 is not the lesion there). Because BH4 deficiency ALSO starves TH and TPH, the read adds a monoamine-replacement arm -- L-dopa + carbidopa and 5-hydroxytryptophan -- that PKU never needs. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only (firewall); the coding lesions are outside the promoter firewall and every magnitude is held [O].
tetrahydrobiopterin_deficiency.emergent_axis: tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) cofactor supply (PTPS enzyme switch) -> aromatic-amino-acid hydroxylation (phenylalanine clearance) + monoamine-neurotransmitter (dopamine/serotonin) synthesis -- a cofactor-supply axis

causal_genes.note: PTS encodes 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin synthase, the committed (rate-limiting) step of de novo BH4 biosynthesis (GTP -> dihydroneopterin triphosphate -> 6-pyruvoyl-tetrahydropterin -> BH4). Biallelic LOF (PTPS deficiency, the commonest BH4-synthesis defect, ~60% of BH4-deficient hyperphenylalaninaemia) abolishes BH4 supply, so EVERY BH4-dependent hydroxylase loses its cofactor -> phenylalanine accumulates (as in PKU) AND dopamine/serotonin synthesis fails. As a deficient ENZYME the pathway throughput falls and the cofactor-supply axis goes DOWN, so the corrective levers RAISE it. Autosomal recessive, 11q23.1 (OMIM 261640). NCBI official symbol PTS. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: Thony 2000 Hum Mutat 16:54 (PTPS deficiency mutations); Opladen 2012 Mol Genet Metab 105:35 (BH4-deficiency genotype-phenotype); Blau 2010 Lancet 376:1417 (hyperphenylalaninaemia spectrum)

context_genes.note: PAH encodes phenylalanine hydroxylase, the BH4-DEPENDENT enzyme whose own deficiency causes classic PKU. It frames the central contrast: PKU is an APOENZYME lesion (PAH), BH4 deficiency is a COFACTOR lesion upstream -- the SAME accumulating metabolite (phenylalanine), two different switch reads, and the reason sapropterin is a chaperone CORRECT arm in PKU but a cofactor REPLACE arm here.

TH encodes tyrosine hydroxylase, the BH4-dependent, rate-limiting enzyme of dopamine (and thence noradrenaline/adrenaline) synthesis. Its BH4 starvation is why BH4 deficiency -- unlike PKU -- causes a dopaminergic movement disorder, and the reason the read adds an L-dopa monoamine-replacement arm downstream of this block.
context_genes.src: Nagatsu 1964 J Biol Chem 239:2910 (tyrosine hydroxylase); Blau 2010

context_genes.note: QDPR encodes dihydropteridine reductase, which REGENERATES BH4 from its quinonoid-dihydro form after each hydroxylation. QDPR LOF is the alternative BH4-RECYCLING cause of BH4-deficient hyperphenylalaninaemia (DHPR deficiency), a distinct genetic form that additionally needs folinic acid -- the recycling counterpart to this synthesis (PTPS) lesion.

GCH1 encodes GTP cyclohydrolase I, the FIRST enzyme of BH4 synthesis (upstream of PTPS). Its dominant LOF causes dopa-responsive dystonia and its recessive LOF another BH4-deficient HPA -- framing PTPS as the second step of the same de novo pathway.

familial_mediterranean_fever.summary: MEFV encodes pyrin (marenostrin), an innate-immune sensor that nucleates the PYRIN inflammasome -- a SECOND, distinct inflammasome from the NLRP3 inflammasome of CAPS. On activation pyrin recruits the adaptor ASC and pro-caspase-1, and active caspase-1 matures pro-IL-1beta to its secreted form. FMF alleles -- clustered in the C-terminal B30.2/SPRY domain (M694V, M680I, V726A, M694I) -- are FUNCTIONALLY gain-of-function: the mutant pyrin escapes its normal RhoA-PKN regulatory brake and assembles the inflammasome at a lowered threshold, so IL-1beta is OVER-produced and the inflammatory drive is pushed UP. (FMF is classically inherited autosomal-recessive / gene-dose-dependent, yet the protein-level lesion is an over-active sensor.) The phenotype is recurrent, self-limited attacks of fever with SEROSITIS (peritonitis, pleuritis), synovitis and an erysipelas-like erythema, with AA amyloidosis as the feared long-term complication. This is read as an over-driven ACCELERATOR of IL-1beta output on the inflammasome / autoinflammatory axis -- the SECOND inflammasome SENSOR the kit reads (after NLRP3) but the FIRST on the PYRIN inflammasome -- so the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN it. The kit re-derives the iconic approved lever: colchicine, the FMF first-line, which neutrophils concentrate and where it depolymerises microtubules and thereby suppresses pyrin-inflammasome assembly and the downstream IL-1beta drive -- a CYTOSKELETAL / microtubule mechanism NOT used in CAPS or DIRA. For colchicine-resistant disease it re-derives IL-1 blockade (canakinumab, FDA-approved for colchicine-resistant FMF; anakinra). The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only (firewall); the B30.2-domain missense lesions are outside the promoter firewall and every magnitude is held [O].
familial_mediterranean_fever.emergent_axis: pyrin-inflammasome IL-1beta drive (MEFV-pyrin over-activation -> caspase-1 -> IL-1beta over-production -> recurrent serosal/synovial autoinflammation) -- a second inflammasome SENSOR on the IL-1 axis

causal_genes.note: MEFV (Mediterranean fever; pyrin / marenostrin) encodes the sensor that nucleates the PYRIN inflammasome; via ASC it activates caspase-1, which matures pro-IL-1beta -- the driver of the autoinflammatory response. FMF alleles in the C-terminal B30.2/SPRY domain are functionally GAIN-of-function: the mutant pyrin escapes RhoA-PKN-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation and assembles/fires at a lowered threshold -> IL-1beta is over-produced -> the inflammatory drive is pushed UP. As an over-driven ACCELERATOR of IL-1beta output the pathological axis goes UP and the corrective levers LOWER it. Classically autosomal-recessive / gene-dose-dependent, 16p13.3 (OMIM 608107 gene). NCBI official symbol MEFV. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the activating B30.2-domain missense lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: International FMF Consortium 1997 Cell 90:797 and French FMF Consortium 1997 Nat Genet 17:25 (MEFV/pyrin cloned); Chae 2011 Immunity 34:755 (FMF pyrin is hyperactive); Park 2016 Nat Immunol 17:914 (RhoA-PKN regulation of pyrin)

context_genes.note: IL1B encodes interleukin-1beta, the effector cytokine the over-active pyrin inflammasome over-produces and the proximate driver of the FMF phenotype. It is the target of the second-line restrain arm: canakinumab neutralises IL-1beta (approved for colchicine-resistant FMF).
context_genes.src: De Benedetti 2018 NEJM 378:1908 (canakinumab in colchicine-resistant FMF)

context_genes.note: CASP1 encodes caspase-1, the inflammasome protease that -- once pyrin/ASC assemble -- cleaves pro-IL-1beta to its mature form, the catalytic step between the over-active sensor and the over-produced cytokine. It frames the axis between MEFV and IL1B but is not the FMF lesion.

NLRP3 encodes the OTHER inflammasome sensor (the CAPS lesion). FMF (pyrin inflammasome) and CAPS (NLRP3 inflammasome) are the kit's two distinct inflammasome SENSORS feeding one IL-1 axis -- both over-driven accelerators restrained toward healthy, but by different upstream levers (colchicine acts on pyrin via microtubules; NLRP3 disease is addressed by IL-1 blockade).

angelman_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is loss of function of the MATERNALLY-expressed, paternally-imprinted UBE3A allele in 15q11-q13 -- typically a maternal multi-megabase DELETION, paternal uniparental disomy, or an IMPRINTING-CENTRE defect, with about 10% from a maternal UBE3A point mutation -- not a single-gene promoter switch. In neurons the paternal UBE3A is silenced by the UBE3A-antisense transcript, so only the maternal allele is expressed; the disease is DEFINED by the parent-of-origin-specific loss of that maternal allele -- a methylation/dosage state across the imprinted locus -- so there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read (even the point-mutation minority is a parent-of-origin-dependent lesion that a promoter switch cannot capture). Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). This is the RECIPROCAL imprinting hold to Prader-Willi: Prader-Willi is loss of the PATERNAL genes of the SAME 15q11-q13 region, Angelman is loss of the MATERNAL UBE3A -- so the kit now holds the same chromosomal region from BOTH parental origins, demonstrating that the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM (imprinting), independent of parent-of-origin. A parent-of-origin (epigenetic) multi-gene model is future work, not a single-switch emergence.
angelman_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- maternal imprinting / structural 15q11-q13 cause, not a single-gene switch)

tuberous_sclerosis_complex.summary: A dominantly inherited multisystem hamartoma syndrome caused by loss-of-function of either subunit of an obligate signalling BRAKE. TSC1 (hamartin) and TSC2 (tuberin) form the TSC protein complex, the GTPase-activating-protein (GAP) that keeps the small GTPase Rheb in its inactive GDP state and so RESTRAINS mechanistic-target-of-rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), the master growth/anabolism kinase hub. The functional brake is the TSC1/TSC2 complex, so biallelic (two-hit, germline + somatic) LOF of EITHER subunit disables the same GAP -> Rheb stays GTP-loaded -> mTORC1 is constitutively over-active -> protein/lipid synthesis and cell growth run unrestrained -> hamartomas across brain (cortical tubers, subependymal giant-cell astrocytoma/SEGA, epilepsy), kidney (angiomyolipoma), heart (rhabdomyoma), skin and lung (lymphangioleiomyomatosis). Read as a released BRAKE on mTORC1 (the TSC1/TSC2 complex brakes Rheb-mTORC1; LOF releases it -> signalling UP) -- the released-brake -> over-activation convention (tyrosinaemia / haemochromatosis / sitosterolaemia) carried onto a NEW INTRACELLULAR SIGNALLING (mTOR / growth-regulation) axis, and the kit's FOURTH TWO-CAUSAL-GENE convergence (after HCM, sitosterolaemia, cystinuria) where both subunits perturb the SAME axis UP (the deeper switch, TSC2, is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the targeted approved arm -- RESTRAIN the over-active node with an mTOR inhibitor (everolimus / sirolimus), which inhibits mTORC1 directly and so lowers the over-driven growth output even though the TSC1/TSC2 GAP remains broken (the upstream/parallel-node restraint logic). Everolimus is approved for TSC-associated SEGA, renal angiomyolipoma and refractory seizures; it modifies the pathway, is not curative, and the neurocognitive (TSC-associated neuropsychiatric / autism) burden is incompletely addressed (recorded honestly). The gamma reads the TSC1 and TSC2 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice/deletion two-hit events outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
tuberous_sclerosis_complex.emergent_axis: mTORC1 signalling output (cell growth / anabolism -> hamartomatous tissue overgrowth) -- a growth-regulation / mTOR-pathway axis; the released-brake -> over-activation read on an intracellular signalling pathway, the signalling contrast to the kit's metabolite/level/transport axes

causal_genes.note: TSC1 encodes hamartin, one subunit of the TSC1/TSC2 GTPase-activating-protein complex that holds Rheb inactive (GDP) and so RESTRAINS mTORC1 -- a BRAKE on growth signalling. Hamartin stabilises tuberin and localises the complex; two-hit LOF disables the shared GAP -> Rheb-GTP -> mTORC1 over-activation (axis UP). 9q34.13, OMIM 605284; TSC1 disease OMIM 191100. NCBI official symbol TSC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice/deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: van Slegtenhorst 1997 Science 277:805 (TSC1/hamartin identified); Tee 2003 Curr Biol 13:1259 (TSC1/TSC2 is the Rheb GAP braking mTORC1)

causal_genes.note: TSC2 encodes tuberin, the obligate partner subunit that carries the catalytic GAP domain acting on Rheb; the functional brake is the TSC1/TSC2 heterodimer, so two-hit LOF of TSC2 disables Rheb GAP activity just as TSC1 loss does -> the same released-brake -> mTORC1 over-activation (axis UP). TSC2 mutations are generally commoner and more severe than TSC1. 16p13.3 (contiguous with PKD1), OMIM 191092; TSC2 disease OMIM 613254. NCBI official symbol TSC2. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding/splice/large-deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
causal_genes.src: European Chromosome 16 TSC Consortium 1993 Cell 75:1305 (TSC2/tuberin identified); Inoki 2003 Nat Cell Biol 5:578 (tuberin is the Rheb GAP)

context_genes.note: MTOR encodes the serine/threonine kinase at the core of mTORC1, the node DOWNSTREAM of Rheb that the broken TSC1/TSC2 brake fails to restrain. It is the target of the approved lead lever everolimus / sirolimus (rapalogues): inhibiting mTORC1 lowers the over-driven growth output and shrinks the hamartomas even though the GAP remains broken (the parallel-node restraint logic).
context_genes.src: Brown 1994 Nature 369:756 (mTOR / FRAP identified); Bissler 2008 NEJM 358:140 (sirolimus shrinks TSC angiomyolipoma/LAM)

context_genes.note: RHEB encodes the small GTPase that, when GTP-loaded, directly activates mTORC1. The TSC1/TSC2 complex is RHEB's GAP, so loss of the complex leaves RHEB constitutively GTP-bound -- the immediate molecular consequence of the brake loss and the reason mTORC1 over-fires. RHEB frames the mechanism but is not the TSC lesion.
context_genes.src: Garami 2003 Mol Cell 11:1457; Tee 2003 Curr Biol 13:1259 (Rheb is the TSC1/TSC2 GAP substrate driving mTORC1)

therapeutic_axes.push: inhibit mTORC1 (rapalogue) to lower the over-active growth-signalling output -> push the axis DOWN toward healthy and shrink the hamartomas; bypasses the broken TSC1/TSC2 GAP brake by acting at the downstream kinase node

therapeutic_axes.push: restore the TSC1/TSC2 GAP brake on Rheb-mTORC1 so the pathway is no longer over-driven -> the NET axis effect is to RESTRAIN the over-shoot back toward normal (gene/function restoration of the deeper causal subunit; restrain-coded by net axis effect, the Wilson/cystinosis convention)

von_hippel_lindau_disease.summary: A dominantly inherited tumour-predisposition syndrome caused by loss-of-function of an E3-ubiquitin-ligase substrate-recognition BRAKE on the hypoxia response. The VHL protein (pVHL) is the substrate-recognition subunit of an E3 ligase (with elongin B/C, cullin-2, Rbx1) that, under normal oxygen, binds the prolyl-hydroxylated hypoxia-inducible factor alpha subunits (chiefly HIF-2alpha / EPAS1, also HIF-1alpha) and targets them for proteasomal degradation -- the BRAKE that keeps the pseudohypoxic transcriptional programme OFF when oxygen is plentiful. Germline LOF of one VHL allele plus somatic second-hit loss disables that recognition -> HIF-2alpha is no longer degraded under normoxia -> it accumulates, dimerises with HIF-1beta/ARNT and drives a constitutive pseudohypoxic transcriptional output (VEGF, PDGF, EPO, GLUT1, TGF-alpha) -> highly vascular tumours: retinal and CNS haemangioblastomas, clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours and cysts, endolymphatic-sac tumours. Read as a released BRAKE on the HIF response (pVHL degrades HIF-2alpha; LOF releases it -> HIF-2alpha drive UP) -- the released-brake -> over-activation convention, but here the released species is a STABILISED TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR, opening a NEW HYPOXIA-SENSING (HIF) axis and the brake-loss -> TF-stabilisation contrast to the kit's metabolite/enzyme/transport released-brake reads. The kit re-derives the targeted approved arm -- RESTRAIN the stabilised driver with the HIF-2alpha inhibitor belzutifan (Welireg, FDA 2021 for VHL-associated tumours not requiring immediate surgery), which blocks HIF-2alpha/ARNT dimerisation and so lowers the pseudohypoxic output even though pVHL recognition remains lost (the downstream-driver restraint logic). Belzutifan is a systemic option for tumours that previously required repeated surgery; it modifies the disease, is not curative, and resistance/residual disease occur (recorded honestly). The gamma reads the VHL locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are missense/truncating/deletion two-hit events outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
von_hippel_lindau_disease.emergent_axis: HIF-2alpha-driven pseudohypoxic transcriptional output (angiogenic / proliferative tumour drive) -- a hypoxia-sensing (HIF) axis; the brake-loss -> transcription-factor-stabilisation contrast to the kit's other released-brake (metabolite/transport) reads

causal_genes.note: VHL encodes pVHL, the substrate-recognition subunit of a cullin-2 E3 ubiquitin ligase that binds prolyl-hydroxylated HIF-alpha (HIF-2alpha/EPAS1, HIF-1alpha) under normoxia and marks it for proteasomal degradation -- the BRAKE on the hypoxia-inducible transcriptional programme. Two-hit (germline + somatic) LOF removes that recognition -> HIF-2alpha is stabilised and the pseudohypoxic drive runs constitutively (axis UP). 3p25.3, OMIM 608537; VHL disease OMIM 193300. NCBI official symbol VHL. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
