beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a parent-of-origin (imprinting) defect of the 11p15.5 imprinted region -- NOT a single-gene promoter switch. 11p15.5 carries two differentially methylated imprinting control regions: IC1 (H19/IGF2, controlling the paternally-expressed growth promoter IGF2 and the maternally-expressed lncRNA H19) and IC2 (KCNQ1OT1/CDKN1C, controlling the maternally-expressed growth-suppressor CDKN1C via the paternally-expressed antisense lncRNA KCNQ1OT1). Beckwith-Wiedemann arises from an EPIGENETIC/STRUCTURAL state across this locus: loss of methylation at IC2 (~50%), gain of methylation at IC1 (~5-10%), paternal uniparental disomy of 11p15.5 (~20%), or a maternal CDKN1C loss-of-function point mutation (~5%, ~40% of familial cases). The net effect -- increased IGF2 dosage and/or reduced CDKN1C -- is an overgrowth phenotype (macrosomia, macroglossia, abdominal-wall defects, hemihyperplasia, embryonal-tumour risk), but it is DEFINED by the parent-of-origin methylation/dosage state of an imprinted multi-gene region, so there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read. Even the CDKN1C point-mutation minority is a parent-of-origin-dependent lesion (pathogenic only on the maternal allele) that a strand-symmetric promoter switch cannot capture. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). This is a THIRD imprinting hold, and the FIRST on a locus OTHER than 15q11-q13: where Prader-Willi (paternal loss) and Angelman (maternal UBE3A loss) are the reciprocal 15q11-q13 pair, Beckwith-Wiedemann is an 11p15.5 imprinting disorder on a DIFFERENT chromosome -- so the kit now demonstrates that the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM (imprinting) and GENERALISES across imprinted loci, not just within 15q. A parent-of-origin (epigenetic) multi-gene dosage model is future work, not a single-switch emergence.
beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- 11p15.5 imprinting / methylation cause, not a single-gene switch)

x_linked_retinitis_pigmentosa.summary: The most common form of X-linked inherited retinal degeneration. Loss-of-function of RPGR -- the retinitis-pigmentosa GTPase regulator that localises to the photoreceptor connecting cilium and organises the ciliary protein trafficking that sustains outer-segment renewal -- removes that maintenance drive, so rod (and progressively cone) photoreceptors mislocalise opsin, fail to renew outer segments, and degenerate -> early-onset night blindness, progressive concentric visual-field loss and eventual central vision loss. The disease is read as the photoreceptor ciliary-trafficking / outer-segment-maintenance throughput axis driven DOWN (a positive maintenance driver whose loss starves outer-segment renewal -- the drive-lost shape, a SECOND ocular read that CONTRASTS with LCA2: LCA2 (RPE65) is a retinoid-CYCLE ENZYME deficiency starving the chromophore, RPGR-XLRP is a ciliary-TRAFFICKING / structural-maintenance deficiency starving outer-segment renewal -- two distinct ocular axes whose lead corrective lever is the same class, gene restoration). Correction is to restore the gene at the locus: replace RPGR (subretinal AAV-RPGR gene transfer). IMPORTANT HONESTY: there is at present NO approved therapy for RPGR-XLRP. The lead clinical agent is botaretigene sparoparvovec (AAV2/5-hRKp.RPGR / bota-vec); its phase 3 LUMEOS trial DID NOT MEET its primary endpoint (consistent secondary-measure signals were reported, and a regulatory filing is planned), so the kit ships this read in the SAME honest pattern as Huntington disease (no approved disease-modifying therapy; a lead clinical agent named). The firewall makes this clean: the emerged switch FORCES the corrective DIRECTION = restore RPGR [F], which the lead agent matches; the EFFICACY / MAGNITUDE is [O] -- and indeed the LUMEOS primary-endpoint result is exactly a magnitude question, recorded honestly, not asserted. Vitamin A / DHA supplementation is a supportive NON-lever (does not halt the degeneration). The gamma read is of the RPGR locus switch STRUCTURE (Xp11.4); the disease lesions are predominantly ORF15 frameshift / nonsense coding changes, outside the promoter firewall. A numerical curiosity worth noting: RPGR's promoter gamma (1.3915) is bit-identical to SMN1's (1.3915) on a DIFFERENT chromosome and a completely different disease/axis/lever -- a live demonstration that gamma alone is NOT the disease (the kit keys on the perturbation + disease spec, not the locus or its gamma). Magnitude [O].
x_linked_retinitis_pigmentosa.emergent_axis: photoreceptor connecting-cilium protein-trafficking / outer-segment-maintenance throughput (RPGR-organised ciliary transport) -- a SECOND ocular axis, the ciliary-trafficking/maintenance contrast to LCA2's retinoid-cycle enzyme axis

causal_genes.note: RPGR (retinitis pigmentosa GTPase regulator) localises to the photoreceptor connecting cilium, where its ORF15 isoform organises the intraflagellar / ciliary protein trafficking that maintains outer-segment renewal -- a positive maintenance DRIVE for photoreceptor homeostasis. LOF (predominantly ORF15 frameshift / nonsense alleles) removes that drive -> opsin mislocalisation, failed outer-segment renewal, progressive rod-then-cone degeneration -> X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (RP3; also RPGR-associated cone-rod dystrophy). Located Xp11.4. NCBI official symbol RPGR. X-linked (hemizygous males affected; carrier females variably). Coding/ORF15 lesions; promoter firewall respected.

hereditary_haemorrhagic_telangiectasia.summary: An autosomal-dominant vascular-dysplasia syndrome in which loss of an endothelial vascular-QUIESCENCE brake produces fragile, dilated, direct artery-to-vein connections -- mucocutaneous telangiectasias (recurrent epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, anaemia) and visceral arteriovenous malformations (pulmonary, hepatic, cerebral). The BMP9/10 ligands (GDF2/BMP10) signal through the endothelial type-I receptor ALK1 (ACVRL1) with the co-receptor endoglin (ENG) to phosphorylate SMAD1/5/8 -- the pathway that holds endothelium QUIESCENT (the BRAKE on endothelial activation / aberrant angiogenesis). Heterozygous LOF of ENG (HHT1) or ACVRL1 (HHT2) (haploinsufficiency) lowers BMP9/10-ALK1-ENG signalling -> the quiescence brake is released -> endothelial activation and arteriovenous malformation (axis UP). Read as a released BRAKE on endothelial quiescence, opening a NEW endothelial / TGF-beta-superfamily VASCULAR axis (the receptor-signalling contrast to the kit's metabolite / transport / inflammasome / mTOR / HIF released-brake reads), and the kit's FIFTH two-causal-gene convergence (after HCM, sitosterolaemia, cystinuria, TSC) -- two obligate partners (ALK1 receptor + endoglin co-receptor) of ONE quiescence pathway, LOF of EITHER releasing the same brake; ENG primary by barrier depth (gamma 1.5009 vs ACVRL1 1.4681). CRITICAL HONESTY (this is a DOWNGRADED read -- the kit does NOT force a drug): there is at present NO approved targeted therapy for HHT anywhere in the world. The emerged switch FORCES the corrective DIRECTION = restore the BMP9/10-ALK1-ENG quiescence brake (re-impose endothelial quiescence), but NO approved agent does this; ALK1-agonist / BMP9-mimetic / ENG- or ACVRL1-restoration approaches are investigational. The only clinically-evidenced agents are DOWNSTREAM, OFF-LABEL ANTI-ANGIOGENICS that lower the VEGF-driven angiogenic over-drive secondary to the lost brake -- bevacizumab (anti-VEGF antibody, used off-label) and pomalidomide (an immunomodulatory anti-angiogenic; approved for multiple myeloma / Kaposi sarcoma, used OFF-LABEL for HHT, with randomised-trial evidence for epistaxis in the PATH-HHT study). These act DOWNSTREAM of the broken brake and do NOT restore ENG/ACVRL1, so each is an INDIRECT (off-causal-gene, VEGFA-target) lever graded [O] by the indirect-lever honesty gate, and explicitly NOT approved for HHT. So unlike the kit's other resolved diseases, HHT does NOT re-derive an approved targeted drug (none exists): it opens the vascular axis, fixes the corrective DIRECTION (restore the brake), and records honestly that current medicine offers only downstream off-label anti-angiogenics -- a deliberate DIVERGENCE between the switch logic and clinical reality, kept transparent rather than papered over (ledger B25). The gamma reads the ENG / ACVRL1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are haploinsufficiency (truncating / missense / deletion) coding/splice changes, outside the promoter firewall. SMAD4-related combined juvenile-polyposis-HHT is a distinct genotype, named-not-conflated. Magnitude [O].

Heterozygous LOF (haploinsufficiency) lowers that signalling -> the quiescence brake is released -> telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations (axis UP); HHT type 1. 9q34.11, OMIM 131195; HHT1 OMIM 187300. NCBI official symbol ENG. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the truncating/missense/deletion lesions are outside the promoter firewall.

facioscapulohumeral_muscular_dystrophy.suspended_reason: The cause is a D4Z4 MACROSATELLITE-REPEAT CONTRACTION with CHROMATIN DEREPRESSION of the DUX4 retrogene -- NOT a single-gene promoter switch. The D4Z4 array at 4q35 is normally heavily methylated and silenced. In FSHD1 (~95%) the array is CONTRACTED from the normal ~11-100 repeat units to 1-10 units, which lowers repeat-array methylation; in FSHD2 (~5%) loss-of-function of a chromatin repressor acting in trans on the array (SMCHD1, or DNMT3B / LRIF1) hypomethylates it. In BOTH cases, ONLY on a permissive distal 4qA haplotype that supplies a polyadenylation signal stabilising the DUX4 transcript from the last repeat unit, the normally-silenced DUX4 transcription factor is aberrantly expressed in skeletal muscle -> a toxic early-embryonic gene programme -> myofibre death (progressive facial, scapular and humeral weakness). The disease is therefore DEFINED by a repeat-array COPY-NUMBER + METHYLATION (chromatin) state plus a haplotype-supplied distal polyA signal -- there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read as a promoter switch: in FSHD1 there is no causal single-gene promoter lesion at all (the lesion is a repeat contraction), and in FSHD2 the causal change is a trans-acting chromatin-modifier's LOSS whose pathogenic effect is the downstream D4Z4/DUX4 derepression, not its own promoter threshold. A strand-symmetric single-promoter gamma read cannot capture macrosatellite copy number, array methylation, trans-acting chromatin state, or a haplotype-supplied polyA. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene promoter DNA -> hold). This is a FOURTH held mechanism class -- distinct from WHOLE-CHROMOSOME ANEUPLOIDY (Down), LARGE-REGION IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman 15q11-q13, Beckwith-Wiedemann 11p15.5), and now REPEAT-CONTRACTION / CHROMATIN-DEREPRESSION (D4Z4 / DUX4) -- demonstrating the suspension rule generalises across the major non-single-gene lesion mechanisms (aneuploidy, imprinting, repeat-derepression). A repeat-array / chromatin-state / DUX4-derepression model is future work, not a single-switch emergence.
facioscapulohumeral_muscular_dystrophy.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- D4Z4 repeat-contraction / DUX4 chromatin-derepression, not a single-gene promoter switch)

choroideremia.summary: An X-linked progressive chorioretinal degeneration. Loss-of-function of CHM -- which encodes Rab Escort Protein 1 (REP1) -- removes a positive intracellular-maintenance DRIVE: REP1 presents newly synthesised Rab GTPases to Rab geranylgeranyl transferase for prenylation (geranylgeranylation), the lipid modification REQUIRED for Rab membrane attachment and vesicular trafficking. Without REP1 a subset of Rabs (notably Rab27a) is left under-prenylated; the autosomal paralogue REP2 (CHML) partially compensates in most tissues, which is WHY the lesion is largely restricted to the eye (retinal pigment epithelium, photoreceptors, choroid) where REP1 is rate-limiting -> progressive degeneration of choroid + RPE + photoreceptors -> night blindness in youth, concentric peripheral-field constriction, eventual central-vision loss. The disease is read as the photoreceptor/RPE Rab-prenylation / vesicular-trafficking maintenance throughput axis driven DOWN (a positive maintenance driver whose loss starves retinal homeostasis -- the drive-lost shape). This is the kit's THIRD OCULAR read and its THIRD distinct ocular GENE CLASS: where LCA2 (RPE65) is a retinoid-CYCLE ENZYME deficiency and XLRP (RPGR) is a ciliary-TRAFFICKING / outer-segment-maintenance deficiency, choroideremia (CHM/REP1) is a Rab-PRENYLATION / vesicular-trafficking maintenance deficiency -- three different molecular machines in the same retina, whose lead corrective lever is nonetheless the same class, gene restoration. Correction is to restore the gene at the locus: replace CHM (subretinal AAV2-REP1 gene transfer). IMPORTANT HONESTY: there is at present NO approved therapy for choroideremia. The lead clinical agent is timrepigene emparvovec (AAV2-REP1 / BIIB111), whose phase 3 STAR trial DID NOT MEET its primary endpoint AND did not demonstrate efficacy on key secondary endpoints, so the kit ships this read in the SAME honest pattern as Huntington disease and XLRP (a DNA-readable disease whose lead gene-replacement agent is genuinely clinical-not-approved). The firewall makes this clean: the emerged switch FORCES the corrective DIRECTION = restore CHM/REP1 [F], which the lead agent matches; the EFFICACY / MAGNITUDE is [O] -- and the STAR primary/secondary-endpoint result is exactly a magnitude question, recorded honestly, not asserted. Antioxidant / vitamin supplementation is a supportive NON-lever (does not halt the degeneration). The gamma read is of the CHM locus switch STRUCTURE (Xq21.2, AT-leaning); the disease lesions are predominantly nonsense / frameshift / splice coding changes, outside the promoter firewall. X-linked (hemizygous males affected; carrier females show patchy fundus changes by X-inactivation, held [O]). Magnitude [O].
choroideremia.emergent_axis: photoreceptor / RPE / choroid Rab-prenylation-dependent intracellular vesicular-trafficking maintenance (REP1-supported Rab geranylgeranylation) -- a THIRD ocular axis, the Rab-prenylation/vesicular-trafficking contrast to LCA2's retinoid-cycle enzyme axis and XLRP's ciliary-trafficking axis

causal_genes.note: CHM encodes Rab Escort Protein 1 (REP1), which presents nascent Rab GTPases to Rab geranylgeranyl transferase (RGGT) for prenylation -- the obligate lipid modification that lets Rabs associate with membranes and drive vesicular trafficking -- a positive maintenance DRIVE for retinal/RPE homeostasis. LOF (nonsense / frameshift / splice alleles) leaves a subset of Rabs (esp. Rab27a) under-prenylated; REP2 (CHML) partially substitutes elsewhere, so degeneration is largely confined to choroid, RPE and photoreceptors -> choroideremia. Located Xq21.2. NCBI official symbol CHM. X-linked. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.

context_genes.note: CHML encodes REP2, the autosomal paralogue of REP1 that prenylates an overlapping Rab set and PARTIALLY COMPENSATES in non-retinal tissues -- the molecular reason choroideremia is retina-restricted despite CHM being ubiquitously expressed. It frames the trafficking axis but is not the lead-lever target.
context_genes.src: Cremers 1994 PNAS 91:11512 (CHML / REP2 paralogue, partial functional redundancy with REP1)

congenital_hyperinsulinism.summary: The commonest cause of persistent neonatal hypoglycaemia, defined by inactivating mutations of the two subunits of the beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium (K_ATP) channel: KCNJ11 (Kir6.2, the pore-forming subunit) and ABCC8 (SUR1, the sulfonylurea-receptor regulatory subunit), two ADJACENT genes on 11p15.1. The K_ATP channel couples cytosolic ATP/ADP to membrane potential: at low glucose it is OPEN (the beta-cell is hyperpolarised and insulin secretion is off); a glucose rise raises ATP, CLOSES the channel, depolarises the cell and triggers insulin release. The channel is therefore the repolarising BRAKE on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Loss-of-function of either subunit leaves the channel unable to open, so the beta-cell is tonically depolarised and secretes insulin INDEPENDENT of glucose -> hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia (macrosomia at birth, severe recurrent hypoglycaemia, risk of hypoglycaemic brain injury). The disease is read as the beta-cell K_ATP channel conductance axis driven DOWN (channel LOF -> the gate is stuck in the OFF basin, the repolarising K+ current is lost); the downstream consequence is unregulated insulin secretion UP. This is the cystic-fibrosis PATTERN (channel / LOF -> axis DOWN -> POTENTIATE the channel) carried onto a DIFFERENT channel and a DIFFERENT axis: where CF is an epithelial chloride-TRANSPORT channel (CFTR), this is a REGULATED-SECRETION ion channel (K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2) -- the kit's first regulated-hormone-secretion channel axis. It is also the kit's SIXTH two-causal-gene convergence (after HCM, sitosterolaemia, cystinuria, TSC and HHT): two subunits of ONE obligate channel, adjacent on the same chromosomal band, with KCNJ11 / Kir6.2 (the PORE) the deeper promoter switch over ABCC8 / SUR1. Correction is to POTENTIATE the channel: the K_ATP-channel opener diazoxide (Proglycem) acts on SUR1 to re-open the channel, restoring the repolarising conductance the LOF removed and curbing glucose-independent insulin release -- the approved first-line medical therapy, which the emerged switch independently re-derives. IMPORTANT HONESTY: diazoxide opens RESIDUAL / trafficking-competent channels, so the very forms most attributable to these two genes -- biallelic recessive (channel-NULL or trafficking-defective) ABCC8 / KCNJ11 disease -- are characteristically DIAZOXIDE-UNRESPONSIVE and are managed by near-total pancreatectomy (focal lesions, arising by paternal-allele loss-of-heterozygosity, can be cured by focal resection); dominant / milder K_ATP alleles are often diazoxide-responsive. So the lead lever is APPROVED but GENOTYPE-LIMITED: the corrective DIRECTION (restore K_ATP conductance) is forced [F], the realised RESPONSIVENESS / MAGNITUDE is [O] and depends on whether functional channels remain. This is the honest approved-but-partial contrast to the same release's choroideremia (a clinical-not-approved gene therapy). Somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide) and glucose-raising agents act DOWNSTREAM of the channel and are recorded as NON-levers on this switch axis; the non-channel hyperinsulinism genes (GLUD1, HADH, GCK ...) are a separate, characteristically diazoxide-RESPONSIVE class, framed as context. The gamma read is of the KCNJ11 / ABCC8 locus switch STRUCTURE (11p15.1); the disease lesions are coding (null / missense / trafficking / splice), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
congenital_hyperinsulinism.emergent_axis: beta-cell ATP-sensitive K+ (K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2) channel conductance -- the repolarising brake on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion; LOF closes the gate (K+ current lost) so the beta-cell cannot repolarise -> sustained depolarisation -> voltage-gated Ca2+ influx -> unregulated insulin release (hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia). The kit's first regulated-secretion ion-channel axis, the secretory contrast to CFTR's epithelial-transport channel axis

causal_genes.note: KCNJ11 encodes Kir6.2, the inward-rectifier K+ channel PORE-forming subunit of the beta-cell K_ATP channel (an octamer of four Kir6.2 + four SUR1). Inactivating (LOF) Kir6.2 mutations leave the channel unable to open, tonically depolarising the beta-cell so insulin is secreted independent of glucose -> hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia. Recessive (biallelic) LOF gives the most severe, diazoxide-unresponsive diffuse disease; dominant alleles are milder and often diazoxide-responsive. Located 11p15.1, adjacent to ABCC8. NCBI official symbol KCNJ11. The deeper promoter switch of the pair (the pore). HHF2 = OMIM 601820. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Nichols 1996 Science 272:1785 (SUR1 + Kir6.2 reconstitute the beta-cell K_ATP channel; diazoxide opener); Thomas 1996 Hum Mol Genet 5:1809 (KCNJ11 in familial persistent hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia of infancy); Bellanne-Chantelot 2010 J Med Genet 47:752 (ABCC8 / KCNJ11 spectrum)

causal_genes.note: ABCC8 encodes SUR1, the sulfonylurea-receptor regulatory subunit of the same K_ATP channel (the ABC-protein partner of Kir6.2; the two genes lie adjacent on 11p15.1). SUR1 confers MgADP nucleotide sensitivity and is the binding subunit for the channel-OPENER diazoxide and for sulfonylureas. LOF of SUR1 disables channel opening exactly as Kir6.2 LOF does -> the same hyperinsulinism; SUR1 is the more common cause overall. Recessive biallelic LOF -> severe, often diazoxide-unresponsive disease (diffuse, or focal via paternal-allele loss-of-heterozygosity). Located 11p15.1. NCBI official symbol ABCC8. HHF1 = OMIM 256450. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Thomas 1995 Science 268:426 (ABCC8 / SUR1 in familial persistent hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia); Bellanne-Chantelot 2010 J Med Genet 47:752; Snider 2013 J Clin Endocrinol Metab 98:E355 (KATP-HI genotype / diazoxide-responsiveness)

context_genes.note: GLUD1 (glutamate dehydrogenase) is the next-most-common congenital-hyperinsulinism gene -- a GAIN-of-function metabolic (non-channel) cause (the hyperinsulinism-hyperammonaemia syndrome) that is characteristically DIAZOXIDE-RESPONSIVE. It frames the diazoxide-responsiveness contrast: the K_ATP-channelopathy (ABCC8 / KCNJ11) is frequently diazoxide-UNRESPONSIVE, whereas the non-channel forms (GLUD1, HADH, ...) are typically responsive, because diazoxide can only open channels that still exist. Not the lead-lever target here.

Diazoxide (Proglycem) approved for hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia

leber_hereditary_optic_neuropathy.suspended_reason: The cause is a MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME (mtDNA) POINT MUTATION -- most commonly m.11778G>A in MT-ND4 (~60-80% worldwide), with m.3460G>A (MT-ND1) and m.14484T>C (MT-ND6) making up most of the remainder -- in genes of respiratory-chain Complex I, NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. Three features place it outside the kit's read. (1) The lesion is in the ~16.6-kb circular MITOCHONDRIAL genome, which is transcribed as long POLYCISTRONIC transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy/light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS-2000..+500 promoter window for MT-ND4 from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA protein genes have no such promoter). (2) Penetrance is HETEROPLASMY-dependent and incomplete -- only a minority of carriers of a primary mutation ever lose vision (markedly more often male than female, with partial spontaneous recovery in a subset, plus nuclear-background, mitochondrial-haplogroup and environmental modifiers) -- a continuous, tissue-variable quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance is MATERNAL (mitochondrial), not Mendelian. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). This is a FIFTH held mechanism class -- distinct from WHOLE-CHROMOSOME ANEUPLOIDY (Down), parent-of-origin IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman 15q11-q13; Beckwith-Wiedemann 11p15.5), and REPEAT-CONTRACTION / CHROMATIN-DEREPRESSION (FSHD D4Z4 / DUX4) -- proving the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM and now generalises to the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME. SHARPEST DISCIPLINE POINT: LHON is suspended DESPITE having an APPROVED drug -- idebenone (Raxone), a coenzyme-Q10 analogue approved for LHON in the EU, Israel, South Korea and elsewhere (US FDA priority review pending as of early 2026) -- and active gene-therapy programmes (intravitreal allotopically expressed MT-ND4, e.g. lenadogene nolparvovec). Idebenone acts DOWNSTREAM (antioxidant / electron-carrier support of retinal ganglion cells) and does not address the mtDNA lesion. The suspension therefore keys purely on whether the ENGINE can READ the lesion (an mtDNA point mutation with no nuclear promoter window, plus heteroplasmy), NOT on whether a therapy exists -- the discipline is about engine-readability, not therapeutic availability. (This is the inverse of the Huntington/XLRP/choroideremia pattern, where the DNA is readable but the lead therapy is unproven: here a therapy is approved but the DNA is unreadable by a nuclear-promoter engine.) An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / Complex-I model is future work, not a single-(nuclear)-switch emergence.
leber_hereditary_optic_neuropathy.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- mitochondrial-genome MT-ND4 / MT-ND1 / MT-ND6 point mutation + heteroplasmy, not a single-gene nuclear promoter switch)

long_qt_syndrome_3.disease: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3; SCN5A gain-of-function, late sodium current)
long_qt_syndrome_3.summary: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3) is the cardiac-sodium-channel form of congenital long QT syndrome, caused by GAIN-of-function mutations in SCN5A, which encodes the alpha-subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5 (chr3p22.2). NaV1.5 normally opens to drive the rapid upstroke of the ventricular action potential and then INACTIVATES; LQT3 GOF alleles impair inactivation (the deltaKPQ in-frame deletion is the classic example) and leave a small persistent LATE sodium current (late INa) flowing during the plateau. That extra inward depolarising charge PROLONGS the action-potential duration and the QT interval, predisposing to torsades de pointes and sudden cardiac death (events characteristically at rest / during sleep). The kit reads this as the cardiac late-sodium-current / repolarisation axis driven UP (channel GOF -> the gate fails to stay in the OFF / inactivated basin -> a runaway persistent current), the action-potential-prolonging drive OVER-shooting. This is the kit's FIRST cardiac ION-CHANNEL axis (distinct from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy's MECHANICAL / contractile cardiac axis) and its FIRST channel GAIN-of-function read: where the two prior channel reads are LOSS-of-function channels restored by POTENTIATION (CFTR in cystic fibrosis; the K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2 channel in congenital hyperinsulinism, both axis DOWN -> potentiate), LQT3 is a channel whose EXCESS current must be RESTRAINED (axis UP -> restrain) -- a NEW channel-lever class, the channel analogue of the gain-of-toxicity reads (HCM hypercontractility, Wilson copper). Correction is to RESTRAIN the late sodium current: mexiletine, an approved late-INa-blocking class-IB antiarrhythmic, is the GENE-SPECIFIC therapy for LQT3 -- it preferentially blocks the persistent late current, shortens the QT interval and reduces life-threatening arrhythmic events, and the emerged switch independently re-derives it (Mazzanti 2016 JACC). IMPORTANT HONESTY: the response is GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- some SCN5A alleles are mexiletine-SENSITIVE and others mexiletine-INSENSITIVE (the biophysics of the specific inactivation defect determine sensitivity), so the corrective DIRECTION (block the excess late INa) is forced [F] while the realised QTc-shortening MAGNITUDE is [O]; an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator remains the mainstay for high-risk patients (not a switch lever). beta-blockers (nadolol / propranolol), the first-line therapy for LQTS OVERALL, are recorded here as a DOWNSTREAM NON-lever on this switch axis: they act by an anti-adrenergic mechanism rather than blocking the late current, are less effective in LQT3 than in LQT1 / LQT2, and can even be pro-arrhythmic in LQT3 by slowing the heart rate -- the Rett / trofinetide downstream-agent discipline. The OTHER major LQTS genes are framed as CONTEXT, deliberately NOT as a convergence: KCNQ1 (LQT1, the slow-delayed-rectifier IKs potassium channel) and KCNH2 / hERG (LQT2, the rapid-delayed-rectifier IKr potassium channel) are LOSS-of-function POTASSIUM channels -- the OPPOSITE channel-level mechanism to SCN5A's gain (a K-current DOWN vs an Na-current UP, both prolonging QT by lowering the net repolarising balance). They CANNOT be folded into one convergent switch read because their channel-level directions are opposite -- a clean demonstration that the kit reads the (gene x mechanism), not the syndrome label, and that the lead therapy is correspondingly GENE-SPECIFIC. The gamma read is of the SCN5A promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3p22.2); the disease lesions are coding (the deltaKPQ deletion; inactivation-impairing missense alleles), outside the promoter firewall. The same gene's LOSS-of-function alleles cause a DISTINCT disease (Brugada syndrome / conduction disease) -- a different (mechanism) read not conflated here. Magnitude [O].
long_qt_syndrome_3.emergent_axis: cardiac late sodium current (late INa) through NaV1.5 / ventricular action-potential repolarisation -- the SCN5A channel normally inactivates after the upstroke; GOF alleles leave a persistent late INa during the plateau, extra inward depolarising charge that PROLONGS the action-potential duration and QT interval (the gate over-stays the conducting state -> a runaway late current). The kit's first cardiac ion-channel axis and first channel gain-of-function (axis UP / restrain) read, the channel contrast to the LOF channels restored by potentiation (CFTR, K_ATP)

causal_genes.note: SCN5A encodes NaV1.5, the pore-forming alpha-subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel that drives the action-potential upstroke and then inactivates. LQT3 GAIN-of-function alleles impair inactivation, leaving a persistent LATE sodium current (late INa) during the plateau that prolongs repolarisation (the deltaKPQ deletion is the classic example). chr3p22.2. NCBI official symbol SCN5A. LQT3 = OMIM 603830. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.
causal_genes.src: Wang 1995 Cell 80:805 (SCN5A deltaKPQ in LQT3, persistent late INa); Bennett 1995 Nature 376:683 (impaired inactivation, sustained inward current); Mazzanti 2016 J Am Coll Cardiol 67:1053 (mexiletine reduces arrhythmic events in LQT3)

context_genes.note: KCNQ1 (KvLQT1) encodes the alpha-subunit of the slow delayed-rectifier potassium channel (IKs); LOSS-of-function causes LQT1 (the commonest LQTS), where the lost repolarising K+ current prolongs QT -- the OPPOSITE channel-level mechanism to SCN5A's Na-current gain. beta-blockers are highly effective in LQT1. chr11p15.5-15.4. Framed as context: a K-channel LOF arm that cannot be folded into the SCN5A Na-channel GOF switch read.
context_genes.src: Wang 1996 Nat Genet 12:17 (KCNQ1 / KvLQT1 in LQT1)

context_genes.note: KCNH2 / hERG encodes the alpha-subunit of the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium channel (IKr); LOSS-of-function causes LQT2 -- again a lost repolarising K+ current prolonging QT (and the channel most often blocked in acquired / drug-induced long QT). The OPPOSITE channel-level mechanism to SCN5A. chr7q36.1. Framed as context.

An ICD remains the mainstay for high-risk patients (not a switch lever).

dravet_syndrome.disease: Dravet syndrome (SCN1A; NaV1.1 loss-of-function, GABAergic-interneuron haploinsufficiency)
dravet_syndrome.summary: Dravet syndrome (severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy) is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused in >80% of cases by heterozygous LOSS-of-function (de novo) mutations in SCN1A, which encodes the neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel alpha-subunit NaV1.1 (chr2q24.3). NaV1.1 is expressed predominantly in fast-spiking GABAergic INHIBITORY interneurons (notably parvalbumin-positive interneurons); SCN1A haploinsufficiency lowers NaV1.1, so these interneurons cannot sustain high-frequency firing -> GABAergic inhibition collapses -> cortical networks are DISINHIBITED -> treatment-resistant seizures from the first year of life, with developmental regression, intellectual disability, features of autism and the highest known risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). The kit reads this as the interneuron NaV1.1 sodium-channel current / inhibitory-tone axis driven DOWN (channel LOF -> too few channels, the gate's current is effectively lost -> the interneuron's repetitive-firing current is deficient); the downstream consequence is network excitation UP, but the SWITCH-LEVEL lesion is a loss of inhibitory drive. This is the cystic-fibrosis / K_ATP channel-LOF PATTERN (channel / LOF -> axis DOWN -> restore the channel) carried onto a NEURONAL voltage-gated sodium channel, and it forms a clean MIRROR PAIR with the same release's LQT3 (SCN5A): both are voltage-gated SODIUM channels of the same family, but in OPPOSITE organs (brain interneuron NaV1.1 vs heart NaV1.5), with OPPOSITE mechanisms (LOF vs GOF), OPPOSITE axis (DOWN vs UP) and OPPOSITE levers (restore vs restrain) -- the channelopathy analogue of the Wilson / Menkes copper pair and the SMA / SOD1-ALS motor-neuron pair. IMPORTANT (the honest discipline point): the corrective direction is to RESTORE NaV1.1, but there is NO approved drug that does so -- the switch-level lever is INVESTIGATIONAL. Zorevunersen (STK-001), an antisense oligonucleotide using TANGO (targeted augmentation of nuclear gene output) to suppress a non-productive poison-exon splice event and so UPREGULATE NaV1.1 from the healthy SCN1A allele, is in Phase 3 (EMPEROR); interneuron-targeted dual-AAV split-intein SCN1A gene replacement (e.g. DLX2.0-SCN1A) is preclinical. The APPROVED Dravet drugs -- fenfluramine (Fintepla), cannabidiol (Epidiolex) and stiripentol (Diacomit) -- are recorded as DOWNSTREAM NON-levers on this switch axis: they reduce seizure frequency by serotonergic / endocannabinoid / GABAergic-augmenting and metabolic mechanisms that do NOT restore NaV1.1; treatment remains palliative and there is no cure -- the Rett / trofinetide downstream-agent discipline. So this is the Huntington / XLRP pattern (a resolved, DNA-readable disease whose lead SWITCH-corrective agent is genuinely investigational, direction [F] / adequacy [O]). A timing caveat is honestly noted: NaV1.1 upregulation may be most effective applied early, before chronic circuit rearrangements set in (a magnitude / timing question, [O]). NOTE the sodium-channel-BLOCKER caveat that follows DIRECTLY from the switch read: because the lesion is a LOSS of the inhibitory sodium current, classic sodium-channel BLOCKERS (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine) tend to WORSEN Dravet seizures -- the engine's axis-DOWN read predicts exactly this contraindication (blocking the already-deficient channel pushes the axis further down), a clean falsifiable consequence. Structural note: SCN1A's promoter gamma 1.2450 (chr2q24.3, AT-rich) is the SECOND-LOWEST gamma in the kit (below only DMD's 1.2388, above F9's 1.2627) -- a shallow-barrier switch. The gamma read is of the SCN1A promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding / truncating / splice (and ~10% large deletions), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

The kit's first NEURONAL ion-channel (epilepsy) axis, the inhibitory-interneuron contrast to LQT3's cardiac NaV1.5 gain

melas.disease: MELAS (mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, stroke-like episodes; m.3243A>G in MT-TL1)
melas.suspended_reason: The cause is a MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME (mtDNA) POINT MUTATION -- in ~80% of MELAS, m.3243A>G in MT-TL1, the gene encoding the mitochondrial transfer RNA for leucine, tRNA-Leu(UUR) (the remainder including m.3271T>C in the same tRNA and m.13513G>A in MT-ND5) -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. The three features that suspend LHON all apply, and a NEW one sharpens the point. (1) The lesion is in the ~16.6-kb circular MITOCHONDRIAL genome, transcribed as long POLYCISTRONIC transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy / light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS -2000..+500 promoter window for MT-TL1 from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA genes have no such promoter). (2) Penetrance is HETEROPLASMY-dependent and tissue-variable -- the mutant load differs between tissues and over time, and (unlike a Mendelian switch) leukocyte heteroplasmy correlates poorly with clinical severity; the SAME m.3243A>G also produces a clinically DISTINCT maternally-inherited diabetes-and-deafness (MIDD) phenotype at lower loads -- a continuous, multi-outcome quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance is MATERNAL (mitochondrial), not Mendelian. (4) THE NEW, SHARPER POINT vs LHON: MT-TL1 is a mitochondrial tRNA GENE, not a protein-coding subunit gene. Where LHON's suspended lesions sit in PROTEIN-CODING Complex I subunit genes (MT-ND4 / MT-ND1 / MT-ND6), the MELAS lesion disables a piece of the mitochondrial TRANSLATION machinery itself: the m.3243A>G tRNA-Leu(UUR) defect (loss of the wobble taurine modification / impaired aminoacylation / reduced tRNA-ribosome association) globally impairs synthesis of ALL thirteen mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS proteins -> Complex I deficiency -> energy failure in high-demand neurons and myocytes (stroke-like episodes, lactic acidosis, encephalomyopathy). So MELAS is the SECOND mtDNA suspend and it GENERALISES the mitochondrial-genome hold ACROSS mtDNA GENE CLASSES -- from a protein-coding subunit gene (LHON) to a mitochondrial tRNA gene (MELAS) -- the within-class generalisation analogue of how Beckwith-Wiedemann (11p15.5) generalised the IMPRINTING hold beyond Prader-Willi / Angelman's 15q11-q13: NOT a brand-new mechanism class, but proof the mtDNA hold keys on the MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME mechanism regardless of whether the mtDNA gene is protein-coding or a tRNA. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). Like LHON, MELAS is suspended NOT for lack of any therapy but purely on engine-readability: management is supportive (the acute stroke-like episodes are treated with L-arginine; high-dose taurine -- aimed at restoring the missing tRNA wobble modification -- is approved for MELAS in Japan; CoQ10 / cofactor 'mito-cocktails' are used), and experimental approaches exist (allotopically expressed / mitochondrially-imported corrective tRNA; mitochondrially-targeted nucleases to shift heteroplasmy), but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / translation-defect model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (Goto 1990 Nature 348:651, m.3243A>G in MELAS.)
melas.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- mitochondrial-genome MT-TL1 tRNA-Leu(UUR) point mutation + heteroplasmy, not a single-gene nuclear promoter switch)

rho_autosomal_dominant_retinitis_pigment.disease: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, RHO-related (adRP; RHO toxic gain-of-function / rhodopsin misfolding, e.g. P23H)
rho_autosomal_dominant_retinitis_pigment.summary: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP) is the dominantly-inherited form of the commonest inherited retinal dystrophy, and RHO -- the gene encoding rhodopsin, the light-sensing G-protein-coupled receptor of the rod photoreceptor outer segment (chr3q22.1) -- is its single commonest cause (~20-30% of adRP). More than 200 RHO alleles are known; the disease is mechanistically heterogeneous, but the dominant, classic and most-studied class is a TOXIC GAIN-of-function (class II), epitomised by P23H: the mutant opsin MISFOLDS, is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, overwhelms proteostasis and exerts a dominant-negative / cytotoxic aggregation gain on the rod, driving progressive rod-then-cone death and concentric visual-field loss. The kit reads this with the PROTEINOPATHY pattern it already uses for Huntington (HTT), transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR) and SOD1-ALS: the toxic misfolded species acts as an OVER-ACTIVE pathological BRAKE suppressing photoreceptor homeostasis (role brake, mechanism GOF -> emergent axis DOWN on photoreceptor maintenance throughput), the burden to be REMOVED rather than a lost function to be supplied. Correction is therefore to REDUCE the toxic mutant rhodopsin: mutation-specific knockdown of the mutant allele -- e.g. the P23H-directed antisense oligonucleotide QR-1123 (which lowers toxic mutant-protein accumulation and reached a Phase 1/2 trial), allele-specific CRISPR/RNAi -- and mutation-agnostic 'ablate-and-replace' (knock down endogenous RHO and supply a resistant wild-type copy, e.g. the dual-AAV EDIT-103, preclinical) all push the toxic-species axis the corrective way (reduce the poison). HONESTLY: there is NO approved drug or gene therapy for RHO-adRP anywhere; the lead corrective agents are clinical-not-approved or preclinical, so the kit ships this in the SAME honest shape as Huntington, X-linked RP and choroideremia (DNA readable, lead lever NOT a clean approved switch-drug; direction [F], magnitude [O]) -- the Huntington pattern, now its FOURTH instance. This is the kit's FOURTH ocular read and its FIRST ocular PROTEINOPATHY: where LCA2 (RPE65) is a retinoid-CYCLE ENZYME deficiency, X-linked RP (RPGR) is a ciliary-TRAFFICKING deficiency and choroideremia (CHM/REP1) is a Rab-PRENYLATION deficiency -- three LOSS reads on three different retinal machines -- RHO-adRP is the FIRST ocular read whose lesion is a toxic GAIN (a misfolded protein), and the FIRST ocular AUTOSOMAL-DOMINANT read (the prior three are recessive or X-linked). It also sharpens a within-kit contrast: rhodopsin is literally a light-sensing GPCR, so RHO-adRP is a GPCR-GENE read carried as a proteinopathy, the toxic-GAIN counterpart to the same release's AVPR2 nephrogenic-DI read (a signalling-GPCR LOSS). Mechanistic heterogeneity is recorded honestly: a MINORITY of RHO adRP alleles act by LOF / haploinsufficiency (class I null / dominant-negative), for which the toxic-reduce read does not apply -- so the read is clean for the toxic-GOF majority but allele-contested (direction_confidence cited-contested). The gamma read is of the RHO promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3q22.1); the disease lesions (P23H and the other >200 coding alleles) are coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

The kit's first ocular proteinopathy and first toxic-GAIN ocular read, the gain contrast to the three loss-of-function ocular reads (RPE65 enzyme, RPGR cilia, CHM Rab-prenylation)

The direction is therefore clean for the toxic-GOF majority but allele-class-contested (Athanasiou 2018 Prog Retin Eye Res 62:1; Mendes 2005 Trends Mol Med 11:177 -- RHO mutation classes I-VII).

nephrogenic_diabetes_insipidus_x_linked.disease: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, X-linked (AVPR2 loss-of-function; vasopressin V2 receptor)
nephrogenic_diabetes_insipidus_x_linked.summary: X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI) is caused by INACTIVATING (loss-of-function) mutations of AVPR2, the gene encoding the arginine-vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) -- a Gs-coupled G-PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTOR on the basolateral membrane of the renal collecting-duct principal cell (chrXq28). In health, circulating vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) binds V2R, which activates Gs -> adenylate cyclase -> cAMP -> PKA, driving aquaporin-2 (AQP2) water channels to the apical membrane so water is reabsorbed and urine is concentrated. AVPR2 LOF (the majority are MISSENSE mutations whose receptor MISFOLDS and is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, never reaching the membrane) abolishes that vasopressin-driven cAMP signal: the collecting duct cannot insert AQP2 and cannot concentrate urine despite high or therapeutic vasopressin -> massive dilute polyuria, polydipsia, recurrent hypernatraemic dehydration. The kit reads this as the V2R -> cAMP -> AQP2 water-reabsorption DRIVE removed (role accelerator -- the hormone-response drive -- mechanism LOF -> emergent axis DOWN on urine-concentrating throughput), the SAME accelerator/LOF/axis-DOWN shape as leptin-receptor deficiency (LEPR), now on a different receptor and a different axis. This is the kit's FIRST GPCR axis and its FIRST receptor-signalling / second-messenger (cAMP) axis -- distinct from the kit's ION-CHANNEL receptor reads (CFTR, K_ATP, NaV1.5/NaV1.1): those are channels carrying a current, V2R is a metabotropic GPCR transducing a hormone into a second messenger. Correction is to RESTORE the V2R -> cAMP -> AQP2 drive. Because most AVPR2 mutants are MISFOLDED-but-intrinsically-functional receptors trapped in the ER, the lead switch-level direction is to RESCUE the receptor's folding/trafficking so it reaches the membrane and signals again: cell-permeant non-peptide pharmacological CHAPERONES (some of which are also biased AGONISTS that directly restore an AVP-dependent cAMP signal on the rescued mutant) do exactly this in vitro and in early proof-of-concept (the V1a/V2 antagonist-chaperone SR49059 / relcovaptan reduced 24-h urine volume in a small NDI patient study; SR121463 and biased-agonist pharmacochaperones rescue many V2R mutants in cell systems). HONESTLY: this is a research strategy, NOT an approved or actively-developed therapy -- no pharmacochaperone is approved for NDI, the chaperone approach rescues MISSENSE/misfolding mutants but NOT nonsense/null alleles (genotype-dependent), and AVPR2 gene/function restoration is preclinical. So the kit ships this as the Huntington pattern (DNA readable, lead switch-level lever investigational, not a clean approved switch-drug; direction [F], magnitude [O]). The conventional clinical MANAGEMENT -- thiazide diuretics + amiloride, a low-solute (low-salt, reduced-protein) diet, and NSAIDs (indomethacin) -- reduces urine volume by paradoxical / prostaglandin mechanisms that do NOT restore V2R signalling, so it is recorded as DOWNSTREAM-symptomatic and is deliberately NOT added as a switch lever (the Rett/trofinetide, XLH/oral-phosphate, HPP/vitamin-D downstream-agent discipline). The AUTOSOMAL-recessive/-dominant forms of NDI, caused by AQP2 mutations (the downstream water channel), are a distinct genotype on the SAME axis (the receptor vs the channel) -- AQP2 is carried as context, not conflated. The gamma read is of the AVPR2 promoter switch STRUCTURE (chrXq28); the disease lesions (missense/misfolding, nonsense, deletions) are coding, outside the promoter firewall. X-linked: hemizygous males affected, carrier females variable by X-inactivation (held [O], the B10 convention). Magnitude [O].
nephrogenic_diabetes_insipidus_x_linked.emergent_axis: renal collecting-duct urine-concentrating drive -- the vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) -> Gs -> cAMP -> PKA -> AQP2 apical water-channel insertion axis. AVPR2 LOF (mostly receptor misfolding / ER retention) removes the vasopressin-response drive so water reabsorption fails despite hormone (axis DOWN). The kit's first GPCR axis and first second-messenger (cAMP) receptor-signalling axis, the metabotropic-GPCR contrast to the ion-channel reads (CFTR, K_ATP, NaV)

The corrective direction (restore V2R signalling) is correspondingly clean; only the realised magnitude / chaperone-responsiveness is genotype-dependent ([O]).

kearns_sayre_syndrome.disease: Kearns-Sayre syndrome / single large-scale mitochondrial-DNA deletion (KSS; e.g. the ~4977-bp 'common deletion')
kearns_sayre_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a SINGLE LARGE-SCALE DELETION of the MITOCHONDRIAL genome (mtDNA) -- most commonly the ~4977-bp 'common deletion' spanning from ND5 to ATP8, which removes SEVERAL protein-coding OXPHOS genes AND several mitochondrial tRNA genes at once -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. This GENERALISES the kit's mitochondrial-genome hold along a NEW axis -- the LESION-TYPE axis -- from POINT MUTATION to STRUCTURAL REARRANGEMENT. The mtDNA hold previously fired for two POINT mutations: LHON (protein-coding Complex I subunit genes, MT-ND4/ND1/ND6) and MELAS (a mitochondrial tRNA gene, MT-TL1) -- a within-class generalisation across mtDNA gene CLASSES. Kearns-Sayre is the THIRD mtDNA suspend and extends the class once more: the lesion is not a base substitution at all but a large contiguous DELETION of a stretch of the circular ~16.6-kb mtDNA, simultaneously deleting multiple genes and tRNAs and crippling mitochondrial protein synthesis / OXPHOS in the tissues carrying a high deletion load (the KSS triad: progressive external ophthalmoplegia + pigmentary retinopathy + onset <20 yr, with cardiac conduction block, ataxia and raised CSF protein). The same three features that suspend LHON and MELAS all apply and a fourth sharpens the point. (1) The lesion is in the MITOCHONDRIAL genome, which is transcribed as long polycistronic transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy/light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS -2000..+500 promoter window from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA has no such promoter, and a multi-gene deletion has no single readable promoter at all). (2) Penetrance/phenotype is HETEROPLASMY- and tissue-distribution-dependent and continuous (the same single deletion produces a SPECTRUM by load and tissue: KSS, the milder isolated chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO), or Pearson marrow-pancreas syndrome) -- a continuous, multi-outcome quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance: single large-scale mtDNA deletions are almost always SPORADIC (arising de novo in the oocyte / early embryo), not Mendelian and (unlike point mutations) usually not maternally transmitted -- a different inheritance mode again. (4) THE NEW, SHARPER POINT vs LHON/MELAS: the lesion is a STRUCTURAL REARRANGEMENT (a large contiguous deletion removing many genes), not a point mutation in one gene -- so even the notion of 'the causal gene' dissolves: there is no single mtDNA gene, let alone a single nuclear promoter, to emerge. Kearns-Sayre therefore proves the mtDNA hold keys on the MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME mechanism regardless of LESION TYPE -- point substitution (LHON, MELAS) OR large structural deletion (KSS) -- NOT a brand-new mechanism class but the lesion-type generalisation of the mtDNA class (the structural-rearrangement analogue of how MELAS generalised LHON across mtDNA gene classes). Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). Like LHON and MELAS, Kearns-Sayre is suspended NOT for lack of any intervention but purely on engine-readability: management is supportive (CoQ10 and cofactor 'mito-cocktails'; cardiac PACING is mandatory and life-saving for the conduction block that defines the syndrome; hearing aids; endocrine surveillance), and heteroplasmy-shifting / mitochondrial-replacement approaches are experimental -- but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / structural-deletion model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (Holt 1988 Nature 331:717, deletions of mtDNA in mitochondrial myopathies; Zeviani 1988 Neurology 38:1339, KSS single large-scale mtDNA deletion.)
kearns_sayre_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- single large-scale mitochondrial-DNA DELETION removing multiple mtDNA genes + tRNAs + heteroplasmy, a structural mtDNA rearrangement, not a single-gene nuclear promoter switch)

usher_syndrome_type_2a.disease: Usher syndrome type 2A (USH2A loss-of-function; usherin, the photoreceptor periciliary-membrane / hair-cell ankle-link complex protein) -- combined congenital sensorineural hearing loss + retinitis pigmentosa
usher_syndrome_type_2a.summary: Usher syndrome type 2 is the commonest form of the commonest cause of combined deaf-blindness, and USH2A -- the gene encoding usherin, a very large (~5,200-residue) transmembrane protein of the photoreceptor PERICILIARY-MEMBRANE complex and the cochlear hair-cell stereocilia ANKLE-LINK region (chr1q41) -- is its single commonest cause (and also a leading cause of non-syndromic recessive retinitis pigmentosa). Usherin is a STRUCTURAL / adhesion scaffold: with ADGRV1 (the giant adhesion-GPCR VLGR1) and whirlin (WHRN) it builds the membrane-to-membrane link that organises the connecting cilium / periciliary region of the photoreceptor and the developing stereocilia bundle. Biallelic LOF (the single commonest allele is the exon-13 frameshift c.2299delG / p.Glu767fs, with c.2276G>T the other common exon-13 lesion) collapses that scaffold -> progressive rod-then-cone photoreceptor degeneration (retinitis pigmentosa) plus congenital, moderate-to-severe sensorineural HEARING LOSS (vestibular function spared in type 2, the type-1/type-2 distinction). The kit reads this with the STRUCTURAL-deficiency pattern it already uses for Duchenne (DMD) and spinal muscular atrophy (SMN1): a structural element is lost, so the maintained tissue integrity falls (role structural, mechanism LOF -> emergent axis DOWN on photoreceptor outer-segment / periciliary-complex maintenance throughput), a lost function to be SUPPLIED rather than a toxic species to be removed. Correction is therefore to RESTORE usherin function. Because the USH2A coding sequence (~15.6 kb) is far too large for a single AAV, the lead switch-level direction is NOT whole-gene replacement but to repair the transcript so a shortened-but-functional usherin is made: the antisense oligonucleotide ULTEVURSEN (QR-421a) induces skipping of the mutation-bearing exon 13 during pre-mRNA splicing, removing the lesion in-frame and yielding a usherin lacking only the exon-13-encoded segment but retaining residual function (the DMD exon-skip logic, lever `correct`). HONESTLY: there is NO approved targeted therapy for USH2A / Usher type 2A anywhere (Luxturna is RPE65-only); ultevursen completed a Phase 1/2 (Stellar) with acceptable tolerability and signals, its ProQR Phase 2/3 programme (Sirius / Celeste) was de-prioritised, and the asset is now in a Phase 2b trial (LUNA, Sepul Bio, NCT06627179) -- so it is held `clinical`, NOT approved, the SAME honest shape as Huntington / X-linked RP / choroideremia / RHO-adRP (DNA readable, lead lever not a clean approved switch-drug; direction [F], magnitude [O]) -- the Huntington pattern, now its FIFTH instance. A CRISPR exon-13-excision programme (EDIT-102, Editas/Allergan) is preclinical (a second `correct`-class arm). This is the kit's FIFTH ocular read and a FIFTH distinct ocular GENE CLASS: where LCA2 (RPE65) is a retinoid-cycle ENZYME, X-linked RP (RPGR) is a ciliary-trafficking GTPase-regulator, choroideremia (CHM/REP1) is a Rab-prenylation chaperone and RHO-adRP is a rhodopsin GPCR proteinopathy, USH2A is a PERICILIARY / ankle-link STRUCTURAL-ADHESION protein -- five ocular genes now span five molecular machine classes in one retinal read-set. It is also the FIRST SYNDROMIC (audio-VISUAL) ocular read in the kit (all four prior ocular reads are eye-only): usherin's dual role in the photoreceptor periciliary complex AND the cochlear hair-cell ankle-link is why one gene gives both RP and deafness. STRUCTURAL note: USH2A promoter gamma 1.2801 (AT-leaning, GC 0.39) is among the LOWEST in the kit -- it sits just above HBB 1.2779 and just below the other ocular AT-rich gene RPE65 1.2842, so the two lowest-gamma ocular promoters (USH2A, RPE65) are now adjacent. The gamma read is of the USH2A promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr1q41); the disease lesions (c.2299delG and the >1,000 other coding/splice alleles) are coding, outside the promoter firewall. direction_confidence = clean (structural x LOF -> axis DOWN gives an unambiguous corrective direction; only the realised exon-skip / vision-preservation MAGNITUDE is [O]). Magnitude [O].

nephrogenic_siad.disease: Nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (NSIAD) -- AVPR2 gain-of-function (constitutively-active vasopressin V2 receptor; e.g. R137C/R137L, F229V, I130N)
nephrogenic_siad.summary: Nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (NSIAD) is the EXACT GAIN-of-function MIRROR of X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, on the SAME gene -- AVPR2, encoding the arginine-vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R), the Gs-coupled GPCR of the renal collecting-duct principal cell (chrXq28). Where X-linked NDI is AVPR2 LOSS-of-function (the V2R->cAMP->AQP2 water-reabsorption drive removed -> the duct cannot concentrate urine -> dilute polyuria, axis DOWN), NSIAD is AVPR2 GAIN-of-function: activating mutations render the V2R CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE, so it signals cAMP -> PKA -> apical AQP2 insertion -> water reabsorption WITHOUT vasopressin. The clinical picture mimics the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIADH) -- hyponatraemia, concentrated urine, water retention -- but with UNDETECTABLE circulating vasopressin (hence NEPHROGENIC inappropriate antidiuresis), first described by Feldman 2005 (NEJM) in two male infants carrying R137C / R137L substitutions at the conserved DRY/DRH motif (TM3 / second intracellular loop). The kit reads this as the V2R->cAMP->AQP2 water-reabsorption DRIVE stuck ON (role accelerator -- the hormone-response drive -- mechanism GOF -> emergent axis UP on urine-concentrating throughput): the disease OVER-shoots and correction RESTRAINS the over-active receptor signal. This is the SAME cached AVPR2 promoter (gamma 1.4618) as X-linked NDI but the OPPOSITE perturbation, so the dwell ordering inverts -- NDI's disease dwell sits BELOW healthy, NSIAD's disease dwell sits ABOVE the same healthy value -- the EXACT analogue of the Rett (MECP2 LOF, axis DOWN) <-> MECP2-duplication (MECP2 GOF, axis UP) same-locus DIRECTION pair, now on a GPCR. It is the kit's SECOND GPCR / receptor-cAMP-signalling axis (consolidating the AVPR2 class opened by NDI) and COMPLETES the V2R axis in BOTH directions on one receptor (the GPCR analogue of the Wilson/Menkes copper pair, the LQT3/Dravet Na-channel pair, the haemophilia/antithrombin coagulation pair and the CLD/LEPR leptin pair). Correction = RESTRAIN the constitutive signal with a vaptan acting as an INVERSE AGONIST (e.g. tolvaptan), which suppresses the basal cAMP of the activated receptor and re-derives an APPROVED V2R-blocking drug as the direct on-target lever (target AVPR2 IS the primary switch). HONESTLY this is GENOTYPE-LIMITED, a beautifully sharp open-magnitude point: NSIAD constitutive activation comes in TWO molecular classes -- a VAPTAN-SENSITIVE class (F229V, I130N and others: high constitutive Gs/cAMP with normal/enhanced inverse-agonist responsiveness, so tolvaptan blocks the basal activity -- Tiulpakov 2016 showed tolvaptan suppresses the I130N mutant) and a VAPTAN-RESISTANT class confined to the Arg137 replacements (R137C/R137L: a sharp decline of ligand sensitivity at all transducer interactions, signalling partly through an alternative Rho-kinase/ROCK -> pT269-AQP2, beta-arrestin-2-biased route -- Ranieri 2020 -- so orthosteric vaptans do NOT suppress them). The Arg137 mutants are the COMMONEST NSIAD genotype, so although tolvaptan is the approved, on-target, mechanism-correct lever, its realised effect is GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT: vaptan-sensitive mutants respond, the common Arg137 mutants need an ALTERNATIVE (a ROCK-pathway restraint, investigational) -- the corrective DIRECTION (restrain the over-active V2R) is forced [F], the realised RESPONSIVENESS / magnitude is [O]. This is the honest approved-but-partial contrast to the same release's USH2A read (a clinical-not-approved Huntington-pattern lead) -- exactly as v0.22.0 paired choroideremia (clinical) with congenital hyperinsulinism (approved-but-genotype-limited). Fluid/osmolar restriction is supportive, not switch-level. direction_confidence = clean (accelerator x GOF -> axis UP gives an unambiguous corrective direction; the genotype-dependence is a MAGNITUDE/responsiveness [O] question, not a direction ambiguity -- exactly as NDI is clean despite genotype-dependent chaperone rescue). The gamma read is of the AVPR2 promoter switch STRUCTURE (chrXq28); the activating lesions (R137C/L, F229V, I130N) are coding, outside the promoter firewall. X-linked (hemizygous males; carrier females variable, B10 convention). Magnitude [O].

The corrective direction (restrain the over-active V2R) is correspondingly clean; only the realised RESPONSIVENESS is genotype-dependent (vaptan-sensitive F229V/I130N vs vaptan-resistant Arg137) -- a magnitude question [O], not a direction ambiguity.

digeorge_22q11_2_deletion_syndrome.disease: DiGeorge / velocardiofacial syndrome -- 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (contiguous-gene microdeletion, typically the ~2.5-3 Mb LCR22A-D deletion encompassing ~40 genes incl. TBX1)
digeorge_22q11_2_deletion_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a CONTIGUOUS-GENE MICRODELETION -- a heterozygous SUB-CHROMOSOMAL deletion of chromosome band 22q11.2 (most commonly the ~2.5-3 Mb LCR22A-D interval, ~85-90% of cases) that removes APPROXIMATELY 40 GENES AT ONCE (including TBX1, COMT, DGCR8, CRKL, plus microRNAs and lncRNAs) -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. The deletion arises by meiotic NON-ALLELIC HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION between the flanking low-copy repeats (LCR22A-H), the same architecture that makes 22q11.2 the MOST COMMON recurrent microdeletion in humans (~1/2,000-1/4,000 live births). This opens a SIXTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- the sub-chromosomal MULTI-GENE COPY-NUMBER-VARIANT (contiguous-gene microdeletion) -- distinct from every class the kit already holds: (1) WHOLE-CHROMOSOME ANEUPLOIDY (Down = a whole extra chromosome 21, a GAIN of one entire chromosome) -- 22q11.2DS is the structural CONVERSE and a different scale: a segmental LOSS of part of one chromosome, not a whole-chromosome gain; (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman 15q11-q13, Beckwith-Wiedemann 11p15.5) -- 22q11.2DS is NOT parent-of-origin-dependent (de novo on either parental chromosome, autosomal-dominant when inherited); (3) REPEAT-DEREPRESSION (FSHD's D4Z4-DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion). The reasons it is unreadable by a single-promoter engine are decisive. (a) ~40 GENES ARE DELETED SIMULTANEOUSLY, so there is NO SINGLE causal gene -- and therefore no single nuclear RefSeq promoter from which to emerge a gamma switch; the kit's data path resolves ONE promoter per locus, and a 40-gene contiguous deletion has no single readable promoter at all. (b) The phenotype is a CONTIGUOUS-GENE syndrome of extreme VARIABLE EXPRESSIVITY and INCOMPLETE PENETRANCE (congenital heart / conotruncal defects, thymic + parathyroid hypoplasia with immunodeficiency + hypocalcaemia, palatal anomalies, craniofacial features, neuropsychiatric risk) shaped by the COMBINED haploinsufficiency of many genes plus genetic modifiers ELSEWHERE in the genome -- a polygenic-within-the-deletion, continuous, multi-system quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (c) TBX1 HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY is the PRINCIPAL DOSAGE-SENSITIVE DRIVER of the major (cardiac / thymic / craniofacial) features -- and rare ISOLATED TBX1 point mutations can PHENOCOPY part of the syndrome -- but the FULL 22q11.2DS is NOT reducible to TBX1 alone (COMT, DGCR8/miRNA biogenesis, CRKL and others contribute), so even reading the TBX1 promoter would NOT emerge 'the disease': the disease is the multi-gene deletion, not one switch. Held per the author's rule -- no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold. Like the other holds, suspended NOT for lack of intervention but purely on engine-readability: management is multidisciplinary and supportive (cardiac surgery, calcium/PTH and immune surveillance with thymus transplantation for complete athymia, palatal and developmental support) -- but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. A multi-gene-CNV / dosage / modifier model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (McDonald-McGinn 2015 Nat Rev Dis Primers 1:15071, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome; Lindsay 2001 Nature 410:97 + Merscher 2001 Cell 104:619, Tbx1 haploinsufficiency drives the DiGeorge phenotype.)
digeorge_22q11_2_deletion_syndrome.emergent_axis: (not applicable -- a ~2.5-3 Mb contiguous-gene microdeletion of 22q11.2 removing ~40 genes (incl. TBX1) at once via NAHR between LCR22 repeats; a sub-chromosomal multi-gene copy-number variant, not a single-gene nuclear promoter switch)

factor_v_leiden.disease: Factor V Leiden thrombophilia (F5 R506Q -- activated protein C resistance; THPH2)
factor_v_leiden.summary: The commonest heritable thrombophilia: a recurrent F5 gain-of-function (R506Q / Arg506Gln, 'factor V Leiden') abolishes the first activated-protein-C (APC) cleavage site on activated factor V, so the procoagulant accelerator cofactor resists inactivation -> the coagulation drive cannot be braked by the protein C/APC pathway -> venous-thrombosis propensity UP.

causal_genes.note: R506Q (Arg506Gln, factor V Leiden) removes the first of the three APC cleavage sites (Arg506/Arg306/Arg679) on activated factor V (factor Va), rendering the procoagulant cofactor APC-RESISTANT -- factor Va stays active far longer, so the procoagulant accelerator cannot be down-regulated by the protein C / APC brake (a functional gain on the procoagulant axis; the accelerator that resists its own brake)
causal_genes.src: Bertina 1994 Nature 369:64 (factor V Leiden / APC resistance); Dahlback 1993 PNAS 90:1004

context_genes.note: prothrombin; the prothrombin G20210A 3'-UTR variant is a DISTINCT gain-of-function thrombophilia on the SAME coagulation axis (mRNA stabilised -> more prothrombin), and F2 is the node of downstream anticoagulation (thrombin inhibition)

protein C; its activated form (APC) is the protease whose factor-Va cleavage the Leiden mutation defeats -- PROC LOF (THPH3) is the BRAKE-loss counterpart on the same axis (the kit reads factor V Leiden as accelerator-GOF, protein C/S loss as brake-LOF -- two routes to the same axis UP)
protein S; the non-enzymatic cofactor accelerating APC cleavage of factor Va -- PROS1 LOF (THPH4) is a second brake-loss counterpart on the same axis
antithrombin; the serpin brake on thrombin/FXa -- SERPINC1 LOF (THPH1; already in the kit as hereditary antithrombin deficiency) is the serpin brake-loss read on the same coagulation axis

therapeutic_axes.push: lower DOWNSTREAM thrombin (and factor Xa) generation by general anticoagulation, pushing the over-driven coagulation axis back toward normal -> reduced venous-thrombosis propensity. Acts DOWNSTREAM of the APC-resistant factor Va and does NOT restore APC sensitivity at F5 (it bypasses the switch defect rather than repairing it); net axis effect RESTRAIN
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: general anticoagulant (vitamin-K antagonist warfarin; direct oral factor Xa inhibitor [rivaroxaban / apixaban] or direct thrombin inhibitor [dabigatran])
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] off-causal-gene DOWNSTREAM anticoagulant; the link from thrombin/FXa inhibition to the corrected coagulation axis is haemostasis pharmacology the gamma read does not capture. Approved for venous-thromboembolism treatment / prophylaxis (the manifestation) -- NOT an F5-targeted agent; whether, when and how intensely to anticoagulate any individual is a clinical risk-stratification decision, asserted nowhere here

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of restored APC sensitivity not derived from sequence; this is the forced switch-level direction, but NO approved agent restores factor Va APC sensitivity -- investigational only
therapeutic_axes.src: APC-resistance mechanism (Bertina 1994); recombinant activated protein C [drotrecogin alfa] was withdrawn 2011 -- no approved factor-V-Leiden-specific corrective
