bardet_biedl_syndrome.summary: A multi-system primary ciliopathy: loss-of-function of BBS1 (the commonest BBS gene, archetype allele M390R) destabilises the BBSome ciliary-trafficking complex, so leptin-receptor / melanocortin signalling at the hypothalamic primary cilium fails -> the satiety drive is lost (hyperphagia, severe early-onset obesity), alongside rod-cone retinal degeneration, post-axial polydactyly and renal anomalies. Read on the hypothalamic melanocortin satiety axis: axis DOWN.
bardet_biedl_syndrome.emergent_axis: hypothalamic melanocortin satiety signalling (energy-balance / adiposity set-point)

causal_genes.note: M390R (the single commonest BBS allele, ~ a quarter of all BBS) destabilises the BBSome core; loss of BBSome-dependent ciliary trafficking of the leptin receptor / melanocortin machinery removes the DRIVE on the hypothalamic satiety axis (an accelerator whose loss under-drives the axis) -> hyperphagic obesity (plus the syndromic retinal / renal / skeletal features of the wider ciliopathy)
causal_genes.src: Mykytyn 2002 Nat Genet 31:435 (BBS1 / M390R); Seo 2009 PNAS 106:1488 (BBSome leptin-receptor trafficking)

context_genes.note: chaperonin-like BBS subunit; the SECOND commonest BBS gene (the C91LfsX5 allele) -- locus-heterogeneity context, not folded into the single BBS1 switch
core BBSome subunit; a further common BBS locus -- locus-heterogeneity context
melanocortin-4 receptor; the DOWNSTREAM hypothalamic satiety node and the setmelanotide target -- agonising it bypasses the upstream BBSome-dependent leptin-receptor trafficking defect

leptin receptor; the receptor whose ciliary trafficking the BBSome supports, and the precedent disease (leptin-receptor deficiency) where the SAME downstream MC4R-agonist bypass [setmelanotide] is the approved lead

therapeutic_axes.push: agonise MC4R, the satiety node DOWNSTREAM of the BBSome-dependent leptin-receptor trafficking defect -> restore the satiety signal the broken ciliary trafficking failed to deliver -> raise the under-driven satiety axis toward normal (axis UP). A DOWNSTREAM receptor bypass: it does NOT repair the BBSome / BBS1
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of hyperphagia / adiposity normalisation not derived from sequence; downstream bypass of the ciliary-trafficking defect. Approved (FDA 2022) for BBS-associated obesity / hyperphagia ONLY -- the retinal degeneration and renal disease of the ciliopathy have NO approved therapy and are not addressed by this lever
therapeutic_axes.src: Haqq 2022 Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 10:859 (setmelanotide in BBS); setmelanotide (Imcivree) FDA 2022 / EMA for BBS obesity

therapeutic_axes.push: restore BBS1 / BBSome assembly and ciliary trafficking itself -> re-enable leptin-receptor / melanocortin trafficking at the cilium -> raise the satiety axis (axis UP); the switch-level corrective, repairing the deficient ciliary machinery rather than bypassing it (and, unlike the downstream bypass, the only arm that could also address the retinal / renal features)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] restored BBSome trafficking not derived from sequence; investigational, no approved BBS1 gene therapy
therapeutic_axes.src: BBSome ciliary-trafficking restoration principle; no approved BBS1 gene therapy

falsifiers.claim: BBS1 LOF moves the hypothalamic satiety axis DOWN (loss of BBSome-dependent leptin-melanocortin drive)
falsifiers.falsifier: a BBS1 LOF allele that INCREASES satiety / reduces adiposity, or a BBSome-deficient hypothalamus in which leptin-melanocortin signalling is enhanced rather than lost, refutes the under-driven (axis DOWN) direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: food-intake / body-weight and hypothalamic melanocortin-pathway readouts in a Bbs1-M390R model; adiposity by genotype in BBS cohorts

falsifiers.claim: agonising MC4R (setmelanotide) is the CORRECTIVE direction (raises the under-driven satiety axis) and acts downstream of the BBSome defect
falsifiers.falsifier: if MC4R agonism reduced rather than restored satiety signalling the 'potentiate downstream' lever sign is wrong; if setmelanotide were shown to repair BBSome trafficking the 'downstream bypass / does-not-repair-the-switch' classification is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: hyperphagia / weight response to setmelanotide in BBS; BBSome-trafficking assays before/after exposure

fragile_x_syndrome.disease: Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 CGG-repeat full-mutation promoter hypermethylation silencing; FRAXA)
fragile_x_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a REPEAT-EXPANSION-DRIVEN PROMOTER METHYLATION SILENCING, not a sequence-level promoter switch the kit can read. In the unaffected population the FMR1 5'-UTR carries ~5-44 CGG repeats; a premutation (~55-200) expands, on MATERNAL transmission, to a FULL MUTATION (>200, often 500-1000+ CGG) -- and the full-mutation expansion triggers CpG-island HYPERMETHYLATION of the FMR1 promoter, packaging it into heterochromatin and TRANSCRIPTIONALLY SILENCING FMR1, so FMRP (the synaptic translational repressor) is lost -> intellectual disability, autism, macro-orchidism, the fragile X phenotype. The defining feature for this kit is that the repeats do NOT alter the FMRP CODING sequence and do NOT change the promoter SEQUENCE the engine reads: the lesion is the (a) repeat COPY NUMBER and (b) the resulting CpG METHYLATION STATE -- both INVISIBLE to a nearest-neighbour stacking gamma read of the reference promoter. The FMR1 promoter is in fact perfectly readable as DNA (cached gamma 1.4563, chrX; it carries the HIGHEST CpG density in the kit's whole panel at 0.0508 -- i.e. it IS a strong CpG island, exactly the substrate that gets methylation-silenced in the full mutation), but the engine reads the UNMETHYLATED REFERENCE state and has no channel for methylation or repeat-length, so it cannot read the silencing lesion. This opens a SEVENTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- repeat-EXPANSION-driven promoter CpG-METHYLATION SILENCING -- genuinely distinct from the six already held: (1) whole-chromosome ANEUPLOIDY (Down); (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman / Beckwith-Wiedemann); (3) repeat-CONTRACTION-driven chromatin DEREPRESSION (FSHD / DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion); (6) the contiguous-gene MICRODELETION (22q11.2). It is the precise MIRROR of the FSHD hold: FSHD is a repeat CONTRACTION that DE-REPRESSES (activates) a silenced gene (DUX4), whereas fragile X is a repeat EXPANSION that SILENCES (represses) an active gene (FMR1) -- the same repeat/epigenetic axis, opposite direction. It is also the sharp same-gene-FAMILY contrast to Huntington (already RESOLVED): both are trinucleotide-repeat-expansion diseases, but HTT's CAG expansion is in the CODING region and produces a TOXIC protein the engine reads at the locus-switch level (resolved), whereas FMR1's CGG expansion is in the 5'-UTR / PROMOTER and acts by METHYLATION SILENCING the engine cannot read (suspended) -- coding-toxic-gain vs promoter-epigenetic-silencing on the same class of lesion. Like the mtDNA and microdeletion holds, fragile X is suspended PURELY on engine-readability, NOT for lack of therapy: there is no approved disease-modifying therapy (FMR1-reactivation / promoter-demethylation strategies -- e.g. CRISPR-dCas9 demethylation, 5-azacytidine -- have not restored meaningful FMRP, and the mGluR5 / GABA-B trials [mavoglurant, arbaclofen] addressed downstream signalling, not the silencing), so the hold keys on whether the engine can READ the lesion, not on whether one can treat it. Prevalence ~1:4,000 males, ~1:8,000 females -- the commonest inherited cause of intellectual disability. Disclosed, not dropped. (Verkerk 1991 Cell 65:905 [FMR1 cloning / CGG repeat]; Pieretti 1991 Cell 66:817 [methylation silencing]; Oberle 1991 Science 252:1097 [unstable DNA / methylation]).
fragile_x_syndrome.emergent_axis: FMR1 / FMRP-dependent synaptic translational regulation (not readable from the reference promoter)

atypical_hemolytic_uremic_syndrome.disease: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (CFH-related; complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy; aHUS)
atypical_hemolytic_uremic_syndrome.summary: Complement factor H (CFH) is the principal FLUID-PHASE and host-surface BRAKE on the ALTERNATIVE complement pathway: it accelerates decay of the C3bBb convertase and is the cofactor for factor-I (CFI) cleavage of C3b. Loss-of-function (most pathogenic aHUS variants cluster in the C-terminal recognition domains SCR19-20, impairing regulation on endothelial surfaces) releases the convertase -> uncontrolled alternative-pathway amplification on microvascular endothelium -> C5b-9 / membrane-attack-complex injury -> thrombotic microangiopathy (microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury). Complement-activation axis UP.
atypical_hemolytic_uremic_syndrome.emergent_axis: alternative-complement-pathway activation on endothelial surfaces (C3 convertase amplification)

causal_genes.note: Factor H is the master negative regulator (BRAKE) of the alternative complement pathway: it accelerates dissociation of the C3bBb convertase (decay-accelerating activity) and is the obligate cofactor for CFI-mediated proteolysis of C3b. Pathogenic aHUS variants are predominantly in the C-terminal short-consensus-repeats SCR19-20 that mediate recognition of host glycan / surface-bound C3b, so the brake fails specifically on self endothelial surfaces -> the convertase amplifies unchecked (loss-of-regulation = a functional loss on the complement-restraint axis).
causal_genes.src: Warwicker 1998 Kidney Int 53:836 (CFH in HUS); Caprioli 2006 Blood 108:1267 (CFH/MCP/CFI genotype-phenotype); Noris & Remuzzi 2009 NEJM 361:1676

context_genes.note: terminal-complement component; the node where the kit's LEAD agent acts. Anti-C5 antibodies (eculizumab/ravulizumab) block C5 cleavage -> no C5a / C5b-9 / MAC, restraining the over-driven axis DOWNSTREAM of the CFH defect (an INDIRECT lever: C5 is not the causal gene).

central complement component / convertase substrate; gain-of-function C3 variants are a DISTINCT aHUS cause on the SAME axis UP (a stabilised convertase), the accelerator-GOF counterpart to the CFH brake-LOF read -- two routes to the same complement-up axis.
complement factor B; the catalytic subunit of the alternative-pathway C3 convertase. GOF CFB variants stabilise the convertase -> another axis-UP route in aHUS.

complement factor I; the protease that CFH cofactors to cleave C3b. CFI LOF is a second BRAKE-loss aHUS gene on the same axis (the kit reads CFH loss as the headline brake-LOF; CFI loss is the protease-side counterpart).
context_genes.src: Kavanagh 2005 J Am Soc Nephrol 16:2150 (CFI mutations in aHUS)

therapeutic_axes.push: block TERMINAL complement at C5 (no C5 cleavage -> no C5a chemoattractant and no C5b-9 membrane-attack complex), pushing the over-activated complement axis back DOWN toward normal -> the endothelial thrombotic microangiopathy is halted. Acts DOWNSTREAM at C5 and does NOT restore factor-H regulation of the convertase (it bypasses the causal switch defect rather than repairing it); net axis effect RESTRAIN.
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] off-causal-gene DOWNSTREAM terminal-complement blockade; the link from C5 inhibition to the corrected complement axis is complement pharmacology the gamma read does not capture. Approved for aHUS (the manifestation) -- NOT a CFH-targeted agent; degree/duration of benefit, the (boxed) meningococcal-infection risk and its vaccination/prophylaxis management, relapse on withdrawal, and whether/when to treat any individual are clinical decisions asserted nowhere here.
therapeutic_axes.src: Legendre 2013 NEJM 368:2169 (eculizumab in aHUS); Rondeau 2020 Kidney Int 97:1287 (ravulizumab)

therapeutic_axes.push: restore factor-H regulation of the alternative-pathway C3 convertase AT THE CAUSAL SWITCH -- re-impose the brake that the SCR19-20 lesion disables -> convertase amplification held down toward normal; net axis effect RESTRAIN (gene/function-level correction of the causal gene, the DIRECTION the switch forces).
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: factor-H regulatory restoration (CFH protein repletion / gene restoration / mini-FH constructs; investigational, no approved agent)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of restored regulation not derived from sequence; this is the forced switch-level direction, but NO approved factor-H-restoring agent exists -- investigational only (recombinant/mini-FH and CFH gene therapy are preclinical/early).
therapeutic_axes.src: Ferreira 2010 J Immunol 185:5328 (factor H regulation); Hebecker 2013 (mini-FH); plasma exchange/infusion is supportive, not an FH-restoring corrective

falsifiers.claim: CFH loss-of-regulation moves the alternative-complement axis UP (the convertase amplifies unchecked on endothelial surfaces)
falsifiers.falsifier: a CFH SCR19-20 loss-of-function variant that REDUCES alternative-pathway activation / endothelial C5b-9 deposition, or lowers TMA incidence, refutes the axis-UP direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: ex-vivo modified-Ham test / endothelial C5b-9 deposition assay and serum sC5b-9 + C3 consumption, stratified by CFH genotype; aHUS incidence by genotype

falsifiers.claim: terminal-complement (anti-C5) blockade is the CORRECTIVE direction (restrains the over-driven axis) but does NOT restore factor-H regulation
falsifiers.falsifier: if C5 inhibition raised rather than reduced TMA the 'restrain the axis' lever sign is wrong; if an anti-C5 agent were shown to restore factor-H convertase regulation the 'downstream / does-not-repair-the-switch' classification is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: haematologic (platelet/LDH/haemoglobin) and renal TMA response on vs off eculizumab/ravulizumab; sC5b-9 and CFH-dependent convertase-regulation assays before/after

mucopolysaccharidosis_type_i.disease: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I (alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency; Hurler / Hurler-Scheie / Scheie syndrome; MPS I)
mucopolysaccharidosis_type_i.summary: IDUA encodes the lysosomal exoglycosidase alpha-L-iduronidase, which removes terminal alpha-L-iduronic-acid residues during the stepwise degradation of the glycosaminoglycans DERMATAN SULFATE and HEPARAN SULFATE. Loss-of-function halts that catabolic step -> progressive lysosomal GAG accumulation across many tissues: dysostosis multiplex, corneal clouding, hepatosplenomegaly, cardiac valve disease, airway disease, and -- in severe Hurler -- progressive neurocognitive decline. Lysosomal GAG-catabolism axis DOWN.

causal_genes.note: alpha-L-iduronidase hydrolyses terminal alpha-L-iduronic acid on dermatan/heparan sulfate; LOF blocks GAG degradation -> lysosomal storage. Severe null alleles (e.g. p.Trp402Ter, p.Gln70Ter -- common in northern-European Hurler) abolish activity (Hurler); attenuated alleles retain residual activity (Hurler-Scheie / Scheie). The classic catabolic-enzyme deficiency-with-substrate-accumulation shape.
causal_genes.src: Scott 1991 PNAS 88:9695 (IDUA cloning); Neufeld & Muenzer 2001 (MMBID, MPS overview)

context_genes.note: iduronate-2-sulfatase (MPS II / Hunter, X-linked); the next-step SULFATASE on the same dermatan/heparan-sulfate pathway -- the enzyme-CLASS contrast (glycosidase vs sulfatase), treated by its own ERT idursulfase. Same GAG axis, adjacent enzyme.

beta-glucuronidase (MPS VII / Sly); another GAG-degrading lysosomal enzyme on the same storage axis, with its own approved ERT vestronidase alfa -- further confirming the lysosomal-catabolism / enzyme-replacement class.

therapeutic_axes.push: supply functional alpha-L-iduronidase to RESTORE the deficient lysosomal GAG-degradation step (raise the catabolic throughput back toward normal) -> reduced somatic dermatan/heparan-sulfate storage; net axis effect UP toward function (DIRECT, on the causal enzyme).
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: enzyme replacement therapy (laronidase, recombinant human alpha-L-iduronidase)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] substrate-clearance fraction / dose / infusion regimen not asserted. Approved (laronidase / Aldurazyme) for the non-CNS manifestations of MPS I. IMPORTANT honest limit: the recombinant enzyme does NOT cross the blood-brain barrier, so the CNS / neurocognitive disease of severe Hurler is NOT addressed by systemic ERT -- a documented gap, magnitude/CNS-reach [O].
therapeutic_axes.src: Wraith 2004 J Pediatr 144:581 (laronidase phase 3); Aldurazyme FDA 2003

therapeutic_axes.push: restore endogenous alpha-L-iduronidase by haematopoietic reconstitution: enzyme-secreting donor-derived cells cross-correct host tissues, and (unlike systemic ERT) engrafted donor microglia provide some CNS enzyme when given early in severe Hurler -> durable somatic and partial CNS GAG clearance; net axis effect UP.
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT; standard of care for early severe Hurler) + ex-vivo autologous IDUA gene-corrected HSC therapy (investigational)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] engraftment, enzyme level and the degree/timing of CNS protection are clinical outcomes not derived from sequence; HSCT is established standard for early severe MPS I but is a procedure with its own risks, not a drug approval, and its CNS benefit is partial and age-dependent -- [O].
therapeutic_axes.src: Aldenhoven 2015 Blood 125:2164 (HSCT outcomes in Hurler)

falsifiers.claim: IDUA loss-of-function moves the lysosomal GAG-catabolism axis DOWN (dermatan/heparan-sulfate accumulate)
falsifiers.falsifier: an IDUA LOF allele that LOWERS tissue / urinary GAG (i.e. raises catabolic throughput) refutes the axis-DOWN direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: leukocyte/fibroblast alpha-L-iduronidase activity and urinary dermatan/heparan-sulfate GAG quantification, stratified by IDUA genotype

falsifiers.claim: enzyme replacement is the CORRECTIVE direction (raises the deficient catabolic throughput)
falsifiers.falsifier: if laronidase raised rather than reduced tissue/urinary GAG storage the 'replace' lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: urinary GAG and liver/spleen-volume response to laronidase infusion

mccune_albright_syndrome.disease: McCune-Albright syndrome (post-zygotic mosaic GNAS activating mutation; polyostotic fibrous dysplasia + cafe-au-lait macules + hyperfunctioning endocrinopathy; MAS)
mccune_albright_syndrome.suspended_reason: The cause is a POST-ZYGOTIC SOMATIC-MOSAIC ACTIVATING mutation of GNAS (the gene for the stimulatory G-protein alpha-subunit, Gs-alpha) -- most commonly p.Arg201His or p.Arg201Cys -- that arises AFTER fertilisation in a subset of cells, so the disease-causing lesion is ABSENT from the inherited / germline reference sequence and is present only as a MOSAIC in affected tissues (the anatomical distribution of mutant cells determines which bones and endocrine organs are involved). The Arg201 substitution disables the intrinsic GTPase of Gs-alpha, locking it GTP-bound -> constitutive adenylate-cyclase / cAMP / PKA signalling -> autonomous endocrine hyperfunction (gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty, hyperthyroidism, growth-hormone excess, FGF23-mediated renal phosphate wasting) plus fibrous dysplasia of bone and cafe-au-lait macules. Why this kit MUST hold it: the GNAS PROMOTER is in fact perfectly readable as reference DNA (cached gamma 1.4256, chr20), but (a) the lesion is a CODING activating point mutation, not a promoter-switch change, AND (b) -- the decisive point -- it is a SOMATIC MOSAIC mutation that is NOT PRESENT in the inherited sequence the engine reads at all. A constitutional (germline) Arg201 activating mutation is thought to be embryonic-lethal, surviving only as mosaicism; by definition such a lesion cannot be recovered from the reference promoter. This opens an EIGHTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- post-zygotic SOMATIC MOSAICISM -- genuinely distinct from the seven already held: (1) whole-chromosome ANEUPLOIDY (Down); (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman / Beckwith-Wiedemann); (3) repeat-CONTRACTION-driven chromatin DEREPRESSION (FSHD / DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion); (6) the contiguous-gene MICRODELETION (22q11.2); (7) repeat-EXPANSION-driven promoter CpG-METHYLATION silencing (Fragile X). It is also a pointed contrast ON THE SAME GNAS LOCUS to the GERMLINE GNAS disorders -- pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1a / Albright hereditary osteodystrophy (INACTIVATING, parent-of-origin-IMPRINTED, germline-readable) -- proving the hold keys on the SOMATIC-MOSAIC nature of the lesion, not on the gene (the germline GNAS disorders would be a separate, imprinting-class question; the activating somatic disease is the mosaicism-class hold). Suspended PURELY on engine-readability (a somatic lesion not in the inherited sequence), NOT for lack of therapy -- management is organ-directed (aromatase inhibitors / tamoxifen for precocious puberty; bisphosphonates / anti-RANKL denosumab for fibrous dysplasia; burosumab where FGF23-driven hypophosphataemia dominates), with a Gs-alpha / cAMP-directed disease-modifying therapy still investigational. Disclosed, not dropped. (Weinstein 1991 NEJM 325:1688 [GNAS R201 mosaic activating mutation]; Schwindinger 1992 PNAS 89:5152; Boyce & Collins 2020 [MAS / fibrous dysplasia review]).
mccune_albright_syndrome.emergent_axis: Gs-alpha / cAMP-PKA signalling (somatic-mosaic activating lesion, not present in the inherited reference)

metachromatic_leukodystrophy.summary: ARSA encodes the lysosomal enzyme arylsulfatase A (cerebroside-3-sulfatase), which removes the 3-O-sulfate from 3-O-sulfogalactosylceramide (SULFATIDE) -- the rate-limiting first step of sulfatide catabolism. Loss-of-function halts that step -> progressive lysosomal SULFATIDE accumulation in the myelin-forming oligodendrocytes (CNS) and Schwann cells (PNS) -> demyelination of the central AND peripheral nervous system -> progressive motor, cognitive and behavioural regression, spasticity and seizures (late-infantile / juvenile / adult forms graded by residual activity). Lysosomal sulfatide-catabolism axis DOWN; the kit's FIRST leukodystrophy and FIRST sulfatide substrate.
metachromatic_leukodystrophy.emergent_axis: lysosomal sulfatide (3-O-sulfogalactosylceramide) catabolic throughput sustaining CNS/PNS myelin

causal_genes.note: arylsulfatase A hydrolyses the 3-O-sulfate of sulfatide (with the sphingolipid-activator protein saposin B as cofactor); LOF blocks sulfatide degradation -> lysosomal storage in myelinating cells -> demyelination. Severe null / 0-activity alleles (e.g. the c.459+1G>A splice null; p.Pro426Leu) give late-infantile MLD; alleles retaining residual activity (e.g. p.Arg370Trp, the 'I' allele) give juvenile/adult forms -- the classic catabolic-enzyme deficiency-with-substrate-accumulation shape, now on a sulfatide/myelin substrate. (A clinically identical MLD also arises from LOF of the saposin-B activator PSAP; that is the activator-deficiency contrast, not the enzyme itself.)
causal_genes.src: Polten 1991 NEJM 324:18 (ARSA molecular basis / genotype-phenotype); Gieselmann 2010 (MLD review)

context_genes.note: prosaposin -> saposin B, the sphingolipid-activator protein that presents sulfatide to ARSA; rare PSAP/saposin-B LOF causes an ARSA-activity-normal MLD phenocopy -- the activator-vs-enzyme contrast on the SAME catabolic step.

arylsulfatase B (N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase; MPS VI / Maroteaux-Lamy), a different lysosomal sulfatase acting on a GAG substrate with its own approved ERT galsulfase -- the sulfatase-family contrast (sulfatide vs dermatan-sulfate): same enzyme superfamily, different substrate axis.

therapeutic_axes.push: restore endogenous arylsulfatase A by haematopoietic reconstitution with ARSA-overexpressing autologous cells: ex-vivo lentiviral gene-corrected CD34+ HSCs engraft, and their progeny -- including donor-derived microglia that migrate across the blood-brain barrier -- secrete supraphysiological ARSA that cross-corrects oligodendrocytes / Schwann cells -> the deficient sulfatide-degradation step is RESTORED -> demyelination halted/slowed; net axis effect UP toward function (DIRECT, on the causal enzyme).
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: ex-vivo autologous ARSA-lentiviral haematopoietic stem-cell gene therapy (atidarsagene autotemcel; Lenmeldy / Libmeldy)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] ARSA expression level / sulfatide-clearance fraction / extent of myelin preservation not derived from sequence. Approved (atidarsagene autotemcel; FDA 2024 / EMA 2020) but ONLY for PRE-symptomatic late-infantile, pre-symptomatic early-juvenile or early-symptomatic early-juvenile MLD -- the corrective window CLOSES once demyelination is established, so TIMING (not magnitude) is the decisive limit; degree of benefit [O].
therapeutic_axes.src: Fumagalli 2022 Lancet 399:372 (atidarsagene autotemcel phase 1/2); Lenmeldy FDA approval 2024-03-18; Libmeldy EMA 2020

therapeutic_axes.push: supply functional arylsulfatase A directly into the CNS (intrathecal recombinant enzyme) to restore the deficient lysosomal sulfatide-degradation step -> reduced sulfatide storage; net axis effect UP. (Systemic IV ERT does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so the CNS-predominant disease requires intrathecal delivery.)
therapeutic_axes.agent_class: intrathecal enzyme replacement therapy (recombinant human arylsulfatase A)
therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] CNS enzyme distribution / clinical benefit not derived from sequence; intrathecal ARSA remains investigational (the systemic recombinant enzyme does not cross the BBB) -- [O].
therapeutic_axes.src: Dali 2020 Ann Clin Transl Neurol 7:518 (intrathecal ARSA trial)

falsifiers.claim: ARSA loss-of-function moves the lysosomal sulfatide-catabolism axis DOWN (sulfatide accumulates in myelinating cells)
falsifiers.falsifier: an ARSA LOF allele that LOWERS tissue / urinary sulfatide (i.e. raises catabolic throughput) refutes the axis-DOWN direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: leukocyte/fibroblast arylsulfatase A activity and urinary sulfatide quantification, stratified by ARSA genotype (controlling for the common pseudodeficiency allele)

falsifiers.claim: restoring ARSA (replace) is the CORRECTIVE direction (raises the deficient catabolic throughput)
falsifiers.falsifier: if ARSA gene-therapy engraftment that raised leukocyte ARSA activity FAILED to reduce CSF / urinary sulfatide, or accelerated demyelination, the 'replace' lever sign would be wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: CSF/urinary sulfatide and MRI demyelination load vs leukocyte ARSA activity after gene therapy, stratified by pre- vs post-symptomatic treatment timing

myotonic_dystrophy_type_1.disease: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DMPK CTG-repeat expansion; dystrophia myotonica; Steinert disease; DM1)
myotonic_dystrophy_type_1.suspended_reason: The cause is a REPEAT-EXPANSION-DRIVEN TOXIC-RNA GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (a spliceopathy), not a sequence-level promoter switch the kit can read. In the unaffected population the DMPK 3'-UTR carries ~5-37 CTG repeats; in DM1 this expands to ~50 to >3,500 CTG, with somatic and intergenerational instability (anticipation). The expanded allele is still TRANSCRIBED -- and crucially the lesion is NON-CODING (3'-untranslated region) and produces NO toxic protein -- but the mutant transcript carries a long CUG-repeat hairpin that accumulates in NUCLEAR FOCI and SEQUESTERS the muscleblind-like (MBNL1 / MBNL2) family of alternative-splicing regulators (with reciprocal stabilisation of CELF1). The resulting MBNL loss-of-function mis-regulates a developmental panel of alternative-splicing events (e.g. CLCN1 -> myotonia, INSR -> insulin resistance, SCN5A -> conduction disease, BIN1, SERCA1/ATP2A1) across muscle, heart and CNS -- a multisystem 'RNA dominance' disease. The defining feature for this kit is that the lesion does NOT change the DMPK promoter SEQUENCE the engine reads, and acts in TRANS at the RNA level on OTHER genes' transcripts: it is the (a) 3'-UTR repeat COPY NUMBER and (b) the resulting toxic-RNA / MBNL-sequestration state -- both INVISIBLE to a nearest-neighbour stacking gamma read of the reference DMPK promoter. The DMPK promoter is in fact perfectly readable as DNA (cached gamma 1.5132, chr19 19q13.32), but the engine reads the encoding locus's unexpanded REFERENCE state and has no channel for 3'-UTR repeat-length or for a trans-acting RNA-protein-sequestration spliceopathy, so it cannot read this lesion. This opens a NINTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- repeat-EXPANSION-driven TOXIC-RNA gain-of-function / spliceopathy -- genuinely distinct from the eight already held: (1) whole-chromosome ANEUPLOIDY (Down); (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman / Beckwith-Wiedemann); (3) repeat-CONTRACTION-driven chromatin DEREPRESSION (FSHD / DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion); (6) the contiguous-gene MICRODELETION (22q11.2); (7) repeat-EXPANSION-driven promoter CpG-METHYLATION SILENCING (fragile X / FMR1); (8) post-zygotic SOMATIC-MOSAIC activating mutation (McCune-Albright / GNAS). It COMPLETES a trinucleotide-repeat-expansion taxonomy by mechanism-of-action: HUNTINGTON (HTT CAG, in the CODING region) makes a TOXIC PROTEIN read at the locus-switch level (RESOLVED); FRAGILE X (FMR1 CGG, in the 5'-UTR / PROMOTER) SILENCES its own gene by methylation (suspended); and now DM1 (DMPK CTG, in the 3'-UTR) makes a TOXIC RNA that acts in TRANS on splicing (suspended) -- coding-protein-toxic vs promoter-epigenetic-silencing vs UTR-RNA-toxic, three distinct fates of one lesion class, the first read by the engine, the latter two not. Like the mtDNA, microdeletion, fragile-X and mosaicism holds, DM1 is suspended PURELY on engine-readability, NOT for lack of therapy: there is NO approved disease-modifying therapy -- the advancing strategies (DMPK-lowering / CUG-targeting antisense oligonucleotides and siRNAs, small molecules that displace MBNL from the CUG hairpin, MBNL-restoring approaches) remain investigational / in clinical trials, and approved care is symptomatic (e.g. mexiletine for myotonia, cardiac pacing for conduction block) -- so the hold keys on whether the engine can READ the lesion, not on whether one can treat it. The commonest adult-onset muscular dystrophy (~1:8,000). Disclosed, not dropped. (Brook 1992 Cell 68:799 [DMPK CTG repeat]; Miller 2000 EMBO J 19:4439 [MBNL sequestration]; Mankodi 2002 Mol Cell 10:35 / Charlet-B 2002 Mol Cell 10:45 [CLCN1 mis-splicing -> myotonia]).
myotonic_dystrophy_type_1.emergent_axis: DMPK-transcript-dependent, MBNL-regulated alternative splicing across muscle / heart / CNS (a trans RNA-toxicity lesion not readable from the reference promoter)

scn4a_skeletal_muscle_channelopathy.disease: Non-dystrophic myotonia and periodic paralysis (SCN4A skeletal-muscle sodium channelopathy: paramyotonia congenita / sodium-channel myotonia / hyperkalaemic and hypokalaemic periodic paralysis)
scn4a_skeletal_muscle_channelopathy.summary: A spectrum of dominant skeletal-muscle channelopathies caused by mutations in SCN4A, which encodes NaV1.4, the pore-forming alpha-subunit of the skeletal-muscle voltage-gated sodium channel (chr17q23.3). NaV1.4 normally opens to drive the muscle-fibre action-potential upstroke and then INACTIVATES. The myotonic forms (paramyotonia congenita; sodium-channel myotonia) are GAIN-of-function alleles that impair fast inactivation, leaving a persistent/late sodium current that makes the membrane HYPEREXCITABLE -- the fibre fires repetitively after voluntary contraction (delayed relaxation = myotonia). In hyperkalaemic periodic paralysis the same gain of persistent inward current, under a rising extracellular K+, depolarises the fibre so far that the normal sodium channels inactivate and the membrane becomes INEXCITABLE (flaccid weakness). The kit reads this as the skeletal-muscle membrane-excitability axis driven UP (channel GOF -> the gate fails to stay in the OFF / inactivated basin -> a runaway persistent current). This is the SKELETAL-MUSCLE analogue of LQT3 (SCN5A GOF, cardiac late sodium current): the same biophysical lesion (persistent late INa from impaired inactivation) in a sister sodium-channel gene and a different excitable tissue, and -- remarkably -- corrected by the SAME drug class. Correction is to RESTRAIN the over-active channel: mexiletine, a class-IB sodium-channel blocker, preferentially blocks the persistent late current and is the FIRST and only disease-specific licensed antimyotonic (NaMuscla, EMA-approved 2018 for non-dystrophic myotonia; pivotal phase-III MYOMEX, Statland 2012 JAMA RCT). A second, INDIRECT approved arm exists for the periodic-paralysis variants: the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor dichlorphenamide (Keveyis, FDA-approved 2015 for primary hyperkalaemic and hypokalaemic periodic paralysis) stabilises excitability through metabolic acidosis / potassium handling rather than by acting on NaV1.4. IMPORTANT HONESTY: the corrective DIRECTION (block the excess sodium current) is forced [F]; the realised benefit MAGNITUDE is [O] and GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT (some SCN4A alleles respond well to mexiletine, others poorly, by the biophysics of the specific inactivation defect -- the LQT3 mexiletine-sensitive/insensitive pattern). The same gene's LOSS-of-function alleles cause a DISTINCT disease (a congenital myasthenic / myopathic phenotype) -- a different (mechanism) read not conflated here. The gamma read is of the SCN4A promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr17, gamma 1.5187); the disease lesions are coding (inactivation-impairing missense / in-frame changes), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
scn4a_skeletal_muscle_channelopathy.emergent_axis: skeletal-muscle membrane excitability -- the persistent / late sodium current through NaV1.4. NaV1.4 normally inactivates after the upstroke; GOF alleles leave a persistent inward current so the fibre is hyperexcitable (myotonia) or, under high K+, depolarised into inexcitability (periodic paralysis). The kit reads the gate over-staying the conducting state -> a runaway late current (axis UP / restrain). The skeletal-muscle contrast to the LOF channels restored by potentiation (CFTR, K_ATP), and the skeletal twin of the cardiac SCN5A late-INa axis (LQT3)

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] benefit MAGNITUDE (stiffness / attack-rate reduction) not sequence-derived; GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- some SCN4A alleles are mexiletine-SENSITIVE, others less so, by the biophysics of the inactivation defect, held [O]; the corrective DIRECTION (reduce the excess sodium current) is forced [F].

neonatal_severe_hyperparathyroidism.disease: Neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism / Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia type 1 (CASR loss-of-function)
neonatal_severe_hyperparathyroidism.summary: A calcium-set-point disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in CASR, which encodes the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), a class-C G-protein-coupled receptor on parathyroid chief cells and renal tubular cells (chr3q21.1). The CaSR senses extracellular ionised calcium and, when calcium rises, SUPPRESSES PTH secretion and reduces renal calcium reabsorption -- it is the BRAKE that holds serum calcium in its narrow band. Heterozygous LOF raises the set-point modestly -> familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia type 1 (FHH1, usually benign: mildly high calcium with inappropriately non-suppressed PTH and low urinary calcium). Biallelic (homozygous / compound-heterozygous) LOF removes the brake almost entirely -> neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism (NSHPT): life-threatening hypercalcaemia, very high PTH, skeletal demineralisation and fractures in the newborn. The kit reads this as the PTH-secretion / serum-calcium axis driven UP (a BRAKE released -> the output over-driven). This is the kit's FIRST calcium-sensing-GPCR axis -- a distinct receptor and physiology from the existing water-balance GPCR axis (the AVPR2 / V2 vasopressin receptor in nephrogenic diabetes insipidus). Correction is to RESTRAIN the over-driven PTH/calcium output by POTENTIATING the residual receptor: cinacalcet, a calcimimetic that allosterically increases CaSR sensitivity to calcium, directly potentiates the brake, lowering PTH and serum calcium. Cinacalcet is APPROVED for related hyperparathyroid conditions (secondary hyperparathyroidism of chronic kidney disease, parathyroid carcinoma, primary hyperparathyroidism) and is used OFF-LABEL but as documented effective first-line therapy in NSHPT and symptomatic FHH, repeatedly allowing serum-calcium normalisation and avoidance / delay of parathyroidectomy. IMPORTANT HONESTY: because cinacalcet works THROUGH the receptor, its effect is GENOTYPE-DEPENDENT -- it requires RESIDUAL CaSR function, so alleles that abolish the receptor (true nulls) may be unresponsive (the corrective DIRECTION is forced [F]; the realised magnitude is [O]). Parathyroidectomy remains the PHYSICAL fallback for unresponsive / homozygous-null NSHPT (a surgical, non-switch option). The CASR coding lesions sit outside the promoter firewall; the gamma read is of the CASR promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3, gamma 1.3299). The OPPOSITE-direction disease of the SAME receptor -- autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia from CaSR GAIN-of-function (over-active brake -> PTH/calcium too LOW) -- is a distinct (mechanism) read not conflated here. Magnitude [O].
neonatal_severe_hyperparathyroidism.emergent_axis: PTH secretion / serum-calcium set-point -- the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is the brake that, on sensing a rise in extracellular calcium, suppresses PTH and renal calcium reabsorption. LOF raises the set-point so PTH and serum calcium are inappropriately over-driven (axis UP). The kit's first calcium-sensing-GPCR axis (brake released -> restrain), distinct from the AVPR2 water-balance GPCR axis

Heterozygous LOF -> FHH1 (benign); biallelic LOF -> neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism. chr3q21.1. NCBI official symbol CASR. NSHPT OMIM 239200; FHH1 145980. biotinidase_deficiency.summary: An autosomal-recessive disorder of vitamin recycling caused by loss-of-function mutations in BTD, which encodes biotinidase (chr3p25.1) -- the enzyme that liberates free biotin from biocytin (and from small biotinylated peptides) during the normal turnover of the biotin-dependent carboxylases, and that releases protein-bound biotin from dietary protein. When biotinidase fails, biotin is not recycled (and is lost in urine as biocytin), the free-biotin pool falls, and the four biotin-dependent carboxylases (pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase) are progressively under-charged -- a late-onset MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY. Untreated, profound deficiency (<10% residual activity) produces seizures, hypotonia, ataxia, developmental delay, a skin rash and alopecia, sensorineural hearing loss and optic atrophy; partial deficiency (10-30%) is milder. The kit reads this as the free-biotin-availability / carboxylase-throughput axis driven DOWN (an enzyme LOF -> pathway throughput falls, the upstream substrate biocytin accumulates). Correction is, beautifully, the simplest possible REPLACE: oral biotin (vitamin B7) supplies the exact free cofactor the broken recycler would have liberated, FLOODING the free-biotin pool and re-charging the carboxylases -- bypassing the recycling defect entirely. This is one of the most treatable inborn errors of metabolism: identified by newborn screening and treated lifelong with inexpensive oral biotin, pre-symptomatic patients have a normal, symptom-free course. IMPORTANT HONESTY: the corrective DIRECTION (replace the missing cofactor) is forced [F]; the realised MAGNITUDE is [O] and TIMING-limited -- biotin almost completely PREVENTS disease when started before symptoms, but established neurological damage (sensorineural hearing loss, optic atrophy) frequently does NOT reverse once present, and the partial-vs-profound dose is [O]. The BTD coding lesions sit outside the promoter firewall; the gamma read is of the BTD promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3, gamma 1.3560). Magnitude [O].
biotinidase_deficiency.emergent_axis: free-biotin availability / biotin-dependent carboxylase throughput -- biotinidase recycles biotin from biocytin during carboxylase turnover and releases dietary protein-bound biotin. LOF lowers the free-biotin pool and under-charges the four carboxylases (axis DOWN, multiple carboxylase deficiency). A cofactor-recycling enzyme LOF whose corrective is to flood the missing cofactor

causal_genes.note: BTD encodes biotinidase, the hydrolase that liberates free biotin from biocytin and small biotinyl-peptides (recycling biotin from carboxylase turnover) and releases protein-bound biotin from food. LOF -> free biotin is lost as urinary biocytin, the carboxylases are under-charged (late-onset multiple carboxylase deficiency). Profound <10% vs partial 10-30% residual activity. chr3p25.1. autosomal recessive. NCBI official symbol BTD. OMIM 253260.
causal_genes.src: Wolf 1983 J Pediatr 103:233 (biotinidase deficiency defined); Cole 1994 J Biol Chem 269:6566 (BTD cloning); Wolf 2010 (GeneReviews, Biotinidase Deficiency)

context_genes.note: HLCS encodes holocarboxylase synthetase, the enzyme that ATTACHES biotin to the apocarboxylases. Its LOF causes the OTHER, neonatal-onset biotin-responsive multiple carboxylase deficiency -- the same downstream carboxylase failure reached by a different step (attachment, not recycling). Framed as context: biotin-responsive but a distinct gene and step.

therapeutic_axes.mechanism_grade: [O] MAGNITUDE / reversibility OPEN -- dramatic, likely complete PREVENTION if started pre-symptomatically (newborn-screened), but established sensorineural hearing loss / optic atrophy often do NOT reverse once present (a TIMING-limited rescue); partial-vs-profound dose [O]. Direction (replace the missing cofactor) forced [F].

primary_carnitine_deficiency.disease: Primary (systemic) carnitine deficiency (carnitine transporter OCTN2 deficiency)
primary_carnitine_deficiency.summary: An autosomal-recessive fatty-acid-oxidation disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in SLC22A5, which encodes OCTN2 (chr5q31.1) -- the high-affinity, sodium-dependent carnitine transporter that actively DRIVES carnitine into heart, skeletal-muscle, kidney and other cells, and reabsorbs filtered carnitine in the renal tubule. Carnitine is required to shuttle long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane for beta-oxidation, the main energy source for heart and muscle during fasting. When OCTN2 fails, carnitine is wasted in the urine, plasma and tissue carnitine fall sharply, and long-chain fatty-acid oxidation collapses -- presenting as hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and hepatic encephalopathy in infants, hypertrophic / dilated cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy in children, and arrhythmia, fatigue or sudden death later. The kit reads this as the intracellular-carnitine-availability / long-chain-fatty-acid-oxidation-flux axis driven DOWN (an active importer / accelerator LOF -> the drive that loads cellular carnitine is lost -> the downstream pathway is under-supplied). Correction is a REPLACE by mass action: high-dose oral levocarnitine (L-carnitine; Carnitor, FDA-approved for primary and secondary carnitine deficiency) floods the system to restore intracellular and tissue carnitine through residual / low-affinity uptake, re-enabling fatty-acid oxidation. This is a once-lethal disease made survivable: started early, levocarnitine REVERSES the cardiomyopathy, myopathy and hypoglycaemic episodes; affected individuals are lifelong dependent on supplementation. IMPORTANT HONESTY: the corrective DIRECTION (replace the missing substrate) is forced [F]; the realised MAGNITUDE is [O] and TIMING-limited (reversal is documented when treatment precedes irreversible organ damage), and the dose is [O] (a clinical / runtime quantity, never sequence-derived). The SLC22A5 coding lesions (and a frequent 5'-UTR uORF-creating variant) sit outside the promoter firewall; the gamma read is of the SLC22A5 promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr5, gamma 1.3724). Magnitude [O].
primary_carnitine_deficiency.emergent_axis: intracellular carnitine availability / long-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation flux -- OCTN2 (SLC22A5) actively imports carnitine into heart/muscle/kidney cells and reabsorbs it in the renal tubule. LOF wastes carnitine in the urine and depletes cellular carnitine, so long-chain fatty-acid import into mitochondria fails (axis DOWN; hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, cardiomyopathy, myopathy). An active-importer LOF whose corrective is to flood the missing substrate

causal_genes.note: SLC22A5 encodes OCTN2, the high-affinity Na+-dependent organic cation / carnitine transporter that actively DRIVES cellular carnitine uptake and renal carnitine reabsorption -- an active import 'drive'. LOF wastes carnitine in urine and depletes tissue carnitine, collapsing long-chain fatty-acid oxidation. chr5q31.1. autosomal recessive. NCBI official symbol SLC22A5. OMIM 212140.

LOF causes a distinct, severe long-chain-FAO disorder. Framed as context: a different step of the same carnitine shuttle.

charcot_marie_tooth_1a.disease: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A; PMP22 17p11.2 tandem duplication -- single-gene dosage excess)
charcot_marie_tooth_1a.suspended_reason: The cause is a single-gene DOSAGE EXCESS produced by a ~1.4-Mb GENOMIC TANDEM DUPLICATION at chromosome 17p11.2-p12 that carries a THIRD complete copy of PMP22 -- not a sequence-level promoter switch the kit can read. In the normal genome PMP22 is present in two copies; the CMT1A duplication adds a third functional copy, so peripheral myelin protein 22 is OVER-expressed by gene DOSAGE, the Schwann cell dysmyelinates, and a progressive length-dependent peripheral neuropathy emerges (CMT1A is the COMMONEST inherited neuropathy, more than half of all Charcot-Marie-Tooth, prevalence about 1 in 2500). The PMP22 promoter SEQUENCE is perfectly readable as reference DNA (gamma 1.3883, chr17) and is NOT mutated; the lesion is a COPY-NUMBER GAIN of the whole locus. The emergence engine reads ONE promoter's switch-threshold (gamma) per locus; it has NO representation of 'how many copies of this promoter exist', so a gene-dosage DUPLICATION is invisible to a single-locus gamma read -- just as a whole-chromosome aneuploidy (Down) or a contiguous-gene microdeletion (DiGeorge) is, but here the change is a SUB-CHROMOSOMAL, single-gene-centric copy-number GAIN. This is the kit's TENTH distinct held mechanism class -- after (1) whole-chromosome aneuploidy, (2) genomic imprinting, (3) repeat-CONTRACTION chromatin derepression, (4) mtDNA point mutation, (5) mtDNA large-scale deletion, (6) contiguous-gene microDELETION, (7) repeat-EXPANSION promoter methylation-silencing, (8) post-zygotic somatic mosaicism, and (9) repeat-EXPANSION toxic-RNA spliceopathy -- being the FIRST copy-number GAIN / gene-DUPLICATION-dosage hold, and the reciprocal MIRROR of HNPP (hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies), which is the SAME 1.4-Mb region DELETED -> PMP22 haploinsufficiency. CMT1A is the canonical 'gene dosage' disease (3 copies -> CMT1A; 1 copy -> HNPP; 2 -> normal), a clean demonstration that COPY-NUMBER, not promoter sequence, is the lesion. Suspended PURELY on engine-readability, NOT for lack of therapeutic interest: there is NO approved disease-modifying or curative drug -- clinical management is multidisciplinary supportive care plus ankle-foot orthoses and corrective surgery (a PHYSICAL / rehabilitative track) -- while the dosage-lowering combination PXT3003 (baclofen / naltrexone / sorbitol, which suppresses PMP22 over-expression) completed a Phase III trial and is not yet approved, and PMP22-targeting antisense oligonucleotides / gene-editing remain investigational. PMP22 gamma 1.3883 chr17 is recorded as reference only; the disease is held, disclosed not dropped.
